Dawnwatcher Shaedlass maintains a presence in the night elven capital of Darnassus, watching over the faction's interests in Kalimdor. From his quiet post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he keeps tabs on covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

npc:dazalar.text: Dazalar. In Dolanaar, Dazalar trains young night elf hunters for the wilds of Teldrassil. He teaches them to aim true and form bonds with the beasts of the great boughs. Dazalar trains young hunters in Dolanaar before they venture beyond Shadowglen. Night elf rangers and sentinels patrol the wilderness, and he teaches newcomers the patience and discipline needed to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem. Dazalar teaches hunters to tame and care for beasts. The Kaldorei seek a pact with forest predators such as nightsabers, owls, and strigid hunters, training them to fight beside their companions with respect rather than force.

npc:deathguard-bartholomew.text: Deathguard Bartholomew. Deathguard Bartholomew is a vigilant Forsaken soldier stationed in the town of Brill. Tasked with maintaining security across Tirisfal Glades, he helps travelers navigate the blighted settlement and assists in enforcing discipline among local defenders. Standing watch in the settlement of Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew represents the stalwart military backbone of the Forsaken. Like his fellow Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, he defends reclaimed territory from lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and any other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. In addition to keeping watch, he provides directions to travelers attempting to navigate the town's facilities and participates in maintaining orderly conduct among the newly risen.

npc:deathguard-burgess.text: Deathguard Burgess. Deathguard Burgess is a Forsaken sentry stationed in the town of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the settlement, he keeps order and directs travelers to vital services across the hamlet. Positioned in the settlement of Brill just north of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess serves as one of the town guards maintaining security against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like other Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, Burgess aids arriving Forsaken by providing directions to local tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services, keeping the vulnerable outpost running smoothly.

npc:deathguard-humbert.text: Deathguard Humbert. Deathguard Humbert is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assigned to monitor the encroaching Alliance presence, he finds himself in an embarrassing predicament after losing his military gear to the dwarves of Dun Garok. While tasked with maintaining Tarren Mill's perimeter against regional threats, Deathguard Humbert suffered a humiliating setback. Sent by High Executor Darthalia to watch Dun Garok from a hidden camp, he left one morning to gather firewood, and dwarven scouts from Dun Garok made off with his prized sword and assorted equipment, leaving the undead soldier desperate to salvage his pride and armament before high command takes notice.

npc:deathguard-linnea.text: Deathguard Linnea. Deathguard Linnea is a Forsaken soldier stationed at a Deathguard waystation in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. She helps secure the roads between Brill and the eastern borders, watching for threats posed by the Scarlet Crusade and lingering Scourge. Adventurers passing along the main thoroughfares often assist her unit with patrol duties. Deathguard Linnea stands sentinel at a small fortified post southeast of Brill. Life—or unlife—on patrol in Tirisfal Glades is treacherous, as the Forsaken must vigilantly defend their fledgling realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and mindless Scourge prowling the wilderness. Stationed alongside her fellow guards, Linnea oversees patrol efforts along the roadway, coordinating reports with local authorities such as Magistrate Sevren in Brill to keep the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

npc:deathguard-samsa.text: Deathguard Samsa. Deathguard Samsa is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining Horde vigilance on a tense frontier, he directs traveling champions to strike at local threats encroaching on the settlement. Standing watch in Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa represents the defensive backbone of the Forsaken in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill serves as the Horde's primary outpost in the region, facing immediate pressure from Alliance outposts like Southshore as well as savage local wildlife. Samsa's duties involve securing the perimeter and directing capable adventurers to eliminate threats before they endanger the encampment.

npc:deathguard-simmer.text: Deathguard Simmer. Deathguard Simmer is a Forsaken soldier stationed just outside Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. He sizes up newly risen Forsaken and sends them to raid the human pumpkin farm to the west, patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade, for reagents the apothecaries of Brill need. Posted just outside Deathknell, Deathguard Simmer represents the Forsaken military line holding the border between the safe haven of Deathknell and the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. The region crawls with living humans—most notably the fanatical Scarlet Crusade—who view all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Simmer tests fledgling Forsaken by sending them west to the Solliden Farmstead, where the Scarlet Crusade patrols from its nearby tower, to steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

npc:deathstalker-faerleia.text: Deathstalker Faerleia. Deathstalker Faerleia is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence agency stationed deep within enemy territory inside Pyrewood Village. Operating out of the settlement's town hall, she orchestrates covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the village leaders Arugal uses as puppets. As an agent of the Deathstalkers—the covert intelligence and assassin branch of the Undercity—Faerleia is tasked with infiltrating Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. The isolated human enclave harbors dark secrets, including a curse that transforms its populace under the night sky. Stationed within the upper levels of the town hall, Faerleia coordinates operations to disrupt the settlement from the inside, calling on Horde operatives to eliminate the influential members of the Pyrewood Council.

npc:deathstalker-lesh.text: Deathstalker Lesh. Deathstalker Lesh is a Forsaken rogue serving as a forward scout at Southpoint Tower in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Operating directly under High Executor Darthalia, she keeps watch over the human farms in the Hillsbrad Fields to gauge when the Forsaken should strike. Perched at Southpoint Tower on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the human farmers and town militia working the nearby Hillsbrad Fields. As an operative of the Deathstalkers—the Forsaken's secretive intelligence and assassination network—Lesh tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends word to Darthalia with a coded message, 'The raven's cry from the west doth beckon', signaling that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

npc:deathstalker-rane-yorick.text: Rane Yorick. Deathstalker Rane Yorick is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence guild stationed deep in Silverpine Forest. Together with her brother Quinn, she was sent to scout the farms of northern Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. The Deathstalkers serve as Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades across Lordaeron. Operating out of shadows and hidden posts, agents like Rane Yorick monitor the wilderness for threats that could disrupt Forsaken dominion. When sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest, Rane and her brother Quinn found themselves hemmed in by surrounding feral dangers, turning an undercover reconnaissance mission into a battle for survival.

npc:deathstalker-vincent.text: Deathstalker Vincent. Deathstalker Vincent was a Forsaken scout sent alongside Deathstalker Adamant to infiltrate Shadowfang Keep. Slain by the mad mage Arugal, his corpse remains inside the stronghold as a grim warning to any who challenge the feral worgen within. Before the Forsaken could launch a full-scale assault against the beasts holding Shadowfang Keep, intelligence on the fortress's interior was desperately needed. Two operatives from the Deathstalkers, the intelligence arm of the Forsaken, slipped past the barricades: Vincent and Adamant. Their mission ended in disaster. While Adamant was captured and locked away in a dungeon cell, Vincent was dragged directly before Shadowfang's master. Refusing to bend the knee or serve Arugal's dark designs, Vincent was executed on the spot, his body discarded on the stone floor to rot as a testament to the mage's fury.

npc:deathwing.text: Deathwing. Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth. Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation. In the present year, the mortal kingdoms largely assume Deathwing was destroyed or permanently driven from the world. However, the black dragonflight remains an active scourge across Azeroth. Led by his cunning brood, including his daughter Onyxia and son Nefarian, black drakes manipulate the politics of mortals and terrorize the landscape from mountain lairs. The scars of the black Aspect's ancient treachery run deep, and travelers wandering through craggy wastelands and deep subterranean tunnels still fear the stirring of the Great Dragon.

npc:deino.text: Deino. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Deino trains Horde mages in the arcane arts. She teaches spellcasters to master arcane and elemental forces, and sends seasoned mages across Kalimdor to study ancient magic and seek remote tutors. Deino trains Horde mages in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Totems, huts, and quiet waters surround the raised platforms where she teaches. Troll spellcasters balance spiritual reverence with arcane mastery, a path Deino shares with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo. Deino sends promising mages beyond Durotar to study arcane mysteries. In Ashenvale's corrupted wilds, they gather tainted Waters of Xavian and enchanted hair from the Laughing Sisters. When a student's power outgrows Orgrimmar's instruction, Deino directs them to remote masters, including Tabetha, a hermit sorceress in Dustwallow's swamplands.

npc:demisette-cloyce.text: Demisette Cloyce. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Demisette Cloyce teaches warlocks beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. She guides students in fel magic and sends those ready for more toward other summoners. Warlocks gather in the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, while the city's authorities uphold order and the Holy Light. Demisette Cloyce lives in the catacombs below, teaching those willing to study forbidden arts. She warns that dark energies corrupt only those without the discipline to master them. Demisette guides warlocks beyond Stormwind when they have gained enough mastery. She connects them with summoners such as Menara Voidrender in the Barrens, where they can seek potent artifacts and learn to bind formidable fel steeds.

npc:deputy-feldon.text: Deputy Feldon. Deputy Feldon is a member of the Redridge town guard stationed just south of the Great Lakeshire Bridge. Tasked with watching the primary road into Lakeshire, he keeps a nervous vigil against the aggressive gnoll packs creeping toward the town perimeter. Standing watch near the southern approach to the Lakeshire bridge, Deputy Feldon represents an overextended town guard fighting to keep basic trade and travel routes open. With the Blackrock orcs pressing from the north and gnoll packs overrunning the southern hills, guardsmen like Feldon are stretched to their limits. Unable to leave his post without compromising the town's perimeter, he relies on passing adventurers to cull the gnolls encroaching on the roadway before they can cut Lakeshire off entirely.

npc:deputy-rainer.text: Deputy Rainer. Outside Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer holds Elwynn's western border. The Stormwind Army officer faces gnolls and bandits from Westfall, coordinating local defenses while reinforcements fail to arrive. At Westbrook Garrison, Elwynn Forest's westernmost post, the road crosses into Westfall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City leaves much of the army abroad or caught in bureaucracy, and border posts like this one lack troops. Deputy Rainer organizes the defense from outside the tower with the few forces at hand. Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves threaten the local roads, so he depends on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers to keep the forest trails secure. Deputy Rainer watches for the Riverpaw pack and warns travelers about Hogger, the infamous gnoll chieftain. He also carries word of the troubled lands beyond the river. The chaos at Elwynn's border begins in Westfall's lawless farmlands, so he sends capable volunteers across the border toward Gryan Stoutmantle and the struggling People's Militia.

npc:dirge-quikcleave.text: Dirge Quikcleave. Inside Gadgetzan's inn, Dirge Quikcleave holds court as a goblin culinary master and vendor. His inventive dishes are renowned across Azeroth, and seasoned chefs come to him to master artisan cooking. In dusty Gadgetzan, Dirge Quikcleave serves drinks and meat to travelers parched by the Tanaris sands. Though his kitchen is in a frontier tavern, he claims to be Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist. Cooking trainers in cities send their most promising students to him when ordinary lessons are spent. Dirge's demanding recipes call for unusual ingredients, from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to exotic beasts from distant shores. Dirge Quikcleave pairs a gourmand's bravado with a goblin's eye for business. Across Kalimdor, he keeps contacts with eccentric figures and seeks out dangerous culinary ventures. Those who bring him fierce beast cuts, such as meat from the monstrous chimaeroks of Feralas's Isle of Dread, can receive hearty recipes fit to sustain champions on perilous journeys. They must not ask too many questions about Dirge's private dealings.

npc:doan-karhan.text: Doan Karhan. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan studies the Burning Legion’s demonic artifacts. A human scholar and practitioner of the dark arts, he lives alone to pursue his research, especially into the enigmatic Orb of Soran'ruk. Doan Karhan keeps a solitary camp in the southern Barrens, far from the Alliance’s civilized bastions. He withdrew into the wilderness to study dangerous demonic relics without disturbance. He knows much about powerful fel vessels, possesses the Orb of Zargain, and is absorbed by the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Warlocks seeking knowledge of artifact crafting and dark rituals often come to him.

npc:doctor-gregory-victor.text: Doctor Gregory Victor. Doctor Gregory Victor is a Forsaken surgeon stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as the premier trauma physician within the Horde, he evaluates aspiring medics seeking to master advanced triage and battlefield first aid. His cold, clinical efficiency keeps frontline warriors stitched together amidst bitter regional conflicts. While many view Forsaken apothecaries with suspicion, Doctor Gregory Victor serves the Horde through practical battlefield surgery rather than blighted alchemy. Stationed deep within the contested Arathi Highlands at Hammerfall, he operates on soldiers battered by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. His station doubles as the primary proving ground for Horde field medics, demanding ruthless efficiency and prioritizing critical patients under intense pressure.

npc:doctor-gustaf-vanhowzen.text: Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen serves as the trauma surgeon and chief physician of Alliance Trauma in Theramore Isle. Stationed within Foothold Citadel, he trains the island's healers and evaluates medics who wish to master the highest tiers of field triage and bandage work. Located on the ground floor of Foothold Citadel in Theramore Isle, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen oversees the medical care of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces and trains the outpost's frontline healers. Facing harsh conditions in Dustwallow Marsh, VanHowzen insists on rigorous field competence, personally putting experienced medics through an intense triage test to ensure they can prioritize critical wounds under severe pressure.

npc:donova-snowden.text: Donova Snowden. Donova Snowden is an intrepid dwarven researcher encamped alongside the thermal waters near Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring. Despite the bitter cold and hostile wildlife, she studies the strange thermal activity of the region and monitors the increasingly corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. While most travelers stick to the safety of Everlook, Donova Snowden has chosen to camp in the freezing wilderness near the Frostfire Hot Springs. She spends her days investigating the curious geothermic anomalies bubbling up through the permafrost, as well as the dark influences encroaching upon Winterspring's native wildlife. Practical and determined, she enlists passing adventurers of both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

npc:donyal-tovald.text: Donyal Tovald. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s historical works. Under an initiative sponsored by young King Anduin Wrynn, he preserves and copies books for wider public use. Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s collection in Stormwind Keep. The library holds historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes, chiefly for the nobility and royal court. Young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an effort to make that knowledge more accessible to ordinary citizens. Tovald preserves and copies the texts, helping keep the Alliance’s lessons and triumphs recorded amid the kingdom’s political troubles.

npc:doomsayer-wiserunner.text: Seer Wiserunner. This respected tauren elder is known as Seer Wiserunner, serving his people faithfully in the rolling hills of Mulgore. From a cave in the hills northwest of Bloodhoof Village, he aids young tauren braves as they undertake the traditional rites of passage that lead toward spiritual adulthood. Seer Wiserunner stands among the gentle bluffs of Mulgore as an elder and mystic of the shu'halo. When young tauren complete their initial trials of strength and vision, they are sent to seek his counsel during their ancestral rites. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and guides the youth on how to honor their forebears, offering the steady wisdom that binds the scattered nomadic tribes into a unified community.

npc:doras.text: Doras. Above Orgrimmar, Doras directs the Horde's wind riders across Kalimdor. He oversees the capital's wyverns, sending couriers, scouts, and travelers on their way. Doras tends the wind riders on a wooden platform above the Valley of Strength. The Horde settled in Durotar, and these clever, leathery-winged beasts became its chief means of communication and travel across Kalimdor. Doras pairs resting mounts with riders and sees that important messages and reinforcements reach distant outposts. Their routes reach the Crossroads, Thunder Bluff, and settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:doren.text: Doren. Lieutenant Doren commands the Rebel Camp nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Once an officer under Colonel Kurzen, Doren led a mutiny after his superior and fellow expeditionaries descended into madness. Now, he directs a guerrilla resistance determined to uncover the source of the affliction and eliminate Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren initially deployed to Stranglethorn Vale under the banner of Stormwind and the command of Colonel Kurzen. The expedition was meant to establish a foothold in the wild southern jungle, but it quickly soured as Kurzen and his inner circle succumbed to an erratic, violent insanity. Refusing to abandon their sanity or their honor, Doren and a cadre of loyalists broke rank. They fled north and carved out the Rebel Camp along the road, choosing defection over servitude to a madman.

npc:drum-fel.text: Drum Fel. Drum Fel is an orc commander stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Alongside his wife, Korin, he directs military efforts to secure the refuge against encroaching trolls, ogres, and human remnants. His strategic push is vital to carving out a lasting foothold for the Horde in Arathi. Situated within the fortified refuge of Hammerfall, Drum Fel oversees the defense and territorial expansion of the Horde in Arathi. Surrounded by rival factions, he coordinates military strikes against the Witherbark forest trolls and the Boulderfist ogre clan holding Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum recognizes that Hammerfall cannot merely survive through isolation; it must break its neighbors' strength to thrive. To that end, he regularly directs veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt regional threats before they can mount an assault on the Horde encampment.

npc:drusilla-la-salle.text: Drusilla La Salle. Outside Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle teaches warlocks in the graveyard. The human trainer works beyond the Holy Order’s reach, guiding new spellcasters in shadow and summoning. When forbidden knowledge leaves the abbey, she moves to claim it. Drusilla La Salle teaches novice warlocks among the headstones outside Northshire Abbey. Paladins and priests practice beneath the abbey’s stained glass, while warlocks keep to society’s edges because demonology and fel magic are taboo in Stormwind. Recruits receive tainted correspondence before Drusilla shows them how to wield shadow power without drawing the abbey authorities’ immediate anger.

npc:duke-hydraxis.text: Duke Hydraxis. Duke Hydraxis is a noble water elemental commanding the Hydraxian Waterlords from a remote, wave-battered islet off the coast of Azshara. Pledged to Neptulon the Tidehunter, he rallies mortal adventurers to strike against his ancient elemental rivals, particularly Ragnaros the Firelord. Perched on a solitary rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara, Duke Hydraxis serves as the primary emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords. While most elementals bound to Azeroth are hostile and chaotic, Hydraxis acts with measured purpose. As a devoted vassal of Neptulon the Tidehunter, he considers water the purest and most essential of the primal forces. He watches the rising turmoil across Azeroth with cold scrutiny, seeking champions capable of shifting the balance of elemental warfare. Hydraxis's central campaign targets the blazing hosts of the Firelord, Ragnaros. He sees the encroachment of fiery elementals as a blight upon the world that must be extinguished. Before bestowing his trust or the tools needed to challenge Ragnaros's fiery stronghold in the Molten Core, Duke Hydraxis demands that mortals prove their strength, resilience, and loyalty by slaying hostile elementals across the continents. Those who prove their worth earn the blessings of the sea and the means to douse the sacred flames guarding the Firelord's domain.

npc:durnan-furcutter.text: Durnan Furcutter. Durnan Furcutter is a dwarven clothier and leather merchant operating out of Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Working inside Anvilmar, he equips freshly trained dwarven and gnomish adventurers with lightweight attire suited to withstand the biting mountain chills. Anvilmar serves as the first proving ground for young dwarves and exiled gnomes, and not every warrior steps forth clad in heavy iron. Durnan Furcutter caters to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who need light, pliable layers to stay agile without succumbing to the bitter winds of Dun Morogh. Positioned right near the hearth of Anvilmar, he sells everyday tailoring and stitched leather, claiming his stock is the finest to be found in the entire valley. Like any true dwarf stationed in the snowy foothills, Durnan appreciates a strong drink almost as much as an honest trade. He orders steaming mugs of Scalding Mornbrew from Nori Pridedrift, who sells the brew piping hot across Coldridge Valley, to fight off the freezing draft. Adventurers running errands in the valley often find themselves rushing a hot mug into his welcoming hands before it cools, then carrying the empty back to Nori.

npc:ebru.text: Ebru. Ebru is a night elf druid sheltering in the crags above the Wailing Caverns. As one of Naralex's few remaining uncorrupted disciples, she watches helplessly as her master's dream of restoring the Barrens curdles into a nightmare. From her perch, she enlists travelers brave enough to enter the subterranean depths to cull the mutated horrors spawned by the Nightmare. While most of Naralex's followers succumbed to the emerald corruption creeping through the caverns, Ebru managed to escape the nightmare's grasp. Camped inside the cavernous skull formation overlooking the entrance to the Wailing Caverns, she keeps vigil over the descent. She knows that Naralex's noble plan—to tap subterranean springs and transform the arid Barrens into lush woodland—has gone horribly awry, and she desperately directs willing adventurers to eliminate the burgeoning deviate beasts threatening to overrun the surrounding plains.

npc:einar-stonegrip.text: Einar Stonegrip. Einar Stonegrip is a dwarven trapper stationed along the main crossroads of the Wetlands. Rather than risk an uncomfortable reunion with his estranged wife in Menethil Harbor, he relies on passing adventurers to haul his crocolisk skins to town. Perched at the central intersection connecting Dun Algaz, Dun Modr, and Menethil Harbor, Einar Stonegrip earns his living braving the sodden marshes of the Wetlands. He hunts the local crocolisks for their sturdy hides, supplying leatherworkers and merchants along the coast. Though rugged enough to wrestle reptiles out of the mire, he is thoroughly cowed by domestic strife. Embroiled in a bitter falling-out with his wife, Sida, Einar stays out on the road, hiring travelers to deliver his bundles of skins to his trading partner James Halloran rather than set foot in Menethil Harbor himself.

npc:elanaria.text: Elanaria. Elanaria is a night elf warrior mentor and coordinator stationed on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She directs developing fighters across Kalimdor, testing their mettle against dangerous threats such as the satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and spiritual entities like the Shade of Elura. Her guidance serves as a crucial bridge for Alliance soldiers honing their martial prowess in the night elven capital. Standing proudly on the Warrior's Terrace within the boughs of Darnassus, Elanaria serves as an instructor and point of contact for martial champions. In an era where the night elves have formally aligned with the Grand Alliance, her role extends beyond mentoring local Sentinels to preparing warriors of all backgrounds for the harsh challenges facing their lands. Elanaria does not offer easy praise; she expects discipline, resilience, and proven strength. She assigns seasoned adventurers to strike down formidable adversaries plaguing Teldrassil and Darkshore, including the corrupt satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and troubled spirits like the Shade of Elura. She also liaises with skilled craftsmen like Smith Mathiel to ensure that deserving warriors are properly armed for war.

npc:elder-bloodhoof.text: Elder Bloodhoof. Elder Bloodhoof is an ancestral spirit found resting just north of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Appearing prominently to travelers during the Lunar Festival, he stands as a revered guardian spirit of the Bloodhoof tribe. Elder Bloodhoof represents the deep spiritual bond the tauren share with their lineage. Manifesting near Bloodhoof Village, this ghostly elder watches over his people and rewards respectful travelers who seek wisdom during the Lunar Festival. His presence reinforces the enduring guidance of deceased chieftains and tribal forebears, whose spirits remain intimately tied to the plains of Mulgore.

npc:elder-bronzebeard.text: Elder Bronzebeard. Elder Bronzebeard is an ancient spirit of the earthen who appears in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge during the Lunar Festival. Bearing the name of the clan that rules the city, his spectral presence serves as a bridge between modern dwarves and their stony stone-hewn ancestors. Appearing near the pool in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Elder Bronzebeard does not wear the flesh of modern dwarves; instead, his ghostly form is that of an earthen, the ancient race forged from living stone by the Titans. Dwarven scholars and explorers are only beginning to uncover their origins through excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond, making this spirit's presence a striking living relic. His very name and visage suggest he is a direct ancestor of the Bronzebeard clan, standing silent witness to how far his stoneborn progeny have evolved.

npc:elder-darkcore.text: Elder Darkcore. Elder Darkcore is an ancient spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival within the throne room of the Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity. Representing the honored ancestors of the world, he offers his blessing and festive tokens to travelers who seek him out. His presence marks a peaceful, reflective moment amidst the ruins of a fallen human kingdom. During the annual Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with adventurers. Elder Darkcore takes his vigil in one of the world's most somber locations: the royal throne room in the Ruins of Lordaeron, directly above the entrance to the Undercity. Surrounded by the blood-stained floor where King Terenas Menethil II fell, this spectral ancestor offers a Coin of Ancestry and his blessing to those brave enough to enter the heart of Forsaken territory to pay their respects.

npc:elder-goldwell.text: Elder Goldwell. Elder Goldwell is an ancient earthen spirit lingering near the dwarven settlement of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Appearing during the Lunar Festival, this revered ancestor represents the forgotten origins of modern dwarven civilization. Elder Goldwell manifests as a translucent earthen spirit, watching over the snowy slopes of Kharanos. Unlike modern mortal dwarves of flesh and bone, his stony form echoes the ancient Titan-forged race from which the Bronzebeard clan descended. His presence during ancestor celebrations offers travelers a chance to honor that ancient heritage.

npc:elder-graveborn.text: Elder Graveborn. Elder Graveborn is an ancestral spirit who manifests just southeast of Brill during the Lunar Festival. Appearing as a spectral earthen elder, he honors travelers and guides pilgrims searching for other ancient spirits scattered throughout northern Lordaeron. Appearing just beyond the Forsaken town of Brill, Elder Graveborn stands among the haunted woods of Tirisfal Glades as part of the worldwide Lunar Festival. Despite the blighted surroundings and the troubled state of the kingdom, the spectral elder offers peaceful greetings to travelers seeking the festival's traditional blessings. In addition to bestowing his own ancestral wisdom, Graveborn shares news of other elders lingering nearby—pointing pilgrims toward spirits abiding in the Undercity, the Sepulcher, and across the Plaguelands.

npc:elder-morningdew.text: Elder Morningdew. Elder Morningdew is an ancient night elf spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. She offers wisdom and ancestral blessings to travelers who seek her out amid the arid canyons and dried salt flats of the Shimmering Flats. Throughout the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to celebrate wisdom, legacy, and peace. Elder Morningdew is one such apparition, visiting Thousand Needles to greet honoring pilgrims. Bound by neither faction nor mortal conflict, she bestows her coin of ancestry upon any adventurer respectful enough to seek her counsel and receive her blessing.

npc:elder-obsidian.text: Elder Obsidian. Elder Obsidian is an ancestral earthen spirit who manifests at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest during the annual Lunar Festival. Appearing among the graves claimed by the Forsaken, he offers the wisdom and blessings of the ancient world to travelers honoring the festival. Standing amid the somber tombs of the Sepulcher, Elder Obsidian provides a striking contrast to Silverpine Forest's gloomy expanse. As an ethereal earthen elder, his spirit manifests during the Lunar Festival to celebrate the ancient heritage of Azeroth. While the surrounding crypts are held by the Forsaken and menaced by feral worgen, Obsidian greets wayfarers of all allegiances in peace, bestowing Coin of Ancestry and ancient blessings upon those who take the time to seek out his wisdom.

npc:elder-runetotem.text: Elder Runetotem. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Runetotem appears outside Razor Hill in Durotar. The tauren spirit offers wisdom and a blessing to travelers who seek her. Elder Runetotem appears beside Razor Hill, far from the grassy plains and sacred burial grounds of Mulgore. Her presence brings the ancient traditions of the Shu'halo to the Horde's home along the Great Sea. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great leaders, shamans, and heroes appear throughout the world to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem carries the name of a line that reveres the Earth Mother and seeks spiritual communion. Travelers who honor her receive ancestral tokens and her blessing.

npc:elder-skyseer.text: Elder Skyseer. Elder Skyseer is the spirit of an ancestral tauren residing atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. As an honoured elder returned from the spirit world, he observes the ongoing journeys of the Horde and remains deeply tied to the resting grounds of his people. Perched high above the salt canyons of Thousand Needles, Elder Skyseer lingers at the windswept mesa settlement of Freewind Post. While the tauren of Freewind Post bustle around the outpost's perilous bridges and wooden platforms, Skyseer watches over the realm as an ancestor who has crossed beyond the mortal veil. He serves as an ancestral beacon for travelers seeking the wisdom of past generations, offering his blessings to those who honor old traditions. Though his spirit commonly manifests among the wind-carved needles, Skyseer belongs to the long line of tauren ancestors whose people honor the sacred soil of Mulgore, where the ancestral spirits of Red Rocks watch over the tribes. Spirits like Skyseer reveal how thin the veil between the physical realm and the ancestral spirits remains for the tauren, guiding future generations through remembrance and ritual.

npc:elder-starweave.text: Elder Starweave. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave rests in Auberdine as a night elf ancestral spirit. She shares ancient wisdom with pilgrims along Darkshore’s coast. In Auberdine, Elder Starweave appears as an ethereal shade among the coastal dwellings. The Cenarion Circle and the peoples of Kalimdor honor her as an ancestor. Travelers pass through the port on their way inland or across the sea, but those who pause before her receive an ancestral blessing. She speaks of the stars, whose paths in this age differ from those of old, and sees them as beacons of hope and fortitude for generations to come.

npc:eleanor-shackleton.text: Eleanor Shackleton. Eleanor Shackleton is a Forsaken outdoorswoman found camping southwest of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than lingering within town or the Undercity, she assists wandering travelers in learning wilderness survival and field crafts. She shares her surname with other Forsaken surviving in the region, suggesting lingering ties from life before the plague. While many newly awakened Forsaken head straight to Brill or delve into the Undercity, Eleanor Shackleton makes her camp in the haunted woods to the southwest. Surviving out in Tirisfal requires pragmatic self-reliance, and Eleanor serves as an instructor for fledgling adventurers seeking to live off the blighted land. Through her various field lessons, she guides travelers in establishing campsites, gathering firewood, and maintaining trade crafts while roaming far from civilization's forge fires and kitchens. In the shattered remnants of Lordaeron, family names often serve as the sole surviving tether to an undead's mortal past. Eleanor carries the surname Shackleton, shared by Pierce Shackleton and Samantha Shackleton in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Whether the three maintain close bonds or merely carry common ancestry from their mortal days, each has carved out a distinct role in serving the Forsaken cause across the blighted kingdom.

npc:elu.text: Elu. Elu is an apprentice wind rider stationed atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Eager to begin his formal training and take to the skies, he tasks Horde travelers with retrieving wild wyvern eggs from nearby roosts. Perched high above the salt flats and canyon floor at Freewind Post, Elu spends his days tending to the settlement's aerial mounts while dreaming of his own flight. As a young tauren apprentice, he longs to join the ranks of the master wind riders who patrol the towering mesas of Kalimdor. Before he can begin true flight training, however, he must prove his capability by supplying the roost with fresh wyvern stock, sending capable adventurers to harvest intact eggs from the fierce wild wyverns nesting at Highperch.

npc:eva-sarkhoff.text: Eva Sarkhoff. Eva Sarkhoff is the spectral remnant of the former head maid of House Barov, lingering alongside her husband Lucien just outside the horrors of Scholomance. Tortured and slain by the Butcher during the fall of Caer Darrow, her spirit seeks brave mortals to avenge their deaths and destroy their cursed remains. Eva served the wealthy Barov family for decades as their head maid, caring for the sprawling keep of Caer Darrow alongside her husband Lucien, the family butler. As the Barovs grew paranoid about their aging mortality and vast wealth, they struck a catastrophic pact with Kel'Thuzad. The manor was gradually handed over to the fledgling Cult of the Damned, warping the grand residence into Scholomance, a secretive academy of necromancy. Eva and Lucien hid in the keep's corridors for six months, scavenging food while watching cultists and monstrosities steadily take over their home.

npc:falfindel-waywarder.text: Falfindel Waywarder. Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid stationed at Thalanaar, the outpost guarding the border between Feralas and the Thousand Needles. From this frontier watchpost, he works to heal corrupted lands and safeguard the southern wilderness of Kalimdor. Travelers wandering down from Stonetalon or the Barrens often find him seeking aid to restore balance to the wild. Thalanaar marks the gateway where the lush forests of Feralas descend into the towering mesas and dry salt plains of Thousand Needles. Falfindel Waywarder stands watch at this remote outpost, greeting weary travelers who have ventured far across the continent. Surrounded by natural grandeur and lurking dangers, he serves as a point of contact for the night elves seeking to monitor both local threats and broader environmental calamities across Kalimdor. Despite his southern post, Falfindel remains deeply concerned with the devastation far to the north in Stonetalon Mountains. The Charred Vale, ruined by dark sorcery and fiery destruction, stands as a painful scar upon Kalimdor's wilderness. When adventurers deliver aid to Falfindel to assist in its recovery, he calls upon the spirits of the forest. Summoning forth swarms of wisps, he directs them to make haste north to Stonetalon to begin mending the scorched earth. In addition to coordinating restoration efforts, Falfindel keeps a close watch on the surrounding region, including the quilboar dens of Razorfen Kraul. By reviewing recovered journals and gathering intelligence on quilboar leadership, Falfindel ensures that the Alliance understands the rising dangers threatening the passes between Feralas and the central deserts.

npc:falla-sagewind.text: Falla Sagewind. Falla Sagewind is a reclusive tauren mystic perched high upon a rocky peak overlooking the central Barrens. Stationed between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, she studies the natural and mystical anomalies troubling the surrounding land. Adventurers probing the twisted corruption seeping from the nearby Wailing Caverns often seek her guidance. Falla Sagewind makes her camp far above the dust and bustle of the Barrens trails, situated on a secluded summit just southwest of the Crossroads. From this vantage, she keeps a solemn watch over the fragile savannas below, observing the sudden shifts in wildlife behavior and the encroaching corruption rising from the subterranean fissures of the Wailing Caverns. Her solitary vigil separates her from the daily trade of the Crossroads, positioning her as an observant hermit tuned to the spirits and the land's silent wounds.

npc:fallen-hero-of-the-horde.text: Fallen Hero of the Horde. The Fallen Hero of the Horde is the lingering spirit of an orc warrior standing watch on the southern road out of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bound by regret and dishonor, he warns passing travelers of the horrors awaiting them in the Blasted Lands and seeks champions willing to deliver his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, this warrior was a celebrated champion dispatched with a handpicked regiment of soldiers to investigate the Blasted Lands and report back on the presence of the Burning Legion. His dispatch never made it; the courier sent north toward Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs. Stranded without orders or reinforcements, the commander eventually marched his soldiers south into the shattered wastes to confront the growing darkness. It was a fatal misjudgment. Overwhelmed by demonic forces, his army was scattered, captured, and subjected to horrific torment at the hands of the dreadlord Razelikh the Defiler.

npc:farmer-furlbrow.text: Farmer Furlbrow. Near the Jansen Stead, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife are stranded beside their broken wagon. Driven from their northern Westfall farm by the Defias Brotherhood, they hope to reach Elwynn Forest. Theodore Furlbrow left his pumpkin patch in northern Westfall with his wife, Verna, as criminals drove them from their home. They salvaged what they could and set out for Elwynn Forest, urging neighbors such as Farmer Saldean to leave too. Near the Jansen Stead, their wagon broke down, leaving them exposed to bandits and wild beasts. Verna tends to their horse, Old Blanchy, while Theodore keeps watch over the road. He hopes to recover the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day and warn Sentinel Hill about the approaching bandits.

npc:farmer-saldean.text: Farmer Saldean. At Saldean's Farm in central Westfall, Farmer Saldean keeps working the troubled fields beside his wife, Salma. While other farmers flee or give up, the veteran homesteader faces rogue harvest golems and growing banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers when Westfall prospered, before those years crumbled away. Overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits now surround his farm, but he refuses to yield his land. Other homesteaders have abandoned their acres or turned to thievery. Saldean and his wife, Salma, stay and work to harvest what little grain they can. He asks wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers that have taken over his fields and his neighbors' fields, so he can clear the soil for planting. Between Sentinel Hill and the northern bridge, Saldean's defense of his homestead helps keep civilian life going. He remains tied to the People's Militia despite the hard times, and sends able-bodied travelers to Gryan Stoutmantle once his immediate troubles are settled. Clearing the wild harvest reapers can only give his farm a temporary reprieve. The lawlessness strangling the countryside still has to be dealt with.

npc:feegly-the-exiled.text: Feegly the Exiled. Near the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens, Feegly the Exiled lurks alone. Once praised as one of the expedition’s finest diggers, he was driven off by General Twinbraid after claiming an uncovered relic’s power as his own.

npc:feero-ironhand.text: Feero Ironhand. Feero Ironhand is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post in the western reaches of Ashenvale. Standing guard along the border between Darkshore and the forest, he works closely with Delgren the Purifier to combat the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand. Located along the road leading south from Darkshore into Ashenvale, Maestra's Post serves as a critical watchpoint for travelers and Alliance defenders alike. Feero Ironhand operates out of this outpost, maintaining communications and trade lines with Auberdine while keeping a vigilant watch over the surrounding woods. Together with Delgren the Purifier, Feero focuses his efforts against the malevolent Cult of the Dark Strand, ensuring the cultists and forest predators do not sever the path between Darnassus's supply lines and the front lines of Ashenvale.

npc:fel-zerul.text: Fel'zerul. Fel'zerul is an orc warlock stationed at Stonard in the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows. Acting under direct orders from Warchief Thrall, he investigates the ominous presence lurking within the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. While Thrall's Horde generally views dark arts with suspicion, the Warchief recognizes that understanding sinister powers requires those who study them. Fel'zerul was dispatched to Stonard specifically to unravel the corruption surrounding the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. By directing adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls, the warlock seeks to determine what evil stirs beneath the murky waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

npc:felgur-twocuts.text: Felgur Twocuts. Felgur Twocuts is a blunt orc scout stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. He coordinates Horde efforts against the regional centaur clans. Standing watch amid the bleak expanse of Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts has little patience for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he assesses the threats facing travelers and settlers venturing west through the mountains, particularly the local Kolkar centaur. Felgur directs Horde champions to cull the local centaur chieftains and collect bounties on the warring tribes who threaten to overrun the region. He is a central contact for anyone seeking to secure the Horde's foothold in Desolace.

npc:felix-whindlebolt.text: Felix Whindlebolt. Felix Whindlebolt is a displaced gnome refugee taking shelter at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. In his haste to flee the radiation flooding Gnomeregan, he lost his personal belongings, and hostile Frostmane trolls made off with them. Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, thousands of gnomes found themselves wandering the freezing reaches of Dun Morogh in search of safety. Felix Whindlebolt fled the irradiated city in such haste that he lost all his personal belongings and tools. To make matters worse, Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, his box and his bucket of bolts back to their camps southwest of Anvilmar, leaving him stranded, destitute, and relying on sympathetic wanderers to retrieve his stolen gear.

npc:field-marshal-snowfall.text: Field Marshal Snowfall. Field Marshal Snowfall is a dwarven military officer stationed in Ironforge's Military Ward to coordinate the Alliance war effort against the rising silithid threat. Facing an ancient evil stirring in the southern sands of Silithus, he oversees the massive logistical drive required to equip the allied armies. Snowfall tracks donated raw materials and rewards those who aid the realm's preparation for war. Standing watch in Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall serves as the central coordinator for the Alliance's mobilization against Ahn'Qiraj. He views the brewing conflict not merely as a border skirmish, but as a critical fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Snowfall oversees staggering stockpiles of supplies—millions of bandages, tons of metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations gathered by adventurers—ensuring that Alliance forces will be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins. Mobilizing an entire faction requires coordination between blacksmiths, gathers, cooks, and soldiers across every Alliance territory. Snowfall monitors each stage of this immense operation, accepting commendation signets and offering supply requisitions to volunteers. Once the required war supplies are fully gathered across both factions, the stockpiles are packed and hauled south to Cenarion Hold, readying the grand assault against the insectoid swarms and the Old God lurking behind the Scarab Wall.

npc:field-marshal-stonebridge.text: Field Marshal Stonebridge. At Stormwind's gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge helps oversee the city's defenses with General Marcus Jonathan. She also receives reports and trophies from major victories. Field Marshal Stonebridge watches the eastern archway at the entrance to the Valley of Heroes, beside Stormwind's main gates. A senior officer in the Grand Alliance, she works closely with General Marcus Jonathan. From the gate, she watches defenders, travelers, and returning champions enter the capital, ready to organize the garrison if danger breaches the outer defenses. Field Marshal Stonebridge also receives reports and spoils from campaigns against great threats to the kingdom. Senior commanders rely on officers like her to confirm important intelligence and mark victories in the field, including the defeat of warlords and monsters in the crags of Blackrock Mountain.

npc:fizzle-brassbolts.text: Fizzle Brassbolts. Fizzle Brassbolts is a prominent gnomish engineer stationed out on the baked salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Alongside his rival, the goblin Pozzik, Fizzle co-founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision engineering against reckless goblin ingenuity in high-speed rocket car races. He constantly seeks parts, fuel, and strange desert reagents to keep his racing team running. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, political alliances and ancient grudges yield to the roar of motorized engines. Fizzle Brassbolts arrived here with one goal in mind: proving once and for all that gnomish craftsmanship is vastly superior to crude goblin tinkering. Together with his goblin counterpart Pozzik, he helped lay out the Mirage Raceway, bringing race cars, pit crews, and spectators to an otherwise desolate basin. Racing across dry salt beds at breakneck speeds requires constant improvisation, and Fizzle does not shy away from unorthodox experiments. Whether testing volatile mixtures concocted from local creature venom or contracting travelers to fetch replacement mechanical parts, Fizzle is determined to keep his driver's wheels turning faster than any explosive goblin contraption.

npc:fleet-master-seahorn.text: Fleet Master Seahorn. Fleet Master Seahorn is a seasoned tauren mariner who serves as the naval commander of the Blackwater Raiders in Booty Bay. Stationed on the upper balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern alongside Baron Revilgaz, he oversees the goblin port's maritime defenses. His primary duty is protecting the harbor from the looming threat posed by their sworn enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. While tauren are renowned across Kalimdor as plains-dwellers, Fleet Master Seahorn chose a vastly different life upon the ocean. Clad in pirate regalia, he commands the fleet of the Blackwater Raiders, the private naval arm of the Steamwheedle Cartel's operation in Stranglethorn Vale. Stationed atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Seahorn works shoulder-to-shoulder with Baron Revilgaz, coordinating shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for the lawless yet strictly managed port of Booty Bay. Beyond repelling pirate raids, Seahorn manages varied commercial and salvage ventures across the Eastern Kingdoms. He coordinates recovery efforts for lost sunken treasures off the Arathi coast near Faldir's Cove, working with salvage divers to secure elven relics. He also keeps Revilgaz informed of lucrative opportunities passing through town, such as competitive angling and local trade, ensuring the Blackwater fleet stays well-funded and ahead of rival operations.

npc:foggy-mackreel.text: Foggy MacKreel. Foggy MacKreel is an intrepid dwarf stranded precariously on the ruined lower masonry of the Thandol Span. Despite the shattered stonework beneath his feet and the dizzying drop below, his only real concern is fulfilling his moonshine delivery north to Southshore. Perched on the broken pylons beneath the shattered Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel appears utterly unfazed by his perilous predicament. While Dark Iron sabotage and war damage have left the grand bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands fractured, MacKreel treats his precarious footing as a minor inconvenience. His primary thought is not his rescue, but an undelivered batch of potent moonshine destined for the patrons of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He readily hires passing adventurers nimble enough to reach his ledge to finish the courier run on his behalf.

npc:foreman-stonebrow.text: Foreman Stonebrow. Foreman Stonebrow is a dwarven overseer representing the Miners' League at Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. After aggressive troggs erupted from the rock and overran the excavation site, he was forced to organize a defense and hire adventurers to clear the pits. Foreman Stonebrow was charged with directing operations at Gol'Bolar Quarry, a key dwarven excavation nestled in the mountains east of Kharanos. When deep digging broke into hidden trogg burrows, subterranean beasts swarmed the pits and drove the miners from their equipment. Refusing to abandon the site entirely, Stonebrow remains at the rim of the quarry to enlist any able-bodied travelers willing to push the troggs back.

npc:foreman-thazz-ril.text: Foreman Thazz'ril. Peons work under Foreman Thazz'ril in the Valley of Trials. The orc labor supervisor keeps crews on schedule and supplies ready for young warriors, but slacking workers and nearby cultists frustrate him. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril directs peons who chop lumber and gather materials for the encampment and young warriors. Building a home in Durotar's harsh red rock takes steady labor, yet the peons often nap under the desert sun. Thazz'ril sends newly arrived recruits to rouse the sleepers with his blackjack, and keep construction moving. While scouting the Burning Blade Coven for mineral resources, Thazz'ril fled the dark cultists inside and accidentally left his treasured enchanted pick behind. Warlocks and their demonic minions now gather in the cave. Too cautious to retrieve the tool himself, Thazz'ril relies on young Horde aspirants to venture into the depths and bring it back.

npc:foreman-thistlenettle.text: Foreman Thistlenettle. In the Deadmines, Foreman Thistlenettle once led a dwarven mining crew. He worked for both the Miners' League and the Explorers' League until a cave-in trapped his crew below Moonbrook. He died with them and rose again as a ghoul, still carrying his guild badge through the dark, collapsed tunnels.

npc:frahun-shadewhisper.text: Frahun Shadewhisper. At Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Frahun Shadewhisper trains night elf rogues. He teaches new scouts and rogues stealth, agility, and covert strikes. Erion Shadewhisper, another rogue trainer in Darnassus, shares his family name. At Aldrassil in Teldrassil, Frahun Shadewhisper teaches new rogues concealment and bladecraft. Night elf society honors priests, sentinels, and druids, yet scouts and infiltrators also help safeguard the World Tree's boughs. Recruits bring Frahun an encrypted sigil. He weighs their potential and guides their first steps in the craft.

npc:furl-scornbrow.text: Furl Scornbrow. At a watchtower northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps watch over Durotar. Too old for the front lines, he crafts sturdy packs for young travelers. Furl Scornbrow watches the central plains from a wooden tower northwest of Razor Hill. In the tense days after Orgrimmar was founded, sentries like Furl sounded signal horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. Durotar has since grown more stable, and Razor Hill has secured its borders. Emergencies come less often, leaving Furl long quiet hours at his post. Furl says his old bones and fading strength leave him unable to fight. Still, an orc does not easily surrender their purpose. He uses his hands to make canvas sacks and packs for fresh recruits carrying supplies. In exchange for coarse thread and practical materials, he equips green adventurers setting out to prove their worth to the Horde.

npc:gaerolas-talvethren.text: Gaerolas Talvethren. At Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids in troubled Teldrassil. He seeks aid against aggressive furbolgs and corruption spreading through the boughs. Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids at Starbreeze Village. They slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream, and his watch has grown uneasy as unnatural corruption spreads through the forest and unsettles Teldrassil. Gaerolas calls on travelers to push back the Gnarlpine furbolgs, whose minds have turned to madness and savagery. He hopes to uncover the taint spreading from their shamans and the roots of their distress, preserving what sanctity remains in eastern Teldrassil.

npc:galgar.text: Galgar. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young recruits serving the Horde. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise. Galgar cooks near the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials, feeding young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, where food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen. Galgar's specialty is called Cactus Apple Surprise. He says gathering spiny desert fruit is a simple task meant to ease fresh recruits into adventuring. The dish still feeds hungry trainees. Every Horde warrior begins somewhere, and Galgar starts them with foraging in the desert.

npc:gar-thok.text: Gar'Thok. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok directs recruits leaving the Valley of Trials to secure Durotar. The veteran orc warrior survived the Kul Tiras landings on Durotar's coast and now coordinates defense against human encroachers and native threats. After the Third War, Gar'Thok marched to Durotar under Warchief Thrall and served as a lieutenant under Nazgrel during the first days of building the new homeland. When Rexxar, the half-ogre wanderer, arrived in Durotar, Gar'Thok warned him that quilboar were raiding the settlement's perimeter. He enlisted the beastmaster to protect the fragile new settlement. Gar'Thok's resolve was tested when Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiras fleet landed on Durotar's eastern shores. At an outlying watch post, Gar'Thok saw naval marines overwhelm and slaughter his garrison. His forces were decimated, but he survived. The surprise assault left him vigilant against the surviving marines, who still occupy Tiragarde Keep and the coastal shipwrecks. From the barracks at Razor Hill, Gar'Thok oversees the defense of central Durotar. He quickly sends emerging Horde warriors, shamans, and scouts to drive out hostile Kul Tiran remnants, repossess salvaged supplies, and recover military orders left in the coastal ruins. Durotar's safety is far from assured, and Gar'Thok keeps pressure on those who challenge the Horde's right to this soil.

npc:gart-mistrunner.text: Gart Mistrunner. Gart Mistrunner is the resident druid trainer stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa. He welcomes novice tauren called by the Earth Mother and guides them through their first rites of nature magic. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner represents the ancient druidic path rekindled among the Shu'halo. New tauren druids are directed straight to Gart upon taking their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often carrying a verdant note commending them into his care. Through his patient guidance, young practitioners learn to commune with the natural world, drawing upon the restorative powers of nature and the lunar radiance of Mu'sha to heal their allies and strike down threats to the land.

npc:gath-ilzogg.text: Gath'Ilzogg. Gath'Ilzogg is the fearsome Blackrock orc warlord who commands the invasion force occupying Stonewatch Keep in the Redridge Mountains. Under his brutal leadership, the orcs seized the fortress and launched devastating raids against the town of Lakeshire, earning him an urgent bounty from the town's desperate magistrate. Gath'Ilzogg marched north out of the Burning Steppes under orders to secure Redridge for the Blackrock clan. Aided by the foul sorcery of the renegade human warlock Morganth, Gath'Ilzogg's warband battered the defenders of Stonewatch Keep and seized the high ground overlooking the entire region. From this entrenched redoubt, he oversees aggressive raids into the valleys and down toward the bridge of Lakeshire, steadily suffocating the human settlement. He rarely fights alone, keeping elite Blackrock guards and a vicious black dragon whelp named Singe close at hand.

npc:gazin-tenorm.text: Gazin Tenorm. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Gazin Tenorm keeps watch near the altar after a dangerous scouting mission in Elwynn Forest. Gazin Tenorm stays in the Cathedral of Light, though his thoughts remain in Elwynn Forest. He and his close friend Henze Faulk went into the woods to gather proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements for the royal court. Defias forces ambushed them. Gazin escaped to Stormwind, but Henze was left in mortal danger. Now Gazin seeks a hero of the Light to help his companion.

npc:gelkak-gyromast.text: Gelkak Gyromast. Along Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded after threshadons sank his ship. The gnome talks like a pirate captain and wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, working again. West of the Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore's northern coast. The gnome talks like an old sea dog and calls himself captain. Threshadons sank his ship just offshore, and he washed up on the misty shore. The key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks. Crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage carried off its pieces.

npc:general-marcus-jonathan.text: General Marcus Jonathan. General Marcus Jonathan is the High Commander of Stormwind Defense, stationed directly at the gates in the Valley of Heroes. A veteran of the Second War, he oversees the garrison protecting the capital and manages military requests from the kingdom's frontier settlements. Mounted atop his steed in the Valley of Heroes, General Marcus Jonathan stands as the first line of defense and the highest-ranking military officer overseeing the city gates. He fought in the Second War alongside renowned soldiers like Reginald Windsor under the command of General Turalyon. In this era of rising tension, Jonathan must balance the immediate security of the capital with the increasingly desperate calls for aid from frontier towns like Lakeshire.

npc:gerard-tiller.text: Gerard Tiller. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works under the warm sun and longs for spring water. He offers a shiny red apple to any traveler who brings him a skin of it. Gerard Tiller works the grounds outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, south of Goldshire. The vineyard is known for its grapes, and keeping the harvest going takes hard labor. The chores leave Gerard thirsty, so he welcomes travelers who bring him a skin of fresh spring water. In return, he gives them shiny red apples gathered from local orchards.

npc:gerrig-bonegrip.text: Gerrig Bonegrip. Gerrig Bonegrip is an unassuming dwarven shopkeeper tucked away in the shadowy corridors of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. Behind the counter of Bonegrip's Runes and Dooms, he quietly buys and sells esoteric texts concerning dark rituals and forgotten ancient powers.

npc:gershala-nightwhisper.text: Gershala Nightwhisper. Gershala Nightwhisper is a night elf researcher residing in the coastal settlement of Auberdine in Darkshore. Driven by grave concern over the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, he studies specimens of cursed aquatic and demonic creatures to understand how magical corruption warps both mind and body. Stationed peacefully within Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond the immediate coastal troubles of Darkshore toward a broader, creeping danger. Watching with dismay as the remaining high elves embrace perilous arcane practices and dub themselves blood elves, Gershala seeks to understand the biological and spiritual descent that follows unchecked magic. To unlock these secrets, he directs seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to harvest corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell within. Gershala's grim focus on brain stems from naga and satyr stems from their shared lineage: both races were once night elves before yielding to Queen Azshara and demonic bargains. By dissecting the physical marks left upon their nervous systems by millennia of demonic and abyssal energies, he hopes to uncover warnings or safeguards that might keep other elven kin from plunging into similar monstrous deformity.

npc:gilshalan-windwalker.text: Gilshalan Windwalker. At Aldrassil's roots in Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the corruption spreading through Teldrassil. His work begins with the Webwood spiders and their growing aggression. Gilshalan Windwalker watches Shadowglen from the stone steps at Aldrassil's entrance. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and their harmony with nature, yet signs of spiritual malaise appeared almost at once. Gilshalan studies how the corruption affects the local beasts, beginning with the venomous spiders weaving webs nearby. Gilshalan studies the Webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Once part of the forest's balance, the spiders have grown hostile and tainted. He sends young novices to gather venom sacs and intact eggs. By studying them, he hopes to learn how the venom has changed and whether the corruption passes through generations or spreads from Teldrassil's soil.

npc:gilthares-firebough.text: Gilthares Firebough. Gilthares Firebough waits in a tower at Northwatch Hold, held captive by Theramore. Once a deckhand on a moonshine transport between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he seeks a chance to escape. Gilthares Firebough is held in a tower at Northwatch Hold. His ship carried illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay when naval forces from Theramore blasted it to splinters. The sole survivor, Gilthares was dragged ashore in chains and locked away. He wears vivid red and bears little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew. Still, he cares little who helps him break free, so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

npc:gnoarn.text: Gnoarn. Gnoarn is an exiled gnome residing in Tinker Town within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Displaced following the devastating fall of Gnomeregan, he assists his scattered people by directing adventurers to assist fellow gnomish engineers and survivors. Like the majority of his brethren, Gnoarn was forced to flee the depths of Gnomeregan when troggs invaded and catastrophic radiation rendered the great subterranean metropolis uninhabitable. Taking refuge in Ironforge's Tinker Town under the hospitality of the Bronzebeard dwarves, Gnoarn spends his days keeping track of other survivors. He serves as an informal coordinator among the refugees, pointing capable travelers toward gnomes abroad who urgently require assistance, such as the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan or the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

npc:godrick-farsan.text: Godrick Farsan. Godrick Farsan is an undead warlock assistant located in the Undercity, serving alongside Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter. Despite being entirely blind, he says that he sees in a different way. Situated amidst the summoning circles of the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar in guiding aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Though he lacks physical sight, Godrick says he can still see in a different way, without explaining the means. He tests practitioners seeking to bind greater demonic entities, dispatching them to gather pure hearts and essences needed for intricate summoning rituals.

npc:golnir-bouldertoe.text: Golnir Bouldertoe. Golnir Bouldertoe is a dwarven mining vendor stationed beside the bustling Great Forge in Ironforge. He provides essential supplies for miners and prospectors while handling dispatches for local couriers and travelers. Standing within the roaring heat of Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. From sturdy mining picks to fluxes and coal, his wares fuel the tireless smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable point of contact for workers arriving in the city, often directing fresh hands or receiving supply missives shuttled in from nearby outposts.

npc:gorbold-steelhand.text: Gorbold Steelhand. In Auberdine, Gorbold Steelhand keeps trade moving along Darkshore’s coast. The dwarven merchant brings goods from far across the Great Sea for travelers, crafters, and night elves. Gorbold Steelhand brings Ironforge trade to Auberdine. Night elves populate much of northern Kalimdor, so Alliance outposts depend on merchants who cross the Great Sea. Gorbold works alongside the kaldorei, selling trade goods, reagents, crafting supplies, and tools. Travelers come to him as they prepare to explore Darkshore’s dangerous shores and forests. Gorbold Steelhand watches the perilous waters off Auberdine as closely as his stock. Reefs along Darkshore have swallowed Alliance vessels, and lost cargo draws the merchant’s interest. Travelers who dive into the deep ocean may find him eager to hear about salvage and lost logs from sunken wrecks.

npc:gordon-wendham.text: Gordon Wendham. Gordon Wendham is a Forsaken weaponsmith and merchant operating out of the bustling Trade Quarter in the Undercity. He equips newly arrived champions and local defenders of the Dark Lady with reliable steel, blades, and bludgeons. Beyond hawking basic armaments, he frequently serves as a local point of contact for couriers arriving from the surface. Situated amidst the damp stonework and chemical canals of the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham provides essential weaponry to those taking up arms for the Forsaken. From basic daggers and hand axes to sturdy broadswords and maces, his stock caters to fledgling fighters who need dependable iron before venturing out into the contested reaches of Lordaeron. Beyond his merchant trade, Wendham is integrated into the capital's busy logistics network. Travelers sent on errands from flight masters and couriers—such as those connecting from the bat handlers atop the ruins—are often directed straight to his stall. His central location in the Trade Quarter makes him an accessible and recognizable fixture for coordinating basic supplies and dispatches throughout the underground city.

npc:gramma-stonefield.text: Gramma Stonefield. At the Stonefield farm in Elwynn, Gramma Stonefield quietly works to ease a family feud. Gramma Stonefield has watched the Stonefields and the Maclures bicker for decades across the road. The oldest living member of the Stonefield clan, she sees their rivalry as senseless and harmful. When her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, Gramma chooses compassion over clan loyalty. She turns to her old friend William Pestle in Goldshire and quietly plans ways for the sweethearts to meet in secret, despite the hostility between their farms.

npc:grand-mason-marblesten.text: Grand Mason Marblesten. Grand Mason Marblesten is an esteemed dwarven stonemason stationed in the busy Commons of Ironforge. Deeply devoted to the royal legacy of Khaz Modan, he has been commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. Adventurers often meet him when assisting with the materials needed to complete this solemn tribute. Dwarven stonemasonry is not merely a trade; it is an enduring art form that shapes the very soul of Ironforge. Grand Mason Marblesten stands among the city's foremost masters of the chisel, representing the centuries-old tradition of carving halls, pillars, and great effigies straight from the living mountain. Based in the Commons, he oversees civic projects and commemorative monuments that immortalize Bronzebeard history. Marblesten's most poignant task is a memorial King Magni commissioned for Sully Balloo, a soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy, as a tribute to his grieving widow. Wanting a truly lasting piece, the Grand Mason insists on one of the finest stones available: Alterac Granite from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad.

npc:granis-swiftaxe.text: Granis Swiftaxe. Granis Swiftaxe is a dwarf warrior trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Known for his blunt demeanor and hardy training regimen, he mentors fledgling Alliance fighters emerging from Coldridge Pass before directing seasoned warriors to the city of Ironforge. Found warming himself among the casks of the Thunderbrew Distillery, Granis Swiftaxe serves as the primary combat instructor for young warriors traversing Dun Morogh. He possesses the unyielding pride typical of dwarven fighters, showing open amusement and disdain toward non-warriors who try to catch his ear. Once a student demonstrates sufficient prowess in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to seek out master trainer Muren Stormpike in the Military Ward of Ironforge.

npc:great-father-winter.text: Great-father Winter. In Orgrimmar, Great-father Winter hears children's wishes during the Feast of Winter Veil. Hired by Smokywood Pastures, he brings holiday cheer near Grommash Hold in the Valley of Strength, though the work wears on him. Greatfather Winter in the Valley of Strength is an orc performer hired by the Smokywood Pastures merchant company. Ancient lore tells of a majestic elemental spirit who wanders the land, bringing snow and seasonal renewal, but the figure in Orgrimmar promotes company wares and entertains Horde children. Some critics say the commercial mascot cheapens genuine seasonal traditions. Still, few deny the festive excitement he brings to the city streets. Greatfather Winter works outside Grommash Hold, beneath decorated evergreens. Children climb onto his lap to tell him what gifts they want, while he promotes Smokywood Pastures discounts and offers holiday greetings. The long shift wears him down. He admits he keeps festive spirits in his pack to quiet the noise when work ends, and visiting adventurers bring him snacks to help him endure.

npc:greatfather-winter.text: Greatfather Winter. Greatfather Winter is the legendary personification of the winter season and the central figure of the Feast of Winter Veil. While ancient legends revere him as a mythical being who blankets Azeroth in snow to allow the land to rest and renew, modern city-dwellers know him primarily through the commercial spectacle managed by the goblins of Smokywood Pastures. According to ancient lore, Greatfather Winter is an ethereal wanderer who walks the world late in the year, casting his billowing snowy cloak across the land so nature may slumber and be reborn. Dwarves view him as an embodiment or herald of the titans, pointing to the frosted crags of Dun Morogh as living proof of his favor. Other traditions, such as those of the tauren, respect his role in the season's turning while attributing the cold and storms to the elemental work of the Sun and Moon, giving the Earth Mother time to rest. Wherever the legend traveled, communities learned to gather and feast together against the cold, celebrating the promise of returning life. In major settlements like Ironforge and Orgrimmar, the ancient spirit has been thoroughly reshaped by the enterprising goblins of Smokywood Pastures. The trading cartel popularized the depiction of Greatfather Winter as a jolly, red-suited elder with a white beard who rides a flying sleigh and hands out holiday treats and toys. Smokywood Pastures hires local actors—a dwarf in Ironforge and an orc in Orgrimmar—to listen to children's wishlists, receive offerings of milk and gingerbread cookies, and advertise seasonal merchandise beneath lavishly decorated trees.

npc:greatmother-hawkwind.text: Greatmother Hawkwind. Greatmother Hawkwind is a revered tauren elder resting by the water well on Red Cloud Mesa. As the mother of Camp Narache's leader, Chief Hawkwind, she embodies the enduring spirit and communal responsibility of the tribe despite her advanced age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside the fresh water well at Camp Narache, serving as the spiritual matriarch for young tauren beginning their rites of passage. Though years have slowed her stride, she refuses to let age sideline her duty to the village. She believes that every member of the tribe, young or old, has an active role to play in sustaining the community, often asking fledgling youths to lend a hand with simple domestic chores like fetching fresh water. As the mother of Chief Hawkwind, the chieftain of Camp Narache, Greatmother Hawkwind provides steady counsel and quiet dignity amidst the threats facing Red Cloud Mesa. While her son organizes hunters and warriors against encroaching Bristleback quilboar and local predators, she tends to the moral heart of the settlement, reminding the newly awakened that strength begins with humility and service to one's kin.

npc:greta-mosshoof.text: Greta Mosshoof. Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid allied with the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood.
