Alongside night elves and fellow guardians of nature, she investigates the foul taint creeping across the ancient forest and directs scouts into the Shadow Council stronghold of Jaedenar. Stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary on the southern boundary of Felwood, Greta Mosshoof works alongside the Emerald Circle to combat the pervasive corruption consuming the ancient woods. Rather than surrendering the blighted lands to the demonic taint left in the wake of the Third War, she coordinates efforts to understand and push back the spreading rot. Her investigations zero in on the poisoned waters of Felwood and the foul cultists burrowed within Jaedenar.

npc:grimbooze-thunderbrew.text: Grimbooze Thunderbrew. In Westfall's Dagger Hills, Grimbooze Thunderbrew brews potent spirits and speaks in verse. The eccentric dwarf belongs to the Thunderbrew clan. Grimbooze Thunderbrew camps in the Dagger Hills, where he tends his private casks. He comes from the Thunderbrew brewing family of Kharanos and left the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh for Westfall's windswept hills. Jovial and devoted to potent spirits, he speaks only in rhymes. A traveler must complete a simple task before he answers any questions, and he is always ready to test a thirsty palate.

npc:grish-longrunner.text: Grish Longrunner. At the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner watches the boundary between the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. The tauren scout carries messages for the Horde and tracks movement across the crossing. Grish Longrunner keeps watch beside the Great Lift in the southern Barrens. Its platform connects the dry southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Quilboar packs roam nearby, and rival groups threaten the crossing. Grish watches travelers and keeps the Horde informed, so reinforcements can be called where they are needed.

npc:grub.text: Grub. At a hut east of the Crossroads, Grub runs a roadside eatery with a cook and a baker. He is known for teaching travelers to cook with the Barrens' local vermin. East of the Crossroads, Grub shares a hut with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. Grub makes use of the Barrens' dig rats instead of letting them go to waste. He offers travelers a recipe for simmering the rodents into stew.

npc:grull-hawkwind.text: Grull Hawkwind. Grull Hawkwind is a young tauren brave stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. As the son of Chief Hawkwind, he helps guide novice tauren taking their very first steps into the world. He directs young hunters and warriors through their earliest trials to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. Standing proudly beside the braves and elders of Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind bears both the proud lineage of Chief Hawkwind and the responsibility of preparing the tribe's youth. He serves as an initial mentor for new arrivals on the Red Cloud Mesa, assessing their readiness to serve the Shu'halo. By assigning trials that test stamina, tracking, and survival against local beasts such as plainstriders and mountain cougars, Grull ensures that young tauren understand that balance and respect for nature are foundational to life in Mulgore.

npc:grunt-dogran.text: Grunt Dogran. Grunt Dogran waits in captivity deep in the southern Barrens. Once assigned to the Crossroads and then Camp Taurajo, he was taken during a patrol into Agama'gor. Grunt Dogran was sent from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo after rising in the Horde military. He led a detachment of grunts into Agama'gor, where they met the Bristleback quilboar in a fierce clash. Dogran was badly wounded and crippled. His comrades retreated without him, and the quilboar dragged him into captivity.

npc:grunt-logmar.text: Grunt Logmar. Grunt Logmar is an orc warrior of the Horde stationed in the southern Barrens at Camp Taurajo. Dutiful and vigilant, he monitors threats surrounding the camp and coordinates efforts to locate and aid missing Horde scouts in the region. Stationed among the tauren at Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar serves as a watchful orc guard on the southern Barrens frontier. The settlement sits close to hostile quilboar grounds and the mountain passes leading into Stonetalon and Mulgore, requiring constant vigilance. Logmar coordinates scouting reports and reaches out to capable Horde travelers when his comrades find themselves ambushed or captured by local hostiles.

npc:grunth.text: Grunth. In Orgrimmar, Grunth eagerly seeks the company of Horde champions. The young orc lives in the Drag orphanage and, during Children's Week, journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero. Grunth is a young orc orphan in the Drag of Orgrimmar, where Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for him. Raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he watches armored adventurers with awe and asks them questions without end. Are armored warriors truly terrifying? Why does lightning on water not kill every fish? Will he ever see someone fight an actual dragon? During Children's Week, an Orcish Orphan Whistle summons Grunth to travel with adventurers on a tour across the world. He wants to meet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Mulgore, see the ruined throne room of Lordaeron, and visit the rugged frontiers where his people fight for their future.

npc:guard-berton.text: Guard Berton. Guard Berton is a human town guardsman stationed outside the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge Mountains. Frustrated by the bureaucratic delays of Stormwind's legal system, he seeks swift justice against Targorr the Dread, an imprisoned orc leader. While Redridge Mountains buckles under the threat of the Blackrock orc invasion, Guard Berton remains posted outside the Lakeshire Inn. Despite local defenses being pushed to the brink, Berton's attention is fixed on a captive enemy: Targorr the Dread. Targorr was captured and locked away deep within the Stormwind Stockade, sentenced to death for his crimes against the kingdom. Yet with Stormwind's execution postponed indefinitely, Berton refuses to let the brutal raider linger in a cell while Lakeshire bleeds. Taking matters into his own hands, he hires willing adventurers to bypass royal delays and execute the orc directly.

npc:guard-howe.text: Guard Howe. Guard Howe is a town guardsman stationed near the southern foot of the Lakeshire bridge in the Redridge Mountains. Driven by a personal vendetta against the Blackrock orcs encroaching on the valley, he offers bounties to any adventurer willing to cut down the invaders. Positioned just south of the large stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill, Guard Howe stands watch over the heart of Lakeshire. Like many in the beleaguered town, he sees the encroaching Blackrock orcs as an existential threat to Redridge. Harbouring a bitter desire for revenge against the clan, Howe actively recruits passing mercenaries to hunt orcs in the eastern hills, offering pay in exchange for tangible proof of their defeat.

npc:gubber-blump.text: Gubber Blump. Along Auberdine’s shore, Gubber Blump fishes, teaches angling, and looks for fresh crab meat. Gubber Blump fishes on the Darkshore coast, between Auberdine’s flight master and ferry pier. While most dwarves favor stone halls or forges, he chooses the shore. He teaches fishing and sells simple angling gear to travelers. Crab meat is among his favorite foods, and he often relies on travelers to bring in catches from the dangerous coast or recover his family fishing tackle. Gubber Blump speaks freely about his family, especially his cousin Graun Blump, who has a beard and an unusual odor. Travelers who help with coastal work, such as gathering crawler legs or finding his family pole, may receive a handwritten thank-you letter and a shiny fishing lure for their next cast.

npc:gurda-ragescar.text: Gurda Ragescar. Gurda Ragescar was an orc stationed at a small Horde outpost southwest of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Alongside Feran Strongwind, she fell defending their camp against local perils in the shadowed forest. Resting just southwest of the fortified walls of Splintertree Post, Gurda Ragescar maintained a modest Horde camp under the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Deep within territory contested by night elven defenders and wild beasts, maintaining such isolated positions is perilous work. Gurda, along with Feran Strongwind and their detachment of guards, was ultimately overrun and killed at their post, leaving only the remnants of their final stand for passing allies to discover. Travelers wandering near the trail may come across the tragic scene of Gurda's defeat. Even in death, the possessions and tasks carried by her encampment offer clues to Horde endeavors across the woods, including missing documents and orders disrupted by the ambush.

npc:hagar-lightninghoof.text: Hagar Lightninghoof. Hagar Lightninghoof is a tauren scout stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Driven by rumors of a strange clutch hidden in the canyon depths, he investigates reports of an alien egg guarded fiercely by local wind serpents. While stationed among the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof caught wind of rumors regarding an unnatural egg nestled deep inside a cavern below. The local wind serpents guarded the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts at bay. Seeking an adventurer bold enough to brave the serpents' den, Hagar hopes to study the specimen firsthand and discern what manner of beast could warrant such defensive instincts from the canyon's natural predators.

npc:halaan-hawk-eye.text: Halaan Hawk-Eye. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne lookout stationed atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Lacking both magical sensitivity and the mystic skysight of his peers, he relies instead on keen mundane vision to monitor the surrounding island. From his perch, he tracks the distant anchor pylons and warns visitors of their faltering arcane stability. Perched high above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye serves his people without the gifts common to many Skyborne. He cannot draw upon the arcane power flowing through the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle, nor can he gaze between worlds through the mystical skysight. Instead, Halaan relies entirely on his sharp natural senses. From his vantage point on the watchtower, he scans the horizon to observe the island's anchor pylons, calling attention to their increasingly volatile and inconsistent arcane energies.

npc:hana-zua.text: Hana'zua. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua lies wounded after meeting Sarkoth on the canyon ridges. The Darkspear scout waits for help from young Horde initiates. Hana'zua lies wounded on the ridges above the Valley of Trials. The Darkspear scout met Sarkoth, a vicious scorpid that stalks the cliffs, and its venomous sting nearly killed him. Unable to move or make his way back to camp, he waits in the dust for passing recruits. He needs them to kill Sarkoth and carry word of his plight to the Den.

npc:hands-springsprocket.text: Hands Springsprocket. Hands Springsprocket is an industrious gnome stationed at the entrance of Coldridge Pass in Dun Morogh. He coordinates shipments between the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley and the town of Kharanos, though recent trogg incursions have severely hampered his efforts. Perched at the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket finds his regular supply runs thoroughly disrupted. He routinely delivers provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos, but hostile Rockjaw troggs have overrun the subterranean tunnel leading out of the valley. With trade and foot traffic halted by the beasts, Hands is forced to rely on capable travelers to carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain corridor.

npc:hansel-heavyhands.text: Hansel Heavyhands. Hansel Heavyhands is an unusually massive Dark Iron dwarf stationed with the Thorium Brotherhood atop Thorium Point in the Searing Gorge. Tasked with perilous field work by the outpost's overseers, he consistently delegates dangerous jobs to passing adventurers using a colorful array of petty physical complaints. His hulking frame stands out among his kin, even if his enthusiasm for fieldwork does not match his size. Even by the broad-shouldered standards of the Dark Iron clan, Hansel Heavyhands is an anomaly. Towering over his brethren with a massive frame that borders on orcish in width and height, his sheer physical presence suggests a warrior built for frontline slaughter. Yet despite his imposing build and formidable moniker, Hansel appears utterly uninterested in unnecessary physical exertion, preferring the relative security of the Thorium Brotherhood's camp high above the volcanic ash. Taskmaster Scrange and Master Smith Burninate frequently assign Hansel the grim chore of culling the fiery beasts lurking in the slag pits below. When told to clear out the predatory Incendosaurs crawling through the Cauldron, Hansel begs off citing sore feet. When ordered to exterminate the Greater Lava Spiders infesting the searing wastes, he claims the blasted volcanic ridge is afflicted with a 'frigid climate' that has given him a miserable cold. Consequently, any mercenary willing to brave the magma flows finds Hansel ready with an open contract.

npc:harb-clawhoof.text: Harb Clawhoof. Harb Clawhoof is a tauren mount breeder stationed just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He tends to the tribe's sturdy kodos, offering them to worthy tauren riders and trusted champions of Thunder Bluff. Situated near the pens of Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof spends his days tending the massive kodo beasts that serve as the backbone of tauren travel and labor. Built to carry immense weight across vast distances, these sturdy animals are essential to life on the plains. Harb ensures each beast is well-cared for, disciplined, and matched only with riders who command the respect of the tauren people. While tauren naturally earn the trust required to ride Harb's kodos, outsiders face stricter scrutiny. Due to their immense size and temperament, kodos are not easily guided by those unfamiliar with their nature. Non-tauren allies who wish to ride away atop one of Harb's prized mounts must first prove their loyalty and earn exalted status with Thunder Bluff.

npc:harken-windtotem.text: Harken Windtotem. Harken Windtotem is a tauren huntsman residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Dedicated to the traditions of his people, he tasks young hunters and travelers with proving their tracking and foraging skills across the golden plains. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem serves as an instructor and guide for those learning the hunting ways of the tauren. Life on the plains of Mulgore demands respect for the natural world alongside the practical skill to sustain one's tribe. Harken evaluates young adventurers by directing them to hunt the native swoops that circle the mesas, collecting their quills to gauge a hunter's patience, aim, and ability to harvest without waste.

npc:harlan-bagley.text: Harlan Bagley. At the Lionheart Armory in Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley tends to the arms and equipment his customers need. He is a human merchant in the Trade District, serving citizens and visiting adventurers from his shop on the district's northern side. Harlan Bagley keeps the Lionheart Armory on the northern side of Stormwind's Trade District. He tends its stock and sells defensive gear from behind the counter. Trade and regional couriers bring supplies to the shop as the capital faces distant border conflicts and shortages.

npc:harlo-barnaby.text: Harlo Barnaby. Harlo Barnaby is a wounded dwarven refugee residing in Menethil Harbor. Having barely escaped the slaughter when the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr, he now alerts travelers to the tragedy that unfolded in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby lived in Dun Modr until the northern stronghold fell to a sudden, savage assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. In the chaos of the ambush, Harlo fled south toward safety, only to catch a stray axe square in the back. Knocked unconscious by the blow, he somehow survived the trek across the marshland and awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor. Though alive, his wounds and memories of the massacre leave him unable to return, prompting him to urge Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

npc:hegnar-rumbleshot.text: Hegnar Rumbleshot. Hegnar Rumbleshot is a dwarven gunsmith stationed along the snowy roadway leading from Coldridge Pass toward Kharanos. He maintains a busy shooting range and equips local hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Set up at a small campsite between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot caters to dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. His camp features a popular shooting range where mountain folk hone their aim against the wild beasts prowling Dun Morogh. Supplying so many eager shooters means Hegnar burns through munitions at a brisk pace, leaving him perpetually reliant on fresh shipments of ammunition from his supplier, the dwarf engineer Loslor Rudge.

npc:henze-faulk.text: Henze Faulk. Near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest, Henze Faulk lies gravely wounded. He shielded his companion Gazin Tenorm from the Defias Brotherhood, and now awaits a paladin's aid. Henze Faulk lies near the stone ring east of Stormwind, at Heroes' Vigil. Defias marauders ambushed him and his friend Gazin Tenorm there. Henze took the attack so Gazin could survive, and fell to the bandits' blades. Gazin reached the Cathedral of Light to seek help. Henze remains between life and death, awaiting the aid of a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

npc:heralath-fallowbrook.text: Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath Fallowbrook is a dying night elf druid imprisoned deep within Razorfen Kraul. Dispatched to investigate the thorny corruption surrounding the remains of the Ancient Agamaggan, he was captured and brutalized by the Razorfen tribe. With his final breaths, he seeks to send word of his fate and a cherished pendant back to his wife in Darnassus. Sent by his people to investigate the ancient boar god Agamaggan and the spreading briars choking the southern Barrens, Heralath Fallowbrook sought the root of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. Instead of unearthing answers, the night elf was taken prisoner by the quilboar. Locked in a squalid pen and relentlessly beaten, Heralath succumbed to severe wounds and raging fever. Before fading entirely, he shared what he knew with a fellow captive, the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, urging him to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred up by the quilboar crone Charlga Razorflank.

npc:high-executor-derrington.text: High Executor Derrington. High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken vanguard stationed at the Bulwark on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades. A no-nonsense military officer, he oversees the Horde's front-line defense against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade threats emanating from the Western Plaguelands. From this fortified barricade, he directs seasoned champions toward contested ruins like Andorhal and Scholomance. Standing directly before the fortified barricades of the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington serves as the gatekeeper between the haunted safety of Tirisfal Glades and the rotting horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Derrington holds little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity, viewing the front lines as a crucible of sheer survival. For Horde soldiers and sellswords seeking to test their mettle, Derrington provides direct military orders, sending scouts and strike teams deep into plagueridden territory to blunt enemy incursions before they breach Tirisfal. Derrington's defensive position is beleaguered on multiple axes. To the east lies the Scourge, entrenched in the shattered town of Andorhal and spilling through the countryside via corrupting cauldrons. Simultaneously, the zealous fanatics of the Scarlet Crusade contest northern fortifications and skirmish relentlessly with Forsaken patrols. Derrington coordinates surgical counterattacks, sabotage against the Scarlet lines, and the systematic disruption of Scourge cauldron fields to safeguard the eastern border.

npc:high-priest-rohan.text: High Priest Rohan. High Priest Rohan is the preeminent leader of the Church of the Holy Light within Ironforge, found pacing inside the Hall of Mysteries. He oversees the spiritual development of fledgling priests across the Alliance and aids those seeking mastery over the Holy Light. Through his guidance and sacred relics, he maintains spiritual ties between the mountain kingdom, Stormwind, and distant allies. Pacing the quiet flagstones of the Hall of Mysteries in the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan acts as the highest-ranking representative of the Church of the Holy Light in Ironforge. While dwarves historically honored the titans, dwarven priests have deeply embraced the Light's virtues of wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan serves as a patient teacher to young acolytes, teaching them the discipline necessary to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair. Rohan recognizes that spiritual insight takes many shapes across the Alliance. Once priests under his tutelage grasp the fundamentals, he directs them outward—sending human and dwarven students to High Priestess Laurena in Stormwind City, or dispatching night elf disciples to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to master elusive mysteries like Elune's Grace. Beyond the capitals, he urges devotees to render assistance wherever hardship strikes, even directing healers abroad to aid the druids of the Cenarion Circle in distant Azshara. In addition to his teachings, Rohan holds custody over sacred relics essential to the wider Alliance priesthood and paladin brotherhoods. Among his possessions is a blessed exorcism censer, seasoned through years of cleansing vile spirits. When the Order of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker require the vessel to temper the holy calling of their knights, Rohan freely yields it—asking only for charitable alms to replenish Ironforge's dwindling food reserves for the city's needy.

npc:highlord-demitrian.text: Highlord Demitrian. Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker. Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

npc:hogger.text: Hogger. In southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger leads the Riverpaw gnolls in raids on farms and travelers. His violent attacks have earned him a bounty from the Stormwind Marshals. Hogger commands the Riverpaw pack from Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest. Since the Third War, the gnolls have grown bolder and more coordinated in their raids on nearby homesteads. The Riverpaw have joined forces with the Defias Brotherhood, exchanging their raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To protect Elwynn's borders and trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has posted a bounty on Hogger's head.

npc:holt-thunderhorn.text: Holt Thunderhorn. Holt Thunderhorn is a tauren hunter trainer stationed upon Hunter Rise in the elevated city of Thunder Bluff. He instructs novice and seasoned track-masters in their craft, offering basic martial guidance and pointing maturing marksmen toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on Hunter Rise above the sweeping plains of Mulgore, Holt Thunderhorn serves the Horde as a seasoned instructor in ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like many elders of his craft, he guides young tauren as they make the transition from roaming hunters into disciplined defenders of their new capital.

npc:huldar.text: Huldar. Huldar is a dwarven teamster stationed along the southern road of Loch Modan, near the shores of the lake. Tasked with hauling vital blast powder to the dig site in the south, his delivery caravan faces relentless harassment from local threats and Dark Iron saboteurs. Hauling explosives through Loch Modan is no simple trade route. Huldar was tasked with driving wagonloads of mining blast powder down toward the southern excavation site, where dwarven archaeologists and prospectors desperately need supplies. However, the wilderness roads have become increasingly hazardous. With local wildlife, troggs, and Dark Iron infiltrators lurking near the lake's southern bend, Huldar finds himself stranded by his damaged wagon, relying on wandering travelers to safeguard the remaining powder kegs and ensure the shipment reaches the dig.

npc:illiyana-moonblaze.text: Illiyana Moonblaze. Illiyana Moonblaze is a night elf supply officer stationed at Silverwing Grove in Ashenvale. Operating alongside the Silverwing Sentinels, she supplies Alliance champions waging war against the Warsong Outriders. Illiyana Moonblaze serves as the supply officer for the Silverwing Sentinels nestled in Silverwing Grove. From her post near the path into Warsong Gulch, she outfits the defenders who hold the southern woods of Ashenvale against the Warsong clan. Beyond keeping the grove's stores, Illiyana equips Alliance volunteers preparing to clash with the Warsong clan in Warsong Gulch. As champions earn favor with the Silverwing Sentinels, she rewards their service with custom rations, specialized draughts, and masterwork armaments designed specifically for woodland skirmishes. She also maintains weapons and armor for weary fighters returning from the frontline, keeping the Sentinels' war effort supplied and functional.

npc:ilthalaine.text: Ilthalaine. In Shadowglen, Ilthalaine keeps watch over the sacred glade and guides young night elves as they begin their lives in Teldrassil. He teaches them to defend their home and tend its balance. Ilthalaine watches the woodland paths just outside Shadowglen's heart. He sees changes in the forest that ordinary eyes miss. When young night elves awaken to their duties, he welcomes them and grounds them in Kaldorei traditions. His guidance prepares them to care for Teldrassil and shoulder the responsibilities of its defenders. Heavy spring rains have brought more nightsabers and thistle boars to Shadowglen than the glade can feed. Ilthalaine asks young defenders to thin their numbers, leaving room for the woodland's other creatures to flourish and restoring nature's balance. Ilthalaine tests young elves against local wildlife and points them toward their chosen callings. He gives each traveler a class sigil and directs them to their mentors in the Aldrassil sanctuary. Warriors, druids, rogues, priests, and hunters all find where their service to the Kaldorei begins.

npc:innkeeper-allison.text: Innkeeper Allison. In Stormwind's Trade District, Innkeeper Allison keeps the Gilded Rose ready for travelers and merchants. The busy inn stands between the bank and auction house, where she offers hearthstone bindings, drinks, and shelter. Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers at the Gilded Rose in Stormwind. The inn stands between the Trade District auction house and the city's main vaults, and its ground floor sees a steady flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. She keeps order behind the main counter and offers lodging and hearthstone services. Allison also joins local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest in the capital.

npc:innkeeper-farley.text: Innkeeper Farley. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Innkeeper Farley welcomes travelers with food, beds, and hearthstones. Well-liked and observant, he keeps misplaced mail and hears the troubles of those on the road. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall, and Duskwood find Innkeeper Farley behind the Lion's Pride Inn counter in Goldshire. He offers meals, ale, cheese, and a bed, and sets hearthstones for those who need one. With a welcoming hand and a sharp eye, Farley serves all who pass through this busy waystation and keeps order at the inn.

npc:innkeeper-firebrew.text: Innkeeper Firebrew. Innkeeper Firebrew manages the Stonefire Tavern in the bustling Commons of Ironforge. A genial host to weary mountaineers and visiting dignitaries alike, he serves hearty dwarven staples and keeps travelers rested beneath the mountain. Situated in the central ring of the Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew's establishment is often the first sanctuary encountered by travelers entering through the Great Gates of Ironforge. Behind a counter laden with flagons of ale, skins of stout, and roasted joints of meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to adventurers bound for the snowy passes of Dun Morogh or deeper into the mountain kingdom. His tavern remains a lively crossroad where miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather to escape the drafty tunnels and exchange tales around the hearth.

npc:innkeeper-grosk.text: Innkeeper Grosk. At Razor Hill, Innkeeper Grosk welcomes travelers on the road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar. His inn offers food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Razor Hill links Durotar’s southern training grounds with Orgrimmar’s high walls. Innkeeper Grosk shelters warriors, scouts, and peons at his inn. Travelers find basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water beneath its sturdy timbers. Grosk also helps the laborers who keep Durotar running. Ukor, a timid peon, hauled food to the Valley of Trials only to learn it was not needed. He asks travelers to carry the load back to Grosk’s inn in Razor Hill.

npc:innkeeper-gryshka.text: Innkeeper Gryshka. At the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers with food, drink, and a hearthstone binding. She keeps the inn supplied with meat from hunters across Durotar and the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers at the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The inn stands just beyond the city's main gates, where warriors, messengers, and newcomers to Thrall's Horde can find shelter. Gryshka keeps the Broken Tusk's kitchen supplied with fresh meat. Trusted hunters across Horde lands send her game, including Zargh at the Crossroads and Grimtak in Durotar, who ship their finest cuts to the inn.

npc:innkeeper-keldamyr.text: Innkeeper Keldamyr. In Dolanaar, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers food, drink, and a place to rest. Young night elves leaving Shadowglen can find shelter at his inn beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the first village many newcomers reach after leaving the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. At the village's central inn, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath Teldrassil's canopy. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus pause at his counter to rest, bind their Hearthstones, and gather rations for the journey through the boughs. An inn high among the branches depends on steady supplies from nearby settlements and tradesfolk. Couriers bringing goods are often sent to Keldamyr's desk, tying his inn to the daily trade that keeps Dolanaar running.

npc:innkeeper-norman.text: Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman tends the hearth at the primary tavern in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity. A quiet, diligent Forsaken, he offers travelers of the Horde respite, hearthstone bindings, and food suited to the varied tastes of both the living and the dead. Located in the bustling Trade Quarter beneath the ruined Capital City of Lordaeron, Innkeeper Norman provides lodging for emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold. Despite the damp chill and alchemical stenches of the Undercity, Norman's tavern remains a bustling hub for travelers looking to anchor their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for expeditions into the Plaguelands. While Norman typically keeps to his duties selling provisions and managing rooms, the seasonal arrival of Hallow's End reveals a more peculiar side. During the holiday, Norman participates in the seasonal revelry, demanding peculiar displays—such as clucking like a chicken—from adventurous patrons eager to earn holiday treats like Undercity mints.

npc:innkeeper-pala.text: Innkeeper Pala. Innkeeper Pala manages the Cat and the Shaman, the bustling tavern situated on the lower tier of Thunder Bluff. She offers visiting adventurers a hearthstone binding, cold drinks, and a place to rest between journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff's sweeping mesas, Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman. The establishment serves as one of the primary gathering points for travelers stepping off the central lifts or arriving from the sprawling plains of Mulgore. Holding a steady vigil over her common room, Pala ensures that weary warriors, wandering druids, and visiting allies of the Horde find a dependable shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar home away from home.

npc:jahan-hawkwing.text: Jahan Hawkwing. At the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing keeps Horde travelers supplied with armor. The tauren armorer works from this outpost in the Barrens, where predators roam the plains. Jahan Hawkwing tends to the armor needs of Horde travelers and defenders at the Crossroads. In the Barrens, durable gear can mean survival against centaur, quilboar, and wild beasts. Jahan works with local leatherworkers, sending cured hides for delivery so his shop stays stocked with dependable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

npc:james-halloran.text: James Halloran. James Halloran is a human tanner working out of the Wetlands to supply fine hides across the eastern continents. Based in Menethil Harbor, he makes a living harvesting the tough, prized skins of the region's native crocolisks. He relies on passing travelers and nearby trade channels to gather raw materials and transport his finished leathers to market. From his home in Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes his living from the marshland just outside town. As an enterprising tanner, Halloran recognized that the perilous bogs offer a lucrative commodity: crocolisk skins. Transforming the rugged hide of marsh reptiles into high-quality leather requires rare craftsmanship, and Halloran's finished goods are shipped out through local trade channels to buyers all across Azeroth. Operating so close to the marsh comes with constant danger. Halloran cannot easily hunt every beast himself while tending to curing vats and trade logistics. He frequently hires hardy travelers to handle the rougher chores of skinning young marsh beasts and managing routine deliveries between his work site and surrounding settlements, ensuring his bustling leather craft stays fully supplied.

npc:jannok-breezesong.text: Jannok Breezesong. In Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong trains young night elf rogues. He teaches stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to kaldorei setting out beneath the World Tree's boughs. Beneath Dolanaar's boughs, Jannok Breezesong teaches novice night elf rogues. He trains those who work quietly beyond the ranks of Teldrassil's sentinels and druids. His lessons teach them to stalk through shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen among the boughs. When rogues finish their first lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok sends them to more experienced trainers in Darnassus.

npc:jasper-fel.text: Jasper Fel. In Stormwind's Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies daggers and vials from SI:7 headquarters. He keeps watch on visitors and warns them to mind their speech. Inside SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies the agents who work there. He offers simple daggers and empty vials for brewing and applying poisons. Jasper works under Mathias Shaw's intelligence division and warns visitors to mind their speech. In a place built for espionage, careless words can put people in danger.

npc:jen-shan.text: Jen'shan. In the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan teaches young hunters the ways of the wild. The Darkspear jungle troll trains orc and troll marksmen in tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Jen'shan trains new hunters in the Valley of Trials. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls come to her with inscribed tablets and parchments that direct them to her. She teaches them archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, preparing them for the scorpids and boars on the canyon floor.

npc:jennea-cannon.text: Jennea Cannon. In Stormwind, Jennea Cannon guides new mages through their first studies. From the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter, she teaches caution and self-control, and investigates disturbances in local arcane energies. At the top of the Wizard's Sanctum's spiral walkway, Jennea Cannon guides those who come to Stormwind to study the arcane. She teaches more than spells, insisting that students learn caution and self-control. Even those who do not study magic hear her warning: without training, magic can burn its wielder. Jennea sends promising apprentices beyond the city walls to test what they have learned. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, they study how natural water sources meet arcane resonance. As they advance, she sends them to investigate disturbances at the Blue Recluse or gather volatile reagents for their first true wizard's implements. When an apprentice outgrows Jennea's lessons, she points the way to greater masters. Those who show true potential may continue up the Sanctum's hierarchy with High Sorcerer Andromath, or travel beyond the kingdom to practitioners such as Tabetha, deep in the Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:jocaste.text: Jocaste. In Darnassus, Jocaste trains night elf hunters arriving from the wilds of Teldrassil. Jocaste trains night elf hunters in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Young trackers come to her after their first training in Shadowglen, ready to take up the hunt in the capital. She teaches marksmanship and survival in the wild, along with the bond between a hunter and the beasts of Kalimdor.

npc:john-j-keeshan.text: John J. Keeshan. Corporal John J. Keeshan is a human soldier of Stormwind's army who fought the Blackrock orcs in the Redridge Mountains. After being captured during the fighting around Stonewatch, he was dragged deep into Render's Rock as a prisoner of war. John J. Keeshan is a corporal in the service of Stormwind, posted to the Redridge Mountains as the Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When the fighting flared up around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan was in the thick of it alongside the other soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

npc:jorah-annison.text: Jorah Annison. In the Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison helps spellcasters find knowledge scattered across Azeroth. The Forsaken cartographer knows both the land and the ancient texts warlocks seek. Jorah Annison makes maps in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, but the work does not hold his interest. He would trade every map in the shop for one good book. Jorah knows more about ancient texts than almost anyone, and warlocks share his taste for a scholar's work. Warlocks seeking the elusive Tome of the Cabal are often sent to Jorah Annison. His knowledge reaches beyond the ruins of Lordaeron, and he can point them toward places where ancient texts and remnants of dark sects might be found. He joins the study of old lore to the geography of distant lands.

npc:jorgen.text: Jorgen. Jorgen keeps watch beside the water at Stormwind's Valley of Heroes entrance. His quiet perch draws people with matters they cannot discuss openly. Jorgen keeps to the water just right of Stormwind's great entrance. Above him, statues of heroes look over the bridge, while he watches those who come and go below. People seeking information they want kept off the record can find a quiet contact there.

npc:josef-gregorian.text: Josef Gregorian. Josef Gregorian is a Forsaken tailoring trainer found working in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. He guides ambitious Horde tailors seeking to weave enchanted fabrics, providing expertise and directing them toward specialized garments. Amid the dim alchemical lanterns and damp vaults of the Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian maintains the fine craft of tailoring for the Forsaken and their Horde allies. While life in the subterranean kingdom has turned cold, cloth-working remains vital for warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian serves as a dependable instructor in the capital, ready to teach foundational patterns and to stitch the first robes of young mages who bring him the right materials.

npc:kaal-soulreaper.text: Kaal Soulreaper. In the Undercity, orc warlock Kaal Soulreaper trains apprentices and keeps close ties with practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde. Among the Forsaken, he guides students toward mentors in distant lands. Kaal Soulreaper works in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where Horde warlocks come to learn from his mastery of demonic entities and curses. Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, while the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron offer practitioners like Kaal ample harbor. Beyond teaching, Kaal connects those seeking greater power with mentors across the sea, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

npc:kali-remik.text: Kali Remik. In Sen'jin Village, Kali Remik guides young hunters toward their next training. She is a Darkspear troll hunter who knows the tracking and survival ways of Durotar. Kali Remik guides young scouts in Sen'jin Village, where they begin their lives beyond the Valley of Trials. A Darkspear troll tracker, she knows Durotar's dry lands and the Horde's settlements. When a novice is ready to leave the local training grounds, Kali sends promising hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill. There they begin learning to tame beasts, strengthening the Horde's frontier ranks.

npc:kaltunk.text: Kaltunk. At the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Kaltunk welcomes young orcs and points them toward their first duties for the Horde. Kaltunk watches over new arrivals in the Valley of Trials and directs them toward Gornek and the path of discipline. While trainers and elders set trials and hunting rites, the orc overseer gives recruits clear orders so they know where to go. The Valley of Trials was chosen to test the strength and resilience of the youths who walk its canyon floors. Kaltunk brings the same rugged practicality to his work. He offers no grand speeches or coddling, and expects each orc to find a place in the world and serve the warchief.

npc:kanati-greycloud.text: Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

npc:kaplak.text: Kaplak. In Razor Hill, Kaplak trains young orc and troll rogues for the Horde. He teaches stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft before sending them to Orgrimmar. Kaplak trains new Horde rogues in Razor Hill. Orcish custom favors open combat and roaring charges, but he teaches the quieter skills needed to survive: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking from behind. When his students outgrow his training in Durotar's dusty red ravines, he sends them north to Orgrimmar, where senior guild operatives can deepen their craft.

npc:karang-amakkar.text: Karang Amakkar. Karang Amakkar is an orc scout stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the rocky coast of Ashenvale. Operating on the fringe of Horde territory, he focuses on curbing the violent furbolg tribes that threaten the outpost's supply lines and borders. Adventurers travelling through the outpost rely on his local intelligence to navigate the perilous tensions of the forest. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar serves the Horde at one of its most vulnerable border outposts. The encampment faces constant pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang keeps a close eye on the hostile native populations that surround the road eastward, ensuring that Horde couriers and scouting parties do not get ambushed by territorial indigenous tribes. Karang focuses much of his attention on the furbolg populations native to the ancient woods, notably the Foulweald tribe. With corruption and primal hostility driving these bear-folk into frenzies, Karang tasks capable warriors with culling their leader and clearing out dens before the tribes can muster organized assaults against Zoram'gar.

npc:kargal-battlescar.text: Kargal Battlescar. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar guards the eastern edge of the Barrens. He watches the crossing from Durotar, judges incoming recruits, and sends capable fighters west to strengthen Horde defenses. Kargal Battlescar watches the road into the Barrens from the Far Watch Post. Travelers and new adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, leaving the Valley of Trials behind. The Barrens is a dangerous, contested land, where aggressive wildlife, centaur raiders, and quilboar tribes threaten the frontier. Kargal inspects those who pass and gathers willing recruits for the Horde. He sends them onward to the Crossroads, where they can aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

npc:karos-razok.text: Karos Razok. Karos Razok is the Forsaken bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. He oversees the roost of undead fliers that connect this contested frontier outpost directly to the Undercity and other Horde strongholds. Perched on the wooden platform above the crypts of the Sepulcher, Karos Razok tends to the skeletal bats vital for Forsaken communications. With Silverpine Forest infested by Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill, overland travel along the northern road is treacherous. Razok ensures that messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies can cross above the haunted canopy, keeping the front line linked straight back to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

npc:katie-hunter.text: Katie Hunter. At the Eastvale Logging Camp stables, Katie Hunter tends horses for Stormwind and trusted Alliance champions. She works with Randal Hunter to keep travelers and soldiers mounted for the kingdom’s roads. Katie Hunter tends the horses at the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. While lumberjacks cut timber for Stormwind’s reconstruction, she raises dependable pintos, mares, and swift steeds for riders. Her horses carry people along the kingdom’s roads and the dangerous routes of southern Azeroth.

npc:kaymard-copperpinch.text: Kaymard Copperpinch. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sells Smokywood Pastures goods for Winter Veil. He trades in the Valley of Strength, where travelers can find festive wares and help with holiday troubles. Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength each Feast of Winter Veil. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby as Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. To a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin. Kaymard also handles troubles that threaten Smokywood Pastures during the festival. Holiday confections go missing, and Metzen the Reindeer disappears. Kaymard calls on Horde adventurers to solve these problems and keep Winter Veil running smoothly.

npc:keeper-albagorm.text: Keeper Albagorm. Keeper Albagorm is a keeper of the grove stationed at the idyllic sanctuary of Stonetalon Peak. Deeply concerned by the devastation corrupting the southern reaches of the mountains, he enlists travelers to help heal the scorched wilderness of the Charred Vale. Perched within the peaceful boughs of Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm stands vigil over one of Kalimdor's sacred elven refuges. Like many sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world acutely. His attention is drawn southward toward the smoldering ruins of the Charred Vale, set afire by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists and now held by Bloodfury harpies who block any regrowth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works tirelessly to halt the spread of the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

npc:keeper-bel-dugur.text: Keeper Bel'dugur. Keeper Bel'dugur is a scholarly Forsaken residing deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity. While ostensibly serving the interests of his people by commissioning expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts, subtle clues reveal far more sinister allegiances. Situated among the vats and researchers of the Apothecarium, Keeper Bel'dugur tasks adventurers with retrieving dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. Among his most prominent interests is the Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings locked away inside Shadowfang Keep. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize the condition of the undead, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions appear tailored toward unearthing ancient, forbidden powers.

npc:keeper-bel-varil.text: Keeper Bel'varil. Keeper Bel'varil is a Forsaken caretaker and researcher stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Working closely alongside Wordeen Voidglare, he directs Horde adventurers to gather magical relics and binding materials from the surrounding lands to further their occult studies. Amid the besieged village of Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil quietly supports the Forsaken's magical and alchemical research. While royal apothecaries and soldiers occupy themselves with the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore, Bel'varil focuses on practical sorcery, dispatching travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

npc:keldran.text: Keldran. North of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar, Keldran works to clear a path toward peace with the Alliance. He directs covert strikes against demonic remnants, hoping to show that the modern Horde has forsaken the Burning Legion. Keldran works from Orgrimmar’s red rock terraces while Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom. The Alliance still sees all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation forged during the first wars. Keldran believes Thrall is weary of endless conflict, but peace talks cannot begin while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without the Warchief’s formal sanction, he takes the initiative himself. He directs trusted agents toward distant threats, hoping to erase the demonic stain and clear the way for diplomacy.

npc:kelm-hargunth.text: Kelm Hargunth. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth keeps the Warsong Outriders supplied. He equips Horde champions fighting night elves in Warsong Gulch with care packages and provisions. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth manages supplies for the Warsong Outriders. The camp stands on the northern edge of the Barrens, beside the border with Ashenvale. Scouts and raiders skirmish beyond its stockade while Kelm sees that weapons, armor, and rations reach the fighters. The Warsong Outriders face the Silverwing Sentinels, and a steady flow of provisions matters as much as fury in battle. Kelm gives specialized supplies to warriors who have proven themselves in Warsong Gulch. His stores include care packages with field dressings and iron rations, along with armaments marked with the Warsong clan's crimson insignia. These supplies go to fighters serving the Horde's campaign in the forests to the north.

npc:kerlonian-evershade.text: Kerlonian Evershade. At the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade wakes from a long sleep in the Emerald Dream. The night elf Druid of the Claw needs help crossing the troubled wilds to reach Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade follows the bear totem as one of the Druids of the Claw. For centuries, these druids slept in barrows and communed with the Emerald Dream. They were called from their slumber during the Third War. Now Kerlonian rests beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his long sleep. He must travel through Darkshore's troubled forests to reach Maestra's Post on the Ashenvale border. The road from the Grove of the Ancients is dangerous. Blackwood furbolgs prowl the Twilight Vale, while Dark Strand cultists lurk along the road into Ashenvale. Sleep has weakened Kerlonian, and sudden bouts of exhaustion still trouble him. He depends on sympathetic Alliance travelers for protection as he journeys south to rejoin his fellow night elves.

npc:kernobee.text: Kernobee. Kernobee is a goblin engineer trapped deep within the ruined halls of Gnomeregan. After stumbling upon dangerous secrets involving Dark Iron dwarf sabotage, he was captured, beaten unconscious, and left to die among the troggs in the dormitory quarters. While conducting business or scavenging within the fallen gnome capital, Kernobee uncovered a grave secret: the Dark Iron dwarves were directly involved in the construction and operation of the massive super rig burrowing beneath the city. Realizing the immense value—and lethality—of this intelligence, he attempted to flee immediately to Ratchet to deliver word to his associate, Tinkerwiz. Unfortunately, the Dark Irons caught him before he could make his escape. Rather than killing him outright, his captors battered Kernobee unconscious and tossed him into a small room along the dormitory corridor, opposite the Clean Zone. Left stranded among feral troggs and radiation fallout, the battered goblin depends entirely on passing adventurers to revive him and shield him until he can reach safety.

npc:keryn-sylvius.text: Keryn Sylvius. On the second floor of Goldshire’s Lion’s Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius trains young rogues. In the reading room, she teaches stealth and bladecraft and quietly guides promising operatives toward Stormwind’s intelligence service. Keryn Sylvius keeps to the reading room above the Lion’s Pride Inn. Downstairs, travelers crowd the floor with town guards, while upstairs she watches the steady flow of road gossip. She mentors rogues learning their trade in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow petty theft and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discreetly sends them to Stormwind City to contact SI:7.

npc:khelden-bremen.text: Khelden Bremen. On the upper floor of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen teaches human mages their first spells. He prepares novices to serve Stormwind through the arcane arts. Khelden Bremen teaches new human mages in a study on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey. While clergy and defenders pursue their work below, he shows novices how to focus and shape magical energy safely. His lessons prepare them for the road through Elwynn Forest and for further study in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

npc:kil-hala.text: Kil'hala. Kil'hala is a jungle troll tailoring trainer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Skilled in working with both everyday cloth and exotic woven materials, he instructs Horde crafters looking to refine their needlework. Beyond common thread, he weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from the laughing sisters of Ashenvale. Positioned at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Kil'hala offers his tailoring expertise to passing travelers and Horde recruits. While much of his craft involves common spun bolts and garments fit for dry plains life, his knowledge extends into rare magical textiles. As a favor to the mage Deino, he fashions nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair taken from the laughing sisters, dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

npc:kin-weelay.text: Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

npc:kindal-moonweaver.text: Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside. Kindal's primary concern lies with the sacred balance and gentle creatures of Feralas that cannot defend themselves against brutish captors. Along with her kin, Jer'kai Moonweaver, she seeks the emancipation of caged beasts and looks out for young animals left stranded by violent poaching. Rather than engaging in grand territorial war, her attention is fixed on compassion: freeing caged sprites and finding a home for an orphaned sprite darter.

npc:kirge-sternhorn.text: Kirge Sternhorn. In the Barrens, Kirge Sternhorn guides travelers crossing central Kalimdor. The tauren keeps watch over the southern trails and sends new Horde adventurers north to the Crossroads. New wanderers often find the sun-baked Barrens daunting. Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers south of the central trails, between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Marauding quilboar and fierce predators roam the savanna, and Kirge helps young adventurers find their footing. He ensures they seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

npc:klannoc-macleod.text: Klannoc Macleod. On Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod puts warriors to the test. The human warrior welcomes fighters from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek mastery of combat stances. Those who earn his respect are sent inland to face greater trials of strength. Klannoc Macleod puts seasoned fighters through their paces on Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast in the Barrens. Though human, he leaves Alliance and Horde quarrels aside. He judges each contender by grit, blade work, and resolve under fire. Klannoc Macleod's trial on Fray Island is called the Affray. Contenders climb onto raised iron grating and face relentless waves of eager brawlers as he watches. Those who endure the onslaught and defeat his chosen champion earn his approval and prove they have the temperament for berserker training.

npc:kor-ghan.text: Kor'ghan. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan watches over remedies and toxins. The Darkspear troll stands outside Rekkul's Poisons and seeks help preparing antidotes for Durotar’s venomous predators. Kor'ghan keeps watch over remedies and toxins outside Rekkul's Poisons in Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow. From the capital, he sends travelers into Durotar’s red canyons to gather venomous components from scorpids. He needs them to prepare antidotes for the dangers of the wilderness.

npc:korran.text: Korran. At the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens for threats to the Horde. The Darkspear troll serves Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar and studies the silithid emerging across the scrublands. At the Crossroads, Korran watches for threats beyond the quilboar and centaur clans. Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar stationed the troll scout there to observe changes in the land. Korran coordinates the gathering of intelligence for the Horde's leadership. Korran now focuses on the Field of Giants in the southern Barrens. Strange, aggressive insectoid creatures called silithid have begun burrowing into the earth. To learn where the swarm came from and what danger it poses to the young Horde, Korran asks passing adventurers to dig up intact eggs with his claw tool.

npc:kravel-koalbeard.text: Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

npc:kreldig-ungor.text: Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery. A primary venture bringing Kreldig to Desolace involves the lost vessel of Karnitol, which wrecked along the treacherous western coast. Karnitol's shipment held prized goods, and Kreldig orchestrates efforts to track down the debris and retrieve the scattered cargo before scavengers or coastal sea giants can claim it all. Beyond maritime salvage, Kreldig oversees the procurement of Desolace's strange biological and mineral treasures for Reclaimers Inc. The harsh environment breeds unique fauna and flora, whose parts fetch high prices among alchemists and engineers back in the Eastern Kingdoms. Adventurers willing to brave the wasteland's predators find steady pay beneath Kreldig's ledger.

npc:krolg.text: Krolg. Krolg is an uncorrupted furbolg living in an isolated hut south of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale. Formerly a member of the Foulweald tribe, he was cast out by his kin, who fell to demonic madness, and will only speak with those who appear to him in furbolg form. While most of the Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left behind by the Burning Legion, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Residing in a secluded shelter south of Mystral Lake, he keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. Having witnessed the tragic descent of his brethren into senseless violence, he refuses to interact with outsiders at face value, speaking only with beings that appear as kin.

npc:krom-stoutarm.text: Krom Stoutarm. Krom Stoutarm is a dwarven scholar and warlock found deep within the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Unlike most of his kin who delve solely into ancient stone and titan relics, Krom studies darker, arcane texts and demonic rituals. He acts as an indispensable contact for Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Hall of Explorers is typically known for dwarven archaeologists obsessed with picks, shovels, and titan artifacts. Krom Stoutarm cuts an unusual figure among them. Lurking in the Library surrounded by massive tomes, he pursues occult lore and the binding rites of demonic summoners. His presence in Ironforge demonstrates that while warlock arts are widely distrusted, scholar-practitioners who study the forbidden arts still operate within the mountain city's halls. When Alliance warlocks seek to bind potent demonic servants like the felhunter, their journey inevitably crosses paths with Krom. Possessing knowledge of scattered occult volumes, he directs aspiring summoners far across the seas—including dangerous forays among the centaur of Thousand Needles—to recover torn pages and fragments of the infamous Tome of the Cabal.

npc:krusk.text: Krusk. Krusk is an orc scout stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Dispatched directly under Warchief Thrall's orders to investigate the Syndicate and recover relics from the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he now coordinates reconnaissance and rescue efforts after his initial infiltration was ambushed. When Warchief Thrall turned his attention back to the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he dispatched Krusk and a small strike team to scout Syndicate activity and retrieve relics tied to the fortress's grim past. However, the human outlaws proved more entrenched and coordinated than anticipated. An ambush inside Durnholde's crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scout squad. Krusk managed to fight his way out, but his comrades were taken captive: Drull and Tog'thar were locked away within the ruins, while the expedition's leader, Gol'dir, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Regrouping at Tarren Mill, Krusk now directs Horde adventurers to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and liberate his trapped comrades. Beyond recovering his scouts, Krusk remains fixated on dismantling the Syndicate's hold over Hillsbrad. The fallen nobles of Alterac represent a volatile threat, operating out of Durnholde Keep and scheming against both Horde outposts and their former Alliance brethren. Working from Tarren Mill, Krusk tracks the movements of Syndicate leaders, such as Lord Aliden Perenolde, hoping to sever their leadership before they can threaten the tenuous Horde foothold in Lordaeron.

npc:kuray-bin.text: Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin is a Darkspear jungle troll scout stationed at a guard post outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He watches the surrounding forest trails for night elf scouts sneaking close to the Horde encampment. Positioned just outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch against Alliance infiltration in the deep woods of Ashenvale. The Silverwing Sentinels constantly patrol the surrounding canopy, sending agile outrunners across the border to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Knowing that unmonitored scouts quickly become ambushing forces, Kuray'bin directs capable Horde fighters to hunt down the outrunners before they can report back to Silverwing Outpost.

npc:kzan-thornslash.text: Kzan Thornslash. In the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to new Horde recruits. He is an orc merchant in Durotar. Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to young orcs and Darkspear trolls in the Valley of Trials. They are taking their first steps as Horde warriors. He offers basic hand axes, shortswords, clubs, and staves for recruits facing local wildlife and hazards.

npc:laird.text: Laird. At Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and cooking supplies to travelers along Darkshore's coast. Laird sells fish and supplies inside Auberdine's inn. Sailors, locals, and travelers come to him while Darkshore's waters churn with dangers greater than those along Teldrassil's sheltered shores. For anglers willing to cast from the misty beaches, the local catch can bring a handsome profit. Laird stays in touch with fishing operations across the channel in Teldrassil. Shipments come from his fellow fisher Nessa Shadowsong, linking Rut'theran Village with the mainland port and keeping coastal trade moving.

npc:lakota-windsong.text: Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

npc:lanka-farshot.text: Lanka Farshot. Lanka Farshot is a tauren hunter trainer stationed at Camp Narache within the Red Cloud Mesa. He guides novice tauren hunters as they take their first steps in tracking, marksmanship, and surviving the plains of Mulgore. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot greets new tauren called to the path of the hunter. Fresh recruits arrive carrying an etched note directing them to seek his counsel. Under his steady eye, apprentices learn the fundamentals of ranged combat, tracking prey, and respecting the wild beasts that roam the grassy plains of Mulgore. His teachings ensure that every young hunter serves as a capable scout and provider for the tribe.

npc:lar-prowltusk.text: Lar Prowltusk. Southwest of Sen'jin Village, Lar Prowltusk watches the Durotar frontier. He guards the young troll settlement and sends travelers against nearby threats. Lar Prowltusk watches the coast southwest of Sen'jin Village. As a Darkspear sentinel, he helps guard the tribe's new home after its people fled their sunken island chain. Hostile neighbors keep harassing Sen'jin Village as the trolls work to secure a permanent home. Lar directs scouts and warriors to watch the coast and curb these attacks, especially those by the Kolkar centaur, giving the settlement room to breathe.

npc:laris-geardawdle.text: Laris Geardawdle. Laris Geardawdle is an eccentric gnomish researcher stationed in the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. He dedicates his academic life to studying the bizarre nature and origins of oozes across Azeroth. Adventurers willing to collect noxious slime samples find him an eager, if slightly unhinged, patron. Tucked away among the towering bookshelves and ancient relics of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle pursues a rather unglamorous niche of natural philosophy: the genesis of oozes. While his dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, Laris is convinced that Azeroth's vile, gelatinous horrors hold fascinating alchemical and biological secrets. He tasks roving explorers with gathering caustic samples from remote corners of the world, eager to test his strange hypotheses on how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

npc:lars.text: Lars. Lars is a beleaguered human survivor camping out in the wilderness of Duskwood. Along with his companion Sven Yorgen, he struggles to hold his ground on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank against the terrors that stalk the forest. Perched in a modest camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars ekes out a precarious survival far from the questionable safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is treacherous at the best of times, but the surrounding woods crawl with ferocious beasts, relentless undead, and creeping worgen. Lars stays close by Sven Yorgen, striving simply to stay alive in an increasingly hostile wilderness. Survival at the camp requires constant vigilance against the local predators. Lars finds himself sorely pressed by the relentless packs of starving dire wolves that haunt the shadows around their fire. Unable to lower his guard or drive them back alone, he relies on capable travelers to thin the hungry predators before his small camp is completely overrun.

npc:lelanai.text: Lelanai. In Darnassus, Lelanai cares for the night elves’ saber mounts in the Cenarion Enclave. She offers nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of the city. Lelanai tends the great cats of Kalimdor in the Cenarion Enclave, beside riding instructor Jartsam. Night elves have long bonded with the fierce predators of northern forests. They train nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged ground with a predator’s grace. In the capital, Lelanai provides these mounts to riders. Lelanai offers saber mounts to night elves with the proper skill, while outsiders face a higher bar. The cats are sacred to the kaldorei, who keep their distance from strangers. She entrusts a mount to a non-night elf only when they have earned the highest respect and renown with Darnassus.

npc:lieutenant-haggerdin.text: Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone. Serving the Stormpike Expedition, Haggerdin ensures that only tested warriors represent Ironforge and the Grand Alliance in the valley. Through challenges like the Proving Grounds, he tasks recruits with recovering banners and relics, and bestows official commendations, insignias, and rank recognitions as soldiers rise through the ranks of the Stormpike Guard.

npc:lieutenant-lisande.text: Lieutenant Lisande. Lieutenant Lisande is an emissary of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. As a human operating openly in tauren lands, she serves as a liaison against the shared existential threat of the Scourge. While human faces are rare across the windblown heights of Thunder Bluff, the Argent Dawn transcends traditional faction enmities. Lieutenant Lisande serves the holy order by watching for signs of the Lich King's taint even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, she rallies brave Horde champions to ride out and investigate the encroaching menace before it can defile the sacred earth.

npc:lieutenant-nevell.text: Lieutenant Nevell. Lieutenant Nevell is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed outside the gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Serving as a bulwark against the spreading darkness of the Scourge, he coordinates local defenders and alerts arriving adventurers to undead threats probing the dwarf kingdom's borders. While the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line in the shattered Plaguelands of Lordaeron, its vigilance reaches far into the south. Stationed in the freezing winds outside Ironforge, Lieutenant Nevell represents the order's proactive defense against necromantic incursions. When Scourge activity stirs in the mountain passes of Dun Morogh, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front lines to ensure Ironforge's snowy doorstep remains secure.

npc:lieutenant-orrin.text: Lieutenant Orrin. At Stormwind's gates, Lieutenant Orrin watches for Scourge incursions and calls for scouts. The Argent Dawn officer stands in the Valley of Heroes, where he directs recruits to investigate undead threats beyond the capital. Lieutenant Orrin watches the road from the Valley of Heroes. The Argent Dawn is known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, but it also guards strongholds farther south, including Stormwind City. When necromantic magic stirs beyond the capital, Orrin sounds the alarm and rallies adventurers before the undead can threaten the people within. Lieutenant Orrin connects the Argent Dawn with volunteers in the southern kingdom. When signs of the Scourge appear beyond Stormwind's gates, he sends scouts to gather intelligence and secure hazardous artifacts. Cracked necrotic crystals are among the objects they recover, helping the order understand and repel the undead threat.

npc:loganaar.text: Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites. Beyond fundamental spellcraft, Loganaar prepares students for the ultimate destiny shared by Kalimdor's traditional protectors: the deep slumber of the Emerald Dream. He instructs initiates on the sacred connection between Azeroth's primal spirit realm and the waking world, reminding them that true mastery will one day require hibernating for centuries to walk among nature's purest, unblemished forms under the guidance of the demigods.

npc:lomac-gearstrip.text: Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac Gearstrip is an ambitious gnome inventor based in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned for formulating the devastating NG-5 explosive, he liaises with fellow gnomish researchers operating across Kalimdor. Amid the clanging gears and hissing pipes of Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues the finer points of gnomish ordnance. Like many exiled gnomes who fled the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Lomac has integrated his tinkering operations directly into the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions designed to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds. Lomac's proudest contribution to modern combat engineering is the NG-5 explosive. Formulated for maximum destructive yield, the compound demands precise handling and rare chemical reagents.
