To refine and deploy such hazardous inventions in the field, Lomac maintains contact with old colleagues stationed in distant theaters, exchanging technical orders and dangerous supplies across the Great Sea.

npc:longbraid-the-grim.text: Longbraid the Grim. Longbraid the Grim is an Ironforge dwarf commander stationed just outside the fallen fortress of Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands. Mourning the loss of his brother and the overrun of the Thandol Span, he coordinates the surviving dwarf forces against the invading Dark Iron clan. Positioned within sight of the bridge to the Arathi Highlands, Longbraid the Grim rallies what remains of the dwarven garrison after the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr. The sudden assault devastated the regional defenders and resulted in the death of Longbraid's own brother during the siege of the Thandol Span. Burdened by grief and hatred, Longbraid refuses to abandon the northern boundary, directing travelers and surviving mountaineers in surgical strikes to curb the Dark Iron advance. Beyond defending the approach to the bridge, Longbraid oversees broader dwarven operations across the Wetlands. He dispatched vital soldiers to escort Prospector Whelgar into the marshlands and works relentlessly to reclaim the lost fortifications of Dun Modr, vowing retribution against the Dark Iron saboteurs.

npc:loramus-thalipedes.text: Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

npc:lord-arkkoroc.text: Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

npc:lord-baurles-k-wishock.text: Lord Baurles K. Wishock. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock lives among the petitioners and dignitaries. Barkeeps know him for unpaid tabs and a taste for strong drink, but his nights in the city’s underbelly brought him near darker dealings. Lord Baurles K. Wishock moves among petitioners and dignitaries in Stormwind Keep, where he belongs to the influential House of Nobles. Though his station is high, he often drinks in the Mage Quarter’s dive bars, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, and leaves large bills unpaid. There, he hears of a warlock coven practicing dark arts in cellars beneath the floorboards. Wishock sets out to have the tavern closed and asks fellow nobles for a formal investigation. Uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

npc:lord-grayson-shadowbreaker.text: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker is a veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. One of the Alliance's foremost paladins, he trains budding champions of the Light and oversees the sacred, arduous trials required for senior paladins to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker stands among the foremost defenders of the Alliance, anchoring the order's presence in Stormwind City. A veteran of the Silver Hand, Grayson does not merely instruct recruits in martial skill; he tests their spiritual conviction. When promising knights demonstrate their readiness, Grayson dispatches them north toward the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands to aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

npc:lord-jorach-ravenholdt.text: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

npc:lord-maxwell-tyrosus.text: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade. Tyrosus now leads the Argent Dawn and oversees the defenses of Light's Hope Chapel. From his command post within the chapel, he oversees broad military operations across the Plaguelands, including tactical assaults led by Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff against Baron Rivendare inside the ruins of Stratholme.

npc:lord-shalzaru.text: Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering. During excavations south of the primary ruins across the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru personally uncovered a strange, ancient relic. The purpose and power of this artifact remain a mystery, but its recovery by such a powerful naga warlord presents a clear threat. Operatives on the mainland seek brave champions to venture into the serpent's den, end Shalzaru's command, and secure the odd relic before the Hatecrest can turn it to darker ends.

npc:lorekeeper-raintotem.text: Lorekeeper Raintotem. Lorekeeper Raintotem is a tauren elder stationed in northern Mulgore just south of Red Rocks. He tends to the sacred burial grounds and asks adventurers to drive off the Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Positioned near the sacred bluffs of Red Rocks in Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends to the spiritual obligations of his people. He asks adventurers to drive Bristleback Interlopers from the burial ground, restoring peace to the ancestors' resting place. Beyond testing fledgling heroes, Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over the hallowed burial sites at Red Rocks. When Bristleback quilboar interlopers disturb the sanctified resting places of deceased tauren chieftains and shamans, Raintotem enlists travelers to restore dignity and quiet the disturbed dead.

npc:loslor-rudge.text: Loslor Rudge. Loslor Rudge is an enterprising dwarven engineering supplier stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. He provides mechanical parts, tools, and munitions to tinkerers across the snowy mountain ridges, keeping critical connections open with gunsmiths like Hegnar Rumbleshot. Operating out of Steelgrill's Depot just down the road from Kharanos, Loslor Rudge keeps a steady inventory of engineering essentials—ranging from copper modulators and bronze tubing to blasting powder and spanners. Dun Morogh's harsh weather and sprawling tinker operations mean practical parts are constantly in demand, and Loslor prides himself on keeping the local gearheads supplied. However, the wilderness between outposts is treacherous; when a courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was chased away by wendigos, an essential shipment of ammunition meant for his valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot, was left behind in the snow.

npc:lotwil-veriatus.text: Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

npc:lucius.text: Lucius. At the Lakeshire docks, Lucius watches the Redridge waterfront. The dwarf works undercover for Stormwind’s SI:7, helping agents with reconnaissance and trade skills. Lucius watches the Lakeshire docks for SI:7, Stormwind’s intelligence service. He keeps an eye on trade, unusual traffic, and threats moving into the Redridge Mountains. Agents sent east from Stormwind come to him to coordinate covert work and practice field skills such as lockpicking. Through Lucius, Stormwind keeps a hidden reach beyond Elwynn Forest.

npc:lyria-du-lac.text: Lyria Du Lac. In Goldshire, Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors behind the village smithy. She teaches them to master their stances and arms. Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors in the yard behind Goldshire's forge. She teaches those fresh from Northshire Abbey, judges their readiness, and introduces specialized combat techniques. Warriors take up shield and blade for Stormwind, facing the threats of Elwynn Forest.

npc:ma-stonefield.text: Ma Stonefield. At Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn, Ma Stonefield tends to hardships close to home. Beside Auntie Bernice, she faces farm troubles, neighboring rivalries, and pests. Ma Stonefield watches over the farm beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, with Auntie Bernice Stonefield at her side. The neighboring Maclure homestead and nearby pumpkin patches bring little peace. Wild boars threaten the Stonefield crops, and Princess causes the greatest trouble. The enormous prize sow tramples fields and devours the harvest the family worked hard to grow.

npc:mad-magus-tirth.text: Magus Tirth. Magus Tirth is an eccentric human wizard dwelling out on the salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Known locally for breeding chickens and tormenting his polymorphed apprentice, he is also a scholar of formidable arcane lore who has squandered valuable tomes on racing bets. While most mages of his caliber study in the libraries of Dalaran or Stormwind, Magus Tirth has taken up residence amid the grease and roar of the Shimmering Flats. Surrounded by speeding rocket cars, Tirth peddles chickens to passersby, drinks, gambles, and has long since cursed his unfortunate apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, into poultry form. Despite this eccentric demeanor, Tirth possesses genuine arcane mastery, having authored esoteric texts on magical power before losing them to reckless wagers on the speedway.

npc:magga.text: Magga. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Magga welcomes new arrivals. The orc lives in Durotar and greets Horde travelers beginning their journey through the valley. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls first meet the wider world in the Valley of Trials. Near the Den, Magga greets those arriving in the valley. Trainers and recruits keep busy nearby, while Magga helps bring the small camp together.

npc:magis-sparkmantle.text: Magis Sparkmantle. Magis Sparkmantle is a gnome mage trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. He offers guidance and training to fledgling spellcasters who venture out from Coldridge Valley into the heart of Dun Morogh. While dwarves gather in the Thunderbrew Distillery for hearty ales, Magis Sparkmantle provides an arcane presence among the casks and kegs of Kharanos. Gnome mages often integrate closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh, and Sparkmantle serves as a key mentor for novice spellcasters ready to expand their theoretical and practical grasp of the arcane arts. Beyond instructing novices in basic incantations, Magis ensures that promising students connect with broader magical circles. When mages outgrow early local instruction or require specialized guidance, Sparkmantle directs them further afield, sending them toward fellow practitioners like Bink or mentors stationed across the Alliance's primary hubs.

npc:magistrate-henry-maleb.text: Magistrate Henry Maleb. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees civic administration in the port town of Southshore, the Alliance's primary coastal bastion in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining order amid constant threats, he focuses much of his authority on hunting down the Syndicate conspirators targeting the town's leadership. Operating from the town hall in Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb handles civil governance for one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. The town sits under constant siege from the Forsaken to the north and West, while ruthless highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb stepped into his current station after the mysterious assassination of the prior magistrate, an act he attributes directly to the Syndicate. Determined not to suffer the same fate, he coordinates active investigations to root out hidden assassins, dismantle Syndicate supply networks, and unmask the rogue nobles pulling the strings from the ruins of Alterac.

npc:magus-rimtori.text: Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

npc:mai-ah.text: Mai'ah. At the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Mai'ah trains young Darkspear trolls in magic. She guides new spellcasters as they begin their path among the Horde. Young Darkspear trolls come to Mai'ah in the Valley of Trials to learn magic. Orcs favor the elements or the warrior's path, but trolls have a rare gift for arcane study. Candidates bring glyphic inscriptions, and Mai'ah teaches them to shape raw power into controlled incantations. That control matters in Durotar, where danger waits beyond the den.

npc:major-mattingly.text: Major Mattingly. At Stormwind’s main gates, Major Mattingly helps guard the capital and advises crafters on protection from dragons. Major Mattingly is a high-ranking officer responsible for Stormwind City's landward defense. He stands watch in the Valley of Heroes under General Marcus Jonathan, alongside the city's garrison. His duties include overseeing gate patrols and travelers entering the city. Mattingly also knows the lethal nature of dragons and guides skilled crafters who seek to make protective dragonscale gear for facing dangerous lairs.

npc:major-samuelson.text: Major Samuelson. In Stormwind Keep, Major Samuelson commands the city guard and its personnel. The high-ranking veteran officer serves in the throne room and once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Before Stormwind's royal court, Major Samuelson leads the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and military orders across the realm. He mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, who serves at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders struggle or seek transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel across the kingdom to Samuelson's desk in the capital.

npc:mankrik.text: Mankrik. At the Crossroads, Mankrik carries grief and a thirst for vengeance. A quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, and he now hunts the bristled beasts across the Barrens. Mankrik and his wife Olgra traveled through the Barrens when quilboar swarmed them during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. The fighting tore them apart, and Mankrik saw Olgra vanish beneath tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Fury drove him to fight recklessly until a blow left him unconscious. Along the Gold Road, a passing tauren druid found Mankrik bleeding out and bound his injuries. He survived the ambush, but Olgra was gone. At the Crossroads, Mankrik recovers, paralyzed by grief and consumed by bloodlust. Thork and other local leaders warn that hatred has clouded his judgment, and they refuse to send official war parties. Mankrik refuses to move on. Uncertain of Olgra's fate, he calls on any willing Horde travelers to search the Barrens for signs of his lost mate and slaughter any quilboar they meet.

npc:marcus-redpath.text: Marcus Redpath. Marshal Marcus Redpath is the senior military authority defending the Alliance town of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts to hold off surrounding ogres, murlocs, and naga. His leadership is essential to maintaining Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. Marcus Redpath is the marshal of Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Southshore endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion, and Redpath now stands at the head of its defense, guarding the port's beleaguered survivors. In the wake of the Third War, Southshore stands virtually alone against hostile forces pressing in from every side. Marshal Redpath coordinates defense operations across the Hillsbrad Foothills, enlisting seasoned adventurers to push back the Crushridge ogres creeping down from Alterac and purge dangerous naga and murloc encampments along the coastline. With the Forsaken occupying the north and Tarren Mill heavily fortified nearby, Redpath's vigilance is one of the few barriers preventing the regional Alliance presence from collapsing entirely.

npc:mardant-strongoak.text: Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

npc:marek-ironheart.text: Marek Ironheart. Marek Ironheart is a veteran dwarven hunter stationed at the Farstrider Lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan. Dedicated to the traditions of the wild, he tests wandering travelers and marksmen alike before welcoming them into the ranks of the lodge's honored hunters. Perched on the scenic ridge overlooking the lake, the Farstrider Lodge serves as an outpost for the finest marksmen and trackers in the dwarven lands. Marek Ironheart embodies this frontier spirit. Unimpressed by titles or talk, Marek requires anyone seeking the lodge's respect to demonstrate their practical prowess against the varied beasts roaming Loch Modan, proving they have the patience and nerve demanded of a true stalker of the wild.

npc:marisa-du-paige.text: Marisa du'Paige. In the caves outside the Deadmines, Marisa du'Paige fights beside Moonbrook's outlaws. Rare among their laborers and highwaymen, she uses arcane magic in the tunnels of southwestern Westfall. Deep in the caves leading toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs guard the tunnels. Marisa du'Paige is a skilled human mage among them. Many spellcasters train in Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, but Marisa has joined the outlaws and brigands in Westfall's underground passages.

npc:marleth-barleybrew.text: Marleth Barleybrew. Marleth Barleybrew is an ambitious dwarven brewer stationed out in Brewnall Village. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan's dominance over the local beer market, she constantly schemes to prove her family's brew is superior to Kharanos's famous Thunder Ale. In Dun Morogh, alcohol is taken as seriously as steel, and the rivalry between the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families is legendary. Marleth Barleybrew resents the near-monopoly that Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin maintain out of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Convinced her own craft is every bit as robust, she seeks clever ways to slip Barleybrew kegs into the hands of tavern patrons. Rather than engaging in open conflict, she opts for petty subterfuge, recruiting passing travelers to secretly swap out Kharanos's prized ale casks with her own.

npc:marryk-nurribit.text: Marryk Nurribit. Marryk Nurribit is the resident gnome mage trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A bit more fond of local brews than disciplined pedagogy, he introduces fledgling gnomish arcanists to their craft while frequently soliciting spare coins for a drink. Tucked away inside the warm hearth of Anvilmar, Marryk Nurribit offers arcane guidance to young gnomes taking their very first steps into magic. Though knowledgeable in the arcane arts, his demeanor is decidedly casual—often seeming far more interested in nursing a flagon of dwarven ale and bumming spare pocket change off his new pupils than drilling them in complex theorems. Despite his vices, Marryk remains acutely aware of the perils outside Coldridge Valley, regularly warning aspiring spellcasters about the lingering radioactive and trogg-infested horrors of fallen Gnomeregan.

npc:marshal-maxwell.text: Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

npc:martie-jainrose.text: Martie Jainrose. Martie Jainrose is Lakeshire's local herbalist, tending to her garden along the edge of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Beside cultivating remedies and flowers for the beleaguered town, she contends with wild beasts trampling her plots and harbors a quiet affection for Guard Parker. Residing in Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose works diligently as the settlement's resident herbalist. Even as Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the region, Martie focuses on keeping the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Her daily labors are often disrupted by local wildlife—most notably the monstrous boar Bellygrub, who frequently ravages her prized garden beds. Beyond her herbal pursuits, Martie seems to hold a fondness for Guard Parker, though Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

npc:marukai.text: Marukai. Marukai is a Darkspear jungle troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the foggy coast of northwest Ashenvale. Dedicated to holding this remote beachhead for the Horde, she coordinates efforts to cull the encroaching Wrathtail naga who threaten the outpost. Zoram'gar Outpost sits isolated on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. As the Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. She directs Horde champions to push the serpent-folk back into the tide and collect their heads, ensuring the outpost remains a viable coastal stronghold.

npc:master-apothecary-lydon.text: Apothecary Lydon. Apothecary Lydon is a morbid researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Tarren Mill. Chronically depressed and intensely bored, he finds joy only in refining lethal concoctions and watching the living suffer. He spearheads the research into potent new toxins aimed at securing Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and furthering Sylvanas's New Plague. Stationed inside the chapel turned laboratory of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon represents the cold, calculating ethos of the Royal Apothecary Society. He is afflicted by a profound, languid melancholy, disgusted by the blooming flowers and crisp air of Hillsbrad Foothills. The only diversion that lifts his perpetual gloom is the art of deathcraft. When left unattended, he passes the time poisoning, dissecting, and reanimating his unfortunate pet frog, Umpi, repeatedly waiting for new reagents to arrive.

npc:master-vornal.text: Master Vornal. In Sen'jin Village, Master Vornal brews for the Darkspear trolls and keeps his craft to himself. The elderly jungle troll refuses to take on apprentices despite his deep knowledge of alchemy. Master Vornal brews draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls in Sen'jin Village. Age is catching up with him, but he remains fiercely independent and refuses to train an apprentice. He mixes his remedies and volatile brews by his own hand. Master Vornal sometimes sends young adventurers to gather harsh or unusual ingredients from the surrounding lands. The materials go into solvents and other mixtures. He rewards those who help, but guards his methods and recipes, keeping the work of brewing to himself.

npc:mastok-wrilehiss.text: Mastok Wrilehiss. Mastok Wrilehiss is an orc officer stationed at Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale. Serving as a crucial defensive coordinator for the Horde in the contested forest, he directs scouts and warriors to secure nearby borders and handle corrupting elemental threats. His presence is vital for maintaining the precarious foothold the Horde holds amidst constant night elf hostility. Splintertree Post stands deep in the shadow of Ashenvale's towering canopy, completely surrounded by hostile night elven territory. Mastok Wrilehiss serves as one of the post's core defenders, monitoring supply routes and forest activity. The position is perilous; any sign of weakness invites swift strikes from the Sentinels who view the settlement as a despoiling intrusion. From his vantage within the stockade, Mastok actively tasks passing adventurers with critical strategic duties. He keeps watchful eyes on the borders leading into neighboring territories like the Stonetalon Mountains and dispatches scouts to consult shamans such as Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring at Zoram'gar Strand. His duties bridge military defense with monitoring the strange, corrupting forces afflicting the local elementals.

npc:mathredis-firestar.text: Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself. Adventurers who bring Mathredis the proper tomes—such as the Librams of Constitution, Resilience, Rumination, Tenacity, or Voracity—along with rare reagents will find him eager to trade his craft. The process binds volatile magical reagents directly to the text, concentrating their essence into an arcanum that can permanently enchant headwear or leg armor. So long as adventurers supply the components, Mathredis receives both payment and the ambient arcane sustenance he desperately craves.

npc:maur-grimtotem.text: Maur Grimtotem. Deep in Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Maur Grimtotem lies dead. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent him to seek peace with the troggs, and his remains and satchel are still in the caverns. Maur Grimtotem went into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar as an envoy to the troggs. Most of the Horde saw them as savage brutes beyond negotiation, but Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought peace might be possible, or at least said so. Maur carried her offer into the winding caverns. The troggs killed him, and his body remains under the watch of their chieftain, Oggleflint.

npc:maur-raincaller.text: Maur Raincaller. Maur Raincaller is a tauren resident found residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Connected to the natural and spiritual life of the plains, he assists the village elders and watches over local matters affecting the herds and wild beasts. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village on the shores of Lake Stonebull, Maur Raincaller serves his community by attending to regional ecological and beast-related concerns. Like many who bear the mantle of Raincaller, he pays close attention to the balance of the elements and wildlife across the fertile plains of Mulgore. After a bite from the fearsome strider Mazzranache left his wound infected, Maur turns to capable young travelers to gather the animal parts he needs for a remedy.

npc:maurin-bonesplitter.text: Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it. Maurin directs most of his malice toward the Burning Blade cult entrenched across Desolace. He harbors utter disgust for their reckless ambition, mocking the cultists for failing to understand that their borrowed power merely binds them as thralls to their demonic masters. Through scrying spells and ritual knowledge, Maurin enlists Horde adventurers to systematically disrupt the cult's summonings and undermine their operations across the barren landscape.

npc:maxan-anvol.text: Maxan Anvol. Maxan Anvol is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Dedicated to the Holy Light, he guides fledgling dwarven priests as they learn to channel divine power amid Dun Morogh's frigid climes. He tests young acolytes to ensure they are worthy of wearing the vestments of the church. While it might seem strange to find an ordained minister of the Holy Light stationed inside Thunderbrew Distillery, it suits dwarven culture well. Kharanos serves as the primary hub between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and the local inn is where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes naturally gather. Maxan tends to the spiritual welfare of the hamlet alongside pints of stout, offering prayers and counsel to any who step through the doors. Maxan Anvol is responsible for vetting novice priests before they venture into the wider world. He tasks initiates with demonstrating mastery over fundamental curative prayers on wounded defenders of Dun Morogh. Those who prove their devotion and practical competence are bestowed their first proper priestly vestments, formally marking their recognized standing within the Church of the Holy Light.

npc:maybell-maclure.text: Maybell Maclure. At the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest, Maybell Maclure loves a Stonefield in secret. Her family’s bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields keeps her apart from Tommy Joe Stonefield. Maybell Maclure works the family vineyards under the shadow of a long feud with the Stonefields next door. She has fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, heir to the rival farm. Their relatives keep them apart, and Maybell searches for a way to speak with him beyond her family’s watchful eyes.

npc:melithar-staghelm.text: Melithar Staghelm. Outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm guides young night elves. He sends them to learn why the dryad Tarindrella has returned to the glade. His Staghelm name links him to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, though their connection is unknown. Melithar Staghelm waits outside Aldrassil, where night elves first step into the world. A druid who listens to the forest spirits, he has learned that Tarindrella, a woodland protector, has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing trouble, Melithar sends newcomers southwest of Aldrassil to find the dryad and learn why she has come back to the grove. The Staghelm name draws notice because Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus, after Malfurion Stormrage disappeared into the Emerald Dream. Melithar makes no claim to a grand heritage and says nothing of his lineage. Whether he belongs to the Archdruid's family or shares an ancient Kaldorei name remains unknown. For now, Melithar tends to his humble duties at the roots of Aldrassil.

npc:merissa-stilwell.text: Merissa Stilwell. At Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell welcomes newcomers to Northshire Valley. The young human townsperson offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to those training nearby. Merissa Stilwell greets fresh recruits arriving in Northshire Valley from her place at Northshire Abbey. She offers newcomers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting and finding their way. Her surname is shared by craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom, including the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell. Merissa remains a peaceful local presence amid the kingdom's rising tensions.

npc:merrin-rockweaver.text: Merrin Rockweaver. Merrin Rockweaver is a dwarven researcher representing the Explorers' League in the Wetlands. Following a violent raptor infestation that overran Whelgar's Excavation Site, she took refuge alongside Prospector Whelgar on a ridge overlooking the site. Merrin Rockweaver traveled to the Wetlands on behalf of the Ironforge Explorers' League to unearth ancient Titan secrets buried beneath the muck. The expedition ended in disaster when the large bones they unearthed drew raptors to the dig. Vicious prehistoric beasts swarmed the trenches, forcing Merrin and the surviving crew to abandon their equipment, notes, and progress. She is now trapped with the few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins. Trapped on the bluff, the survivors refuse to let the expedition become an outright failure. While Ormer Ironbraid plots vengeance against the beasts and Prospector Whelgar seeks the tablet fragments left behind in the raptor-infested trenches, Merrin's thoughts turn to her husband Tarrel, who has not heard from her in weeks. She relies on the scout Longbraid sent to find the team to carry word of their plight back to him.

npc:miles-welsh.text: Miles Welsh. Miles Welsh is a Forsaken priest trainer residing deep within the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. He offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline to priests traversing the tauren capital. Miles Welsh stands far from the plague-scarred ruins of Lordaeron, making his home in the humid, spirit-laden grotto beneath Thunder Bluff known as the Pools of Vision. As a Forsaken priest, he instructs travelers who channel divine and shadowy energies. His presence in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous diplomatic ties binding the Forsaken to the Horde, sharing sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in the arts of shadow and faith.

npc:milli-featherwhistle.text: Milli Featherwhistle. Milli Featherwhistle is a master gnomish mechanostrider engineer stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Following the fall of Gnomeregan, she meticulously handcrafts and maintains the clockwork mounts favored by her kin. She sells her prized mechanical creations to fellow gnomes and trusted allies of the exiled Gnomeregan survivors. Operating outdoors in the biting chill of Steelgrill's Depot just east of Kharanos, Milli Featherwhistle oversees the supply of clockwork steeds for Gnomeregan's displaced populace. Unlike the biological beasts favored by dwarves and night elves, Milli builds her entire inventory herself, personally calibrating gears, pistons, and balancing gyros to ensure each mechanical bird runs at peak efficiency across the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. Every frame and spring in Milli's workshop is rooted in blueprints originally drafted by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. While Milli has integrated modern performance improvements over the years—streamlining chassis weights and refining exhaust vents—she faithfully adheres to the High Tinker's foundational schematics. Her mechanical wonders prove that even in exile, gnomish technological ambition remains thoroughly unbroken.

npc:milton-sheaf.text: Milton Sheaf. In Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf guards the kingdom's written history. He tends the Royal Library and calls on Alliance travelers to recover lost books and records. Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. While the court handles politics, noble disputes, and military concerns, he preserves the written record. He sees accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms as a duty, especially amid war, loss, and instability. Milton Sheaf sends travelers to recover books scattered across the realm. Volumes wear with use, while records lie in monastic archives, distant outposts, and forgotten ruins. He sends Alliance adventurers from Northshire Abbey to Southshore in the north to retrieve misplaced books, examine ancient texts, and return rare manuscripts safely to the keep.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-earth.text: Minor Manifestation of Earth. A Minor Manifestation of Earth is a localized elemental spirit bound to sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar. Invisible to ordinary sight, it reveals itself only to fledgling shamans who drink the sacred Earth Sapta, providing the rough quartz required to carve their very first earth totem. The spirits of the earth dwell everywhere beneath the dirt and stone, but communicating with them requires deliberate ritual. At sacred landmarks like Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger in the unseen realm, surrounded by even smaller elemental presences. Only initiates who have drunk the Earth Sapta—a ritual draught brewed by shamanic mentors—can lift the veil between the physical world and the elements. Once acknowledged, the spirit imparts the earth's blessings along with a piece of rough quartz, granting the novice the spiritual focal point needed to fashion an Earth Totem.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-water.text: Minor Manifestation of Water. The Minor Manifestation of Water is an elemental spirit found along North Tide's Run on the coast of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital trial for Horde shamans seeking to commune with and master the element of water. Before this peaceful spirit can be consulted, initiates must first cleanse its corrupted counterpart. Lurking along the mist-shrouded shores of North Tide's Run, west of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, the Minor Manifestation of Water represents an essential rite of passage for developing shamans. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, but they can easily fall victim to malevolent blight. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation of this elemental before the pure Minor Manifestation of Water can reveal itself. Once cleansed, the spirit offers guidance to shamans completing their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

npc:misha.text: Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles. Misha is far more than a tame pet; she is a seasoned warrior. She fought alongside Rexxar in the brutal conflict against Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, helping ensure the young Horde's survival. When not in battle, her keen senses and strength serve as an extension of Rexxar's will. Currently, travelers venturing along the long tracks through the Stonetalon Mountains, Desolace, and Feralas can spot Misha padding quietly beside Rexxar. Though fierce enough to tear apart any predator foolish enough to threaten them, she remains Rexxar's steadfast anchor in an otherwise untrustworthy world.

npc:misha-tor-kren.text: Misha Tor'kren. At the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, Misha Tor'kren waits for word of her son. Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks, but has not returned. Misha Tor'kren tends her farm near Thunder Ridge, southeast of the ridge. Her son Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never came home. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching the orcish watchtowers thin, Misha has no word of where he is. She needs travelers willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her son.

npc:mitsuwa.text: Mitsuwa. Mitsuwa is a Darkspear troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the misty coast of Ashenvale. Deeply troubled by the ambush of his traveling kin, he enlists Horde champions to avenge the fallen and reclaim stolen spiritual talismans. Situated at the remote Zoram'gar Outpost on the strand of the Zoram Strand, Mitsuwa serves the Horde alongside his companion Marukai. When a group of traveling trolls bound for the encampment was ambushed and slaughtered by the aggressive Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale, Mitsuwa took the loss as a grievous offense. Driven by duty and anger, he directs able-bodied warriors toward the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms, ensuring the spirits of his kin are honored and their sacred possessions recovered from the beasts.

npc:monte-gazlowe.text: Monte Gazlowe. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe keeps a neutral port open to traders from every side. He founded the town with the fortune he earned as the Horde’s chief engineer during the building of Durotar and Orgrimmar. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe runs a port where rivals can trade under the Steamwheedle Cartel. He founded the town on the barren coast after earning a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde. Horde, Alliance, and independent traders may barter there, so long as they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy. After the Third War, Warchief Thrall hired Monte Gazlowe as Durotar’s chief engineer to solve urgent problems for the new orc capital. Gazlowe took on the dangerous work of securing freshwater for Orgrimmar. His tunnels broke into underground kobold dens, but the wandering beastmaster Rexxar arrived in time to help blast the caverns shut. Gazlowe finished his assignments and remains a favored contractor and friend to Thrall. He has even sent his foreman, Rezlak, to keep helping with orc construction across Durotar. Trade brings good earnings to Ratchet, but maritime rivals and thieves trouble Monte Gazlowe’s business. The Southsea Freebooters have camps along the nearby Merchant Coast, where they seize cargo bound for Ratchet and steal goods from raw ore to Gazlowe’s custom-ordered boots. To protect his profits, the port boss often hires passing sellswords of any allegiance to clear pirate camps, recover stolen shipments, and settle scores with troublemakers at the docks.

npc:moon-priestess-amara.text: Moon Priestess Amara. West of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara watches Teldrassil’s road to Darnassus. Two huntresses guard her as she keeps watch over the woodland paths. Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west of Dolanaar with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. As a priestess of the Sisterhood of Elune, she brings spiritual guidance to her post, while her watch helps keep Teldrassil’s roads secure. Travelers heading west can seek her direction toward Darnassus. Those burdened in spirit can also seek a path of redemption from her.

npc:mor-rogal.text: Mor'rogal. Mor'rogal is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. He serves as an advisor and guide for travelers seeking glory and peril within the rugged subterranean reaches of the crags. Perched within the refuge of Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal takes a keen interest in the deep crevices and caverns that cut through the Stonetalon Mountains. Recognizing that the region's twisting subterranean passes offer both great riches and lethal danger, he directs brave Horde wanderers to investigate troubled areas like the Boulderslide Ravine. For Mor'rogal, delving into these treacherous depths is not merely a matter of survival, but a test of spirit for those who follow their heart and soul in search of glory.

npc:morgan-pestle.text: Morgan Pestle. In Stormwind, Morgan Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. He works with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, handling supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Morgan Pestle sells alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. His brother William keeps a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, while Morgan tends their family trade in the capital. He receives supplies from the rural heartlands, including candles sent by William.

npc:morgan-the-collector.text: Morgan the Collector. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Morgan the Collector directs Defias extortion and gathering across Elwynn Forest. A high-ranking operative, he coordinates local theft from the farmhouse while Goldshire's guard keeps watch nearby. Morgan the Collector skims gold from Elwynn Forest's mines for the Defias Brotherhood. While common bandits harass travelers on the roads, he directs organized shakedowns and gathers stolen coin and supplies for the Brotherhood's wider network. His headquarters is the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor surround him.

npc:mountaineer-barleybrew.text: Mountaineer Barleybrew. Mountaineer Barleybrew is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at the South Gate Outpost in Dun Morogh. Guarding the pass leading eastward toward Loch Modan, he relies on hearty dwarven brews to keep sentries alert in the biting cold. Perched at the South Gate Outpost guarding the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew stands as part of Ironforge's border watch. Like many mountaineers serving in the bitter winds of Dun Morogh, he appreciates the fortifying qualities of fine dwarven drink. Bearing the name of the renowned Barleybrew clan, he helps see to it that shipments of potent Shimmer Stout make their way to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts along the mountain passes.

npc:mountaineer-kadrell.text: Mountaineer Kadrell. Mountaineer Kadrell is a stalwart dwarven sentry stationed across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Serving as a crucial liaison within the Loch Modan Mountaineers, he coordinates reconnaissance, supply deliveries, and border defense across the region. Standing watch in the bustling settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell acts as an anchor for dwarven defenses throughout Loch Modan. While outposts on the valley's fringes face relentless pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts, Kadrell remains at the center of town to organize reinforcements, relay orders, and assess incoming field reports from wandering scouts. Kadrell's duties frequently involve maintaining contact between Thelsamar and remote forward positions. Whether coordinating with Mountaineer Stormpike or sending adventurers to report to sentries like Mountaineer Rockgar, Kadrell ensures that the isolated outposts guarding the mountain passes receive vital supplies, reinforcements, and defensive intelligence.

npc:mountaineer-stormpike.text: Mountaineer Stormpike. Mountaineer Stormpike is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan. Watching over the mountain pass leading toward the Wetlands, he works tirelessly to keep vital supply routes safe from lurking troggs and kobolds. As a proud member of the Stormpike clan, his loyalty lies squarely with Ironforge and the safety of dwarven lands. Perched along the northern border of Loch Modan, Algaz Station serves as a critical checkpoint before the perilous descent into the Wetlands. Mountaineer Stormpike is stationed here amid rocky crags and constant wilderness threats. His primary duty is maintaining the line of communication and keeping the roads open for travelers and supply convoys traversing through Dun Algaz. The northern reaches of Loch Modan are plagued by relentless pests, from kobolds infesting nearby digs to subterranean troggs. Stormpike routinely enlists passing adventurers to disrupt these threats, particularly targeting the kobolds who have moved into the Silver Stream Mine and put their filthy paws on the Miners' League's stored dwarven tools.

npc:mountaineer-thalos.text: Mountaineer Thalos. Mountaineer Thalos is a dwarven sentry stationed at the Coldridge Valley mouth of Coldridge Pass. Tasked with guarding the route, he warns travelers about the sudden trogg infestation choking the tunnel. Adventurers carrying urgent reports from the valley rely on him to point the way safely toward Kharanos. Perched on the snowy border where Coldridge Valley gives way to the deeper crags of Dun Morogh, Mountaineer Thalos serves as the first line of defense for travelers leaving the dwarven training grounds. Coldridge Pass has become a treacherous chokepoint overrun by hostile troggs who have burrowed up from the subterranean depths. Thalos stands vigil in the cold, warning the unready to turn back and assessing whether hardy couriers possess the grit to fight their way through to the wider kingdom. When Grelin Whitebeard finishes his report on the Frostmane troll movements within the secluded valley, the courier carrying it to his brother Senir in Kharanos is told to speak with Mountaineer Thalos before entering the tunnel. After verifying that an adventurer is capable of braving the infested passage, Thalos directs them onward to Kharanos, where regional commanders coordinate Dun Morogh's defense. His watchful presence ensures that vital intelligence reaches Ironforge's military leaders rather than dying in the snow.

npc:mupsi-shacklefridd.text: Mupsi Shacklefridd. Outside Ratchet in the Barrens, Mupsi Shacklefridd helps travelers repair ties with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Mupsi Shacklefridd works along the coastal road just outside Ratchet. Steamwheedle guards patrol the port town's edge as merchants come and go. Travelers on poor terms with the goblins can seek a way back into the cartel's good graces through Mupsi, if they bring the supplies and labor it demands.

npc:mux-manascrambler.text: Mux Manascrambler. Mux Manascrambler is an eccentric goblin engineer dwelling in the desert outpost of Gadgetzan. Unlike many of his peers focused strictly on explosives or mining equipment, Mux harbors a peculiar fascination with the supernatural and occult energies. Tucked away inside a building in central Gadgetzan, behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots, sits Mux Manascrambler. While the Steamwheedle Cartel trades heavily in oil, guns, and salvage, Mux focuses his ingenuity on more esoteric pursuits: the realm of spirits and supernatural anomalies. He uses his technical acumen to design bizarre devices capable of detecting, distilling, and interacting with spectral remnants, bridging crude goblin craftsmanship with the invisible worlds of the dead.

npc:mydrannul.text: Mydrannul. At the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mydrannul keeps basic supplies ready for sentinels, soldiers, and visitors. Mydrannul keeps a supply stall among the Warrior's Terrace military pavilions and training grounds. Darnassus's defenders and travelers can find everyday field gear there, including ammunition for archers and gunners, throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. His stall helps sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil find the basic sundries they need.

npc:nalpak.text: Nalpak. Nalpak is a tauren druid disciple who watches over the troubled Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. Stationed in the high cliff-cave overlooking the cavern entrance, he enlists passing adventurers to help contain the nightmare twisting the subterranean ecosystem. Perched inside a hidden cavern directly above the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak remains loyal to the vision of Naralex. While his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber deep below, Nalpak works to keep the spreading corruption at bay. He asks adventurers to gather deviate hides for use as leather.

npc:nara-meideros.text: Nara Meideros. In Stormwind's Park, Nara Meideros guides young seekers in Elune's teachings. As a night elf priestess in the human capital, she offers a familiar spiritual presence to her kin. Nara Meideros serves Elune far from Kalimdor, across the Great Sea in Stormwind City. In the Park, night elf druids and priests have tended a green refuge. Nara guides young seekers in devotion to the Moon Goddess. Human priests serve the Holy Light in nearby Cathedral Square, while Nara gives night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms a connection to their own faith.

npc:narain-soothfancy.text: Narain Soothfancy. Narain Soothfancy is an eccentric gnome dwelling in a secluded beach hut just north of Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. While he loudly advertises himself as a master soothsayer capable of divining the future, those who know him consider his psychic talents a complete farce compared to his genuine engineering genius. Perched on the eastern coast of Tanaris just north of the goblin docks, Narain Soothfancy lives as a retired engineer turned self-proclaimed master fortune teller. He routinely greets visitors by pressing unopened envelopes against his forehead or making wildly inaccurate guesses about their business, such as wondering if they have arrived seeking the legendary Ashbringer. Despite his theatrical charade, Narain possesses deep technical knowledge. Even ancient beings like the blue dragon Azuregos note that while Narain is a terrible psychic, his engineering aptitude is undeniably brilliant. A handbook titled 'Soothsaying for Dummies' rests nearby. Before settling by Steamwheedle Port, Narain suffered a catastrophic flying machine crash far to the south along Land's End Beach. He survived the wreck thanks to an unexpected rescue, though his eccentric personality and strange obsessions have kept him isolated on the desert shores, tinkering with arcane-adjacent technology and peddling dubious prophecies to anyone who passes by.

npc:nat-pagle.text: Nat Pagle. Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience. Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals. Pagle makes his camp on a small spit of land along the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, far from the bustling taverns of the Eastern Kingdoms. He remains fiercely independent and uninterested in the politics of factions, welcoming Alliance travelers sent by trainers like Grimnur Stonebrand as well as Horde aspirants directed to him by Lumak in Orgrimmar. For Nat, anyone willing to scour the corners of the world for rare specimens deserves a lesson in genuine angling. Pagle has ventured into perilous waters, including an excursion into the ruins of Zul'Gurub where he misplaced his favorite measuring tape and tackle box near the waters prowled by the monstrous hydra Gahz'ranka.

npc:natalia-mar-alith.text: Natalia Mar'alith. Mistress Natalia Mar'alith is a night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher lost deep within the silithid nests of Hive'Regal. Once part of the expedition investigating Silithus alongside her husband, Commander Mar'alith, she has succumbed completely to the maddening influence of the Old Gods. When the Cenarion Circle established their outpost at Cenarion Hold to monitor the awakening sands, Natalia accompanied her husband, Commander Mar'alith, into the wastes. Eager to unravel the mystery behind the resurgence of the silithid and the ancient Qiraji ruins, she joined an exploratory party led by the famed explorer Brann Bronzebeard, accompanied by the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

npc:nathanos-blightcaller.text: Nathanos Blightcaller. Nathanos Blightcaller, once Nathanos Marris, stands at his ruined homestead in the Eastern Plaguelands as the deadly champion of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. In life he was the first and only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, and in undeath he trains Forsaken hunters while guarding the eastern frontier with biting contempt for all who approach. Before the Third War, Nathanos Marris was an extraordinary marksman and tactical genius hailing from the rural outskirts of Lordaeron. Trained by the high elves of Quel'Thalas and close to Sylvanas Windrunner, he became the only human to ever attain the prestigious rank of Ranger Lord. His home remained the family estate in Lordaeron, the Marris Stead. When Prince Arthas and the Scourge swept through Lordaeron following the purge of Stratholme, the plague consumed the kingdom. Nathanos made a desperate stand at his estate, but fell to the monstrous abomination Ramstein the Gorger. Raised as a mindless undead thrall, he roamed the blighted fields killing in the Lich King's name. After Sylvanas shattered the Scourge's mental grip and established the Forsaken in the Undercity, she came for him, as he had somehow known she would, and tore his consciousness free from the Lich King's will, returning his tactical brilliance and fiery loyalty to her side.

npc:nida.text: Hilary. Hilary is a young human girl living in the lakeside town of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Distraught after dropping a cherished gift from her father into the lake, she spends her time crying along the town's docks. Amid the mounting threats of gnoll invasions and Blackrock orc warbands pressing down on Lakeshire, the children of the town still face everyday childhood troubles. Hilary accidentally dropped a necklace given to her by her father into the murky waters of Lake Everstill. Terrified that her father will be angry with her, the distraught girl waits by the town pier in tears, hoping someone brave enough will plunge into the lake to retrieve it.

npc:nikova-raskol.text: Nikova Raskol. In Old Town, Nikova Raskol grieves for her murdered grandson. The elderly Stormwind townswoman seeks justice against the Defias Brotherhood rioters held in the Stockade. Nikova Raskol wanders Old Town, carrying the grief of a recent loss. Her beloved grandson, Mac, was slain by Defias Brotherhood brigands. While the kingdom faces treason on a grand scale, Nikova bears the private cost of the Brotherhood's lawless rampage. Many criminals who wrecked havoc were captured and locked in the Stockade, but a violent inmate rebellion has seized the prison. The guards have failed to restore order, and Nikova turns to adventurers heading inside. She asks them to bring back red Defias bandanas as proof that her grandson's killers have faced retribution.

npc:nissa-firestone.text: Nissa Firestone. Nissa Firestone is a dwarven physician stationed above the bustle of the Great Forge in Ironforge. She serves as an instructor in field medicine, teaching travelers and soldiers how to dress wounds and bind trauma. Amid the clanging metal and blistering heat of the Great Forge, Nissa Firestone practices medicine from the upper floor of the Ironforge Physician shop. While dwarven warriors are famed for their endurance, even stone-hard skin splits against blade and claw. Nissa ensures that those heading out into the snows of Dun Morogh or beyond know how to keep themselves and their allies alive with basic bandaging and field dressings. For field medics who have mastered the basics of cloth and lint, Nissa recognizes when a student has outgrown her clinic. When practitioners reach the limits of what she can teach, she points them toward specialized triage officers in far-flung outposts, directing skilled healers to where the Alliance's casualties are heaviest.

npc:nogg.text: Nogg. Nogg is a goblin engineer operating out of a workshop in the Valley of Honor in Orgrimmar. He offers tinkering expertise and specialized craftsmanship to the Horde, notably analyzing strange mechanical salvage recovered from deep within Gnomeregan. Tucked away in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Nogg runs an independent engineering workshop catering to adventurers and craftsmen alike. While the surrounding city relies heavily on traditional orcish steel and brute strength, Nogg provides the specialized mechanical finesse that only a goblin can offer. He maintains a keen interest in foreign contraptions and tech, happily examining curious trinkets and mechanical oddities dragged back from Alliance lands or subterranean ruins. Nogg takes special interest in items recovered from the fallen gnomish capital of Gnomeregan. When Horde operatives retrieve intricate rings or technological remnants from the irradiated vaults across the sea, Nogg is one of the few minds in Durotar capable of disassembling, deciphering, and retrofitting such bizarre clockwork mechanisms for Horde use.

npc:nori-pridedrift.text: Nori Pridedrift. Nori Pridedrift is an enterprising dwarf peddling his piping-hot Scalding Mornbrew throughout snowy Coldridge Valley. He makes his living braving the cold to supply shivering mountaineers with their morning pick-me-up, often enlisting swift recruits to run deliveries while the drink remains steaming. Life in Coldridge Valley is harsh and bitterly cold, and nothing cuts through the chill quite like a draught of Scalding Mornbrew. Nori Pridedrift has carved out a living by brewing and distributing this hot, coffee-like morning drink across the frozen drifts. Because the brew must be consumed while still scalding to be fully appreciated, delivery is a race against the elements. Nori frequently recruits brisk couriers to sprint fresh draughts out to freezing sentries before the mountain air robs the brew of its heat. Just as important as the brew itself are his limited supplies of sturdy mugs, which he expects his runners to return promptly.

npc:novice-elreth.text: Novice Elreth. Novice Elreth is an undead member of the Forsaken stationed inside the chapel at Deathknell. As newly risen undead awaken into their second life, she directs them to confront the mindless Scourge haunting the nearby graves and tend to the tragic aftermath of the plague. Inside the desecrated chapel at Deathknell, Novice Elreth assists the emerging undead as they struggle to understand their horrific awakening. Rather than succumbing to despair or the mindless hunger of the Scourge, the Forsaken must organize quickly to secure their territory. Elreth provides newly freed souls with early tasks, directing them to gather paws and wings from the wolves and bats to the south and deal with the lingering remnants of Lordaeron's tragic downfall, including the sorrow of her friend Marla Fipps, slain by her own husband Samuel after he joined the mindless Scourge.

npc:oben-rageclaw.text: Oben Rageclaw. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw's spirit wanders, unable to wake or pass on. His sleeping body remains under the Gnarlpine furbolgs' control. Oben Rageclaw entered Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream, as many Druids of the Claw do. When the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, Oben lay defenseless in his trance. A corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to take control of his comatose body. His spirit was left behind as an anguished ghost, unable to wake or pass on.

npc:ogtinc.text: Ogtinc. Ogtinc is an independent furbolg hunter perched on a high ridge overlooking the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Having parted ways with his tribe to serve the balance of nature, he acts as a trusted ally and mentor for the Cenarion Circle. Skilled hunters seeking to test their craft against the fiercest beasts of Kalimdor often seek out his guidance. While most furbolg in Kalimdor remain fiercely bound to their tribes—or have succumbed to corruption following the Third War—Ogtinc chose a distinct path. Departing from his kin, he dedicated his bow and survival lore to aiding the Cenarion Circle. He makes his camp high on a bluff southeast of Timbermaw Hold, vigilantly watching over the ancient, shattered lands of Azshara. Ogtinc is renowned among seasoned trackers for his intimate understanding of Kalimdor's wilderness. He tests hunters who have honed their skills across the continents, dispatching them to gather rare trophies—such as the antlers of courser beasts, the scale of wave-thrashed sea serpents, and parts from green dragonkin. Through these trials, he teaches that true hunting honors the natural world and preserves balance rather than mindlessly taking life.

npc:ogunaro-wolfrunner.text: Ogunaro Wolfrunner. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends the Horde’s foremost wolf kennel beside the Hunter’s Hall. He breeds and trains fierce wolves for orc champions and their trusted allies. Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends Orgrimmar’s battle wolves beside the Hunter’s Hall in the Valley of Honor. Orcs and wolves have shared a bond for generations, across Draenor’s plains and Durotar’s wilderness. It rests on mutual respect, not simple domestication. Ogunaro entrusts only the hardiest beasts, from dire wolves to agile timber prowlers, to warriors who have proven their strength and worth to the warchief.

npc:old-murk-eye.text: Old Murk-Eye. Near the Westfall Lighthouse, Old Murk-Eye prowls the southern coast. His kind revere him, and sailors fear the lethal menace he poses to anyone who wanders near the lighthouse. Old Murk-Eye prowls the surf around the Westfall Lighthouse, where he is far tougher and more aggressive than the murlocs common along Westfall’s shores. His attacks have brought enough grief to local mariners that the spectral Captain Grayson seeks his death. Grayson offers a bounty for Old Murk-Eye’s pristine scales, hoping to break his hold on the shallows.

npc:orendil-broadleaf.text: Orendil Broadleaf. Orendil Broadleaf is a skilled night elf herbalist and healer stationed at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Known for his deep knowledge of forest flora, he concocts vital remedies to save young lives across the troubled woodlands. Positioned at Maestra's Post along the western threshold of Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick as a skilled healer. Recognized for his masterful knowledge of local herbs and restorative craft, Orendil relies on passing travelers to gather rare natural reagents. Even as tension and conflict encroach upon the forest, his tireless focus remains on safeguarding his kin and soothing their ailments.

npc:orenthil-whisperwind.text: Orenthil Whisperwind. Beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves of Shadowglen. Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves beneath Teldrassil’s canopy in Shadowglen. Little is known of his personal history.

npc:ormak-grimshot.text: Ormak Grimshot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Ormak Grimshot trains hunters for life in the wild. Beside his wolf, Grimfang, he teaches Horde hunters to track, shoot, and tame beasts. Ormak Grimshot trains Horde trackers and marksmen in the Hunter's Hall. With his wolf, Grimfang, at his side, he teaches the skills needed to survive Kalimdor's wilderness. Orc and troll hunters who have completed their trials in Durotar learn from him how to tame and command wild beasts, and to form a lasting bond with an animal companion.

npc:ormer-ironbraid.text: Ormer Ironbraid. Ormer Ironbraid is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at Whelgar's Excavation Site in the southern Wetlands. His team's historical research has been violently interrupted by ravenous raptors that overran the dig. Ormer seeks adventurous allies to clear out the beasts and avenge the miners driven from the site. Ormer Ironbraid arrived in the Wetlands as part of the dwarven effort to uncover Titan relics and ancient history at Whelgar's Excavation Site. Unfortunately, uncovering ancient stones also unearthed—or at least provoked—packs of fierce Wetlands raptors. Rather than cataloging ancient earthenware and tablets, Ormer spends his days watching the beasts prowl among the ruins, nursing a fierce hatred for the creatures that disrupted their work. Ormer refuses to abandon the dig, but he lacks the raw muscle to purge the site alone. He directs his frustration into a systematic campaign of extermination, enlisting passing travelers to slay raptors of increasing size and ferocity. For Ormer, reclaiming the excavation is not just about the artifacts—it is a deeply personal matter of dwarven pride and vengeance against the local wildlife.

npc:orokk-omosh.text: Orokk Omosh. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh keeps his family's smithing craft alive. The aging orc has no children to inherit it, so he seeks worthy Horde apprentices to learn the Omosh armorcraft secrets. In the Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh is the last smith of the Omosh line. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. Capable Horde blacksmiths can undertake his demanding trials of metalwork. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft. Among fellow artisans, Orokk is known for his boisterous delight in true mastery. Those who complete his craftsmanship trials often see him perform the Omosh Dance of Joy, a jubilant celebration of traditional smithing that echoes through Orgrimmar's halls.

npc:orphan-matron-battlewail.text: Orphan Matron Battlewail. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children left without families by war. With Tosamina, she gives them shelter and raises young orcs. Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children who have lost their kin to violence. In Orgrimmar, where war's toll reaches even the young capital, she and Tosamina shelter and nurture the next generation of the Horde. The orphanage in the Valley of Honor opens its doors to passing adventurers. During Children's Week, travelers are called upon to mentor the children.

npc:orphan-matron-nightingale.text: Orphan Matron Nightingale. In Cathedral Square, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s orphaned children. She and Matron Shellene give them shelter and guidance, and invite Alliance adventurers to spend Children's Week with them. Outside the orphanage, south-east of the Cathedral of Light, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s most vulnerable children. Recent wars, gnoll attacks, and the rise of the Defias Brotherhood have left many without homes or parents. Nightingale and Matron Shellene give them shelter, basic care, and guidance under the Church of the Holy Light’s watch. Matron Nightingale believes children need hope as well as food and shelter. Each Children's Week, she asks Alliance heroes to take an orphan on journeys across Azeroth. She hopes meeting celebrated champions will build their confidence, show them the wider world beyond the city walls, and remind them they are not forgotten.

npc:osric-strang.text: Osric Strang. In Stormwind's Old Town, veteran armor merchant Osric Strang supplies weary travelers and Alliance defenders with sturdy gear. His shop, Limited Immunity, specializes in heavy mail and plate armor, along with shields. Osric Strang runs Limited Immunity, where fighters find heavy armor and shields. He also helps arriving couriers who need a point of contact in the capital, including those coming from nearby settlements such as Sentinel Hill in Westfall.

npc:overlord-mok-morokk.text: Overlord Mok'Morokk. Overlord Mok'Morokk is the brute chieftain of the Stonemaul ogres, presiding over Brackenwall Village in Dustwallow Marsh. Originally appointed by Rexxar for his strength, he has become a tyrannical and cowardly ruler who refuses to defend his clan against the black dragonflight. When Rexxar bested the previous chieftain Kor'gall and led the Stonemaul clan in defense of Durotar, he left Mok'Morokk in command, seeing promise in his sheer martial strength. That faith proved misplaced. Mok'Morokk quickly succumbed to the corrupting influence of absolute authority, ruling through intimidation and self-indulgence rather than stewardship. Instead of caring for his kin, he demands unearned tribute, lounges in Brackenwall Village, and bullies anyone who questions his command.

npc:pao-ka-swiftmountain.text: Pao'ka Swiftmountain. Pao'ka Swiftmountain is a young tauren naturalist stranded among the wild wyverns of Highperch in Thousand Needles. Having traveled south under the guidance of Motega Firemane, his youthful curiosity got the better of him when he ventured too close to a nesting site and ended up cornered in the cliffs. Pao'ka came to the canyon country of Thousand Needles alongside Motega Firemane, eager to catalog and study the dangerous beasts of the canyons. His father had been reluctant to let his son go on such a perilous journey, and Pao'ka's recent misadventure proves those concerns were warranted. Fascinated by the magnificent wyverns inhabiting Highperch, the young scholar crept up the mountain trail behind a solitary tauren totem. Unsurprisingly, the territorial beasts took offense to his intrusion, driving him deep into the crags where he found himself trapped and terrified, unable to slip past the swooping predators to return to Whitereach Post.

npc:parqual-fintallas.text: Parqual Fintallas. Parqual Fintallas is a Forsaken scholar and former human historian of Lordaeron, currently residing in the Undercity's Apothecarium. Despite the grim surroundings of his undead existence, he retains a polite demeanor and an enduring passion for ancient lore, often assisting travelers sent to consult his deep historical expertise. In life, Parqual was a respected human scholar of Lordaeron who knew all there was to know of the kingdom, immersing himself in historical texts. When the plague of undeath struck, Parqual was among the many citizens slain and raised, only to eventually break free under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. While the Forsaken largely embrace cold pragmatism and turn away from their former lives, Parqual retains his scholarly passion and pleasant manners, still seeking enlightenment, though of a different nature than in life. Parqual dwells among the bubbling vats and alchemists of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Despite his macabre surroundings, he remains an invaluable font of knowledge regarding Azeroth's history. When adventurers undertake rigorous intellectual trials—such as the elusive 'Test of Lore'—they are directed to Parqual, who sends them to the Scarlet Monastery's library for a book and then puts a question of his own to them.

npc:pilot-bellowfiz.text: Pilot Bellowfiz. Pilot Bellowfiz, affectionately known as 'Fizzer,' is a dwarven driver stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh.
