Takata Steelblade was sent from the capital to Desolace under direct orders from Keldran, an influential figure in Orgrimmar committed to uncovering and purging demonic subversion. Operating out of the isolated Tauren encampment of Ghost Walker Post, Takata coordinates military efforts against the Legion-aligned forces plaguing the barren wastes. While his companion Maurin Bonesplitter attempts to track and dismantle the clandestine Burning Blade cultists directly, Takata focuses on their demonic allies: the satyrs. Takata has orchestrated aggressive strikes against Desolace's corrupted satyrs, decimating their ranks to break the cult's local power structure and halt their spreading taint.

npc:tal.text: Tal. Tal is the primary wind rider master of Thunder Bluff, tending the city's aerial roost high above the plains of Mulgore. He provides seasoned wyverns to Horde travelers looking to traverse the vast reaches of Kalimdor. Perched upon the central mesa of Thunder Bluff, Tal manages the vital aerial thoroughfare connecting the tauren capital to the rest of the Horde. From his perch, he tends to the loyal wind riders, or wyverns, ensuring they are healthy, well-fed, and prepared for long-distance journeys across Kalimdor's rugged landscapes. Whether sending messengers down to Camp Taurajo or dispatching scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar, Tal maintains an indispensable lifeline that keeps the towering mesa city in constant touch with its allies.

npc:talen.text: Talen. Talen is a night elf amateur archaeologist encamped near the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Despite the constant danger posed by nearby naga and Horde outposts, he is dedicated to recovering ancient kaldorei relics buried along the coast. Perched at a small camp on the edge of the Zoram Strand, Talen spends his days pursuing historical curiosities rather than waging war. While the wilderness of Ashenvale is fraught with territorial skirmishes and hostile shoreline denizens, Talen remains focused on gathering long-lost treasures from the ruins submerged beneath the waves and sands. He relies heavily on passing adventurers to brave the savage Wrathtail naga and retrieve elusive artifacts—including pristine statuettes and the Ring of Zoram held by the naga leader Ruuzel.

npc:tallow.text: Tallow. Tallow is a Forsaken warrior stationed in the fortified settlement of Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Serving the Dark Lady and the Horde, he watches over the contested front lines, helping organize strikes against local Alliance threats. Situated in the heart of Tarren Mill, Tallow stands among the Forsaken and Horde forces holding the line in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The region is a powder keg of conflict, caught between nearby Southshore humans, wandering Syndicate outlaws, and hostile wildlife. Tallow helps direct capable adventurers into the field, testing their strength against the Boulderfist ogres of the Arathi Highlands before sending them on to aid the besieged outpost of Hammerfall.

npc:talvash-del-kissel.text: Talvash del Kissel. Talvash del Kissel is a down-on-his-luck gnome jeweler who fled the fall of Gnomeregan and now resides in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Plagued by debt and persistent rumors following the loss of his home, he seeks capable adventurers to help recover lost treasures and restore shattered relics. His keen eye for precious gems and ancient baubles makes him a valuable contact for those plumbing the depths of Uldaman. Once a respected jeweler in the technological heart of Gnomeregan, Talvash saw his livelihood obliterated alongside his home when the troggs overran the underground city. Escaping with the surviving refugees to the dwarven capital of Ironforge, he set up camp in the Mystic Ward. Unfortunately, relocation did not treat him kindly. Rumors of questionable dealings and unpaid obligations quickly piled up, sinking the craftsman into deep financial distress. Unable to rebuild his trade through conventional means, Talvash relies on freelance adventurers to retrieve lost assets and salvage his ruined reputation. Despite his misfortunes, Talvash has lost none of his gem-cutting precision or appraisal acumen. When explorers in the Badlands uncover an ancient, shattered necklace deep within the Titan vault of Uldaman, Talvash proves to be one of the few craftsmen in the Eastern Kingdoms capable of understanding its intricate enchantments. Restoring such power requires rare components and painstaking labor, but Talvash is eager to ply his trade—both to clear his debts and to prove his enduring skill.

npc:tammra-windfield.text: Tammra Windfield. Tammra Windfield is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat, nestled within the heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Deeply attuned to the balance of the land, she guides Horde travelers in honoring the natural cycle of renewal and keeping hope alive amid the peaks. Her concerns lie with both the health of the untamed wilderness and the safety of her kin. Sun Rock Retreat serves as a vital sanctuary for the Horde within the craggy peaks of Stonetalon, surrounded by hostile harpies, Venture Company loggers, and lurking predators. Tammra Windfield stands among the settlement's caretakers, keeping a watchful eye on both the mountain wilderness and travelers who cross its threshold. Her gentle demeanor belies the resolve necessary to maintain a home in such rugged terrain. Like many of her people, Tammra honors the Earth Mother by observing the constant rhythm of growth and decay in nature. Through the tasks she entrusts to travelers—such as tending the cycle of rebirth and bringing forth new life—she works to counter the ravages that conflict and exploitation bring upon Stonetalon. To Tammra, protecting the land requires active healing, ensuring that life flourishes even in scarred mountain soil. Beyond her spiritual duties to the surrounding wild, Tammra bears deep concern for the companions and kin who brave the treacherous trails of the Stonetalon Mountains. When word spreads that travelers or family have vanished along the crags, she is among the first to seek out reliable aid. For Tammra, the endurance of Sun Rock Retreat depends as much on mutual protection and loyalty as it does on harmony with nature.

npc:tannok-frosthammer.text: Tannok Frosthammer. Tannok Frosthammer is a dwarven resident found at Thunderbrew Distillery outside Kharanos in Dun Morogh. He serves as an anxious recipient of goods coming from Coldridge Valley, deeply troubled by how trogg attacks have cut off the roads to Anvilmar. Stationed around the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer keeps a watchful eye on incoming deliveries and local tidings. The sudden surge of troggs swarming Coldridge Pass has severed normal transit from Coldridge Valley, leaving Tannok cut off from regular communication with the settlement at Anvilmar. Relying on couriers like the gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket to ferry vital supplies and news through the perilous, snowy mountain pass, Tannok represents the quiet worry shared by many Bronzebeards as subterranean threats crawl closer to their doorsteps.

npc:tarindrella.text: Tarindrella. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella watches over Teldrassil's sheltered woods. The dryad works with night elf protectors to investigate corruption among the World Tree's wildlife. Tarindrella dwells in Shadowglen, a protected glade atop Teldrassil. Dryads are fierce caretakers of nature, born of the demigod Cenarius. Many live deep in ancient Kalimdor forests such as Ashenvale, but Tarindrella watches over this young grove. She bridges the wild spirits and young night elf defenders taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil. Her chief concern is a taint creeping through the forest. She sends reliable adventurers to drive back local pests and gather clues to its source. Teldrassil is the new crown of the night elf people, yet sickness has reached its groves. Furbolgs once lived peacefully in their homes; now they have gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Grells and grellkin tainted by wicked Fel Moss infest the hills around Shadowglen. Tarindrella suspects the moss is behind these changes. She directs initiates to confront the grells and bring back samples, hoping to halt the corruption before it overtakes the young grove.

npc:tarrel-rockweaver.text: Tarrel Rockweaver. Tarrel Rockweaver is an anxious dwarven husband stationed on the bridge leading into Menethil Harbor. Deeply worried for his wife Merrin, an archaeologist who ventured inland with Whelgar's excavation team, he watches the road hoping for news of her safety. While trade and military shipments flow through Menethil Harbor, Tarrel Rockweaver keeps an anxious vigil at the bridge on the edge of town. His wife, Merrin Rockweaver, joined Prospector Whelgar's prestigious archaeological expedition deeper into the Wetlands. When violent raptors overran the excavation site and cut off regular communication, Tarrel was left stranded in town, begging passing travelers to scout east toward Whelgar's Excavation Site to ensure she survived the disaster.

npc:tatternack-steelforge.text: Tatternack Steelforge. On the Barrens frontier, Tatternack Steelforge offers work to travelers who can handle raw metal and dangerous wildlife. The orc smith studies local ores and seeks to arm Horde forces against threats across the plains. Across the Barrens, Horde outposts need weapons to face wild beasts, centaur raiders, and hostile quilboar. Tatternack Steelforge brings his people's metalworking knowledge to the frontier. He seeks practical weapons and unusual geological specimens to strengthen the Horde's foothold against those threats.

npc:tenaron-stormgrip.text: Tenaron Stormgrip. High in Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves through their people's recent history. He also asks them to gather water from a moonwell. Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves on Aldrassil's winding wooden platforms. From high in Shadowglen's central tree, he watches the local woods and their moonwells. He teaches novices about their spiritual bond with the World Tree. Tenaron sends initiates to gather a phial of water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Along the way, he teaches them what followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Their journey carries on through Teldrassil and into Darnassus.

npc:teronis-corpse.text: Teronis' Corpse. Teronis' Corpse lies on a secluded island within Lake Falathim in western Ashenvale. Before his untimely demise, this night elf scout was dispatched from Astranaar on a crucial mission to recover Dartol's Rod to aid in cleansing the forest. Sent forth by Raene Wolfrunner from the settlement of Astranaar, Teronis was tasked with recovering the lost rod of Dartol, an ancient night elf relic capable of purifying corrupted woodland magic. His search brought him deep into the waters of Lake Falathim, but the journey turned fatal when hostile murlocs swarmed the island. Teronis fell in battle, leaving his journal behind and the rod's radiant gemstone plundered by the lake's aggressive amphibians.

npc:thadius-grimshade.text: Thadius Grimshade. Thadius Grimshade is a Wildhammer dwarf diviner dwelling within the mage tower of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Though he parted ways with Aerie Peak long ago to study esoteric and darker magical arts, he remains loyal to his kin at heart. Unlike most Wildhammer dwarves who prefer the open skies and roaring winds of the Hinterlands, Thadius Grimshade makes his home inside Nethergarde Keep. Driven by a thirst for arcane divination and darker mystic lore, he relocated to the edge of the tainted Blasted Lands to pursue his esoteric studies. Despite his brooding discipline and separation from his clan, he retains a deep fondness for his homeland and gryphonkind, offering his rare scrying talents to those who come seeking aid on behalf of Aerie Peak.

npc:thalia-amberhide.text: Thalia Amberhide. Thalia Amberhide is a tauren residing at Freewind Post in the jagged canyon of Thousand Needles. A loyal friend to her kin, she waits with mounting concern for the safe return of Lakota Windsong from the clutches of the Grimtotem clan. Perched atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide is a quiet presence among the bustling tauren settlement. Her heart is heavy with worry for her close companion, Lakota Windsong, who was taken captive by Arnak Grimtotem and his treacherous kin. Thalia relies on passing Horde adventurers who brave the canyon depths to find Lakota, break her bonds, and guide her safely back up the lifts to the haven of the mesa.

npc:tharek-blackstone.text: Tharek Blackstone. Tharek Blackstone is a hardworking toolsmith residing in Kharanos, in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh. Known for supplying heavy hardware to local craftsmen, his primary patron is Beldin Steelgrill of Steelgrill's Depot. Though constantly busy at his trade, he also serves as a reliable point of contact for travelers seeking work around the settlement. Situated amidst the cold drifts of Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone keeps busy turning out reliable dwarven tools. Between repairing gear for the locals and supplying larger operations, he rarely finds a moment to rest. His biggest headache—and most reliable customer—is Beldin Steelgrill, whose mechanostrider depot just outside town demands a steady stream of heavy wrenches, gears, and replacement implements. To keep his forge running without falling behind on deliveries, Tharek often hires wandering travelers to haul newly finished tool crates over to the depot for him. Beyond his trade at the anvil, Tharek carries considerable respect among the folk of Dun Morogh. While he holds no formal military title, his standing in town makes him an approachable liaison for odd jobs, supply runs, and coordinating local efforts.

npc:tharnariun-treetender.text: Tharnariun Treetender. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches Darkshore’s wilds for signs of sickness. The night elf naturalist studies the corruption spreading through local plants and animals, seeking ways to protect them. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches the woods beyond the port. Hostile satyrs and foul shoreline washaways threaten the village, but his work centers on the natural world around it. He believes neglecting nature invites ruin, so he studies the decline of the local woods and searches for ways to fight the sickness spreading across the forest floor.

npc:the-defias-traitor.text: The Defias Traitor. At Sentinel Hill, The Defias Traitor has given up the Brotherhood's hidden base to save his life. The captured outlaw is held beneath the watchtower after the People's Militia caught him stealing Farmer Saldean's wagon.

npc:theldurin-the-lost.text: Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost is a reclusive, half-mad dwarf wandering the scorched expanses of the Badlands. Formerly aligned with the insidious Twilight's Hammer cult, he fled their ranks with stolen sacred relics after realizing the horror of their designs. Perched in the barren hills of the Badlands, clutching bags of explosives in wild paranoia, Theldurin is far more than a simple mad hermit. He was once an initiate of the Twilight's Hammer cult. When the sinister cabal sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, Theldurin recoiled in terror, rejected their mad teachings, and fled into the desert. He carried with him the Scroll of Myzrael, desperate to prevent his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. Though the escape cost him his sanity, his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

npc:therylune.text: Therylune. Therylune is a dryad found held captive at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Entrapped by the insidious Twilight's Hammer cultists who have occupied the ancient site, she relies on bold travelers to help her break free and escape their clutches. Dryads are guardians of nature and daughters of Cenarius, normally roaming the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor. However, Therylune ventured too close to the ominous excavation at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, where Twilight's Hammer cultists have gathered. Ambushed and trapped by the dark cult, she is unable to fight her way out alone through the swarms of cultists and requires an escort to flee to safety.

npc:therysil.text: Therysil. Therysil is a dryad dwelling at the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale. Deeply devoted to the preservation of nature, she waits anxiously for word of her sister, Therylune, who fell into the hands of sinister cultists. Therysil makes her home near the tranquil waters of the Shrine of Aessina, a sacred glade within the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Like all dryads, the daughters of Cenarius, she is bound to the defense of the wild and the spirits dwelling within it. Yet her focus has been torn from quiet stewardship to gnawing worry. Her sister, Therylune, was captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult, leaving Therysil desperate for any wandering ally willing to aid in her sister's rescue.

npc:thor.text: Thor. At Sentinel Hill, Thor keeps Westfall linked to Stormwind by gryphon flight. His trained mounts carry travelers and urgent messages above the dangerous roads. Thor tends the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill, linking Westfall's defenders with the rest of the kingdom. The People's Militia faces bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems on the ground. Thor's gryphons carry travelers and military dispatches above the perilous roads. Reports from Gryan Stoutmantle and urgent requests for aid can reach the court in Stormwind far faster than a ground messenger.

npc:thorgas-grimson.text: Thorgas Grimson. Thorgas Grimson is the resident dwarf hunter trainer stationed inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A seasoned outdoorsman of Dun Morogh, he firmly believes that hands-on survival in the freezing wilds is the finest teacher any fledgling marksman can have. Perched inside the stone halls of Anvilmar, Thorgas Grimson welcomes novice mountaineers and scouts taking their very first steps into the harsh snowdrifts of Coldridge Valley. Rather than bogging young hunters down with dry lectures, Grimson espouses a practical philosophy: real skill is forged out in the freezing winds, bow or gun in hand, tracking Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

npc:thorgrum-borrelson.text: Thorgrum Borrelson. Thorgrum Borrelson is the dwarven gryphon master stationed above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. From his roost overlooking the settlement, he tends the aerial mounts that connect the valley to Ironforge and the surrounding mountain passes. Perched on the bluff rising immediately above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson handles aerial transport for the Alliance across Loch Modan. With trogg incursions and gnoll packs threatening overland paths, his trained gryphons provide vital transit over the jagged ridges. He maintains frequent connections back through the South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, as well as routes onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

npc:thorvald-deepforge.text: Thorvald Deepforge. Thorvald Deepforge is a dwarven weapon merchant stationed near the border pass in the Valley of Kings. He helps arm travelers and defenders securing the critical pathway between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Positioned within the towering monument of the Valley of Kings, Thorvald Deepforge serves the Alliance as a reliable arms dealer. The mountain passes connecting Khaz Modan's interior to the outlying territories are plagued by trogg incursions and roving wildlife, making well-forged steel essential for any Mountaineer or recruit on the road. Thorvald ensures that those arriving from Dun Morogh or heading deeper into Loch Modan carry the blades and axes needed to defend dwarven lands.

npc:thran-khorman.text: Thran Khorman. Thran Khorman is the resident dwarven warrior trainer stationed in Anvilmar, nestled within the snowy Coldridge Valley. He oversees the basic combat drilling for newly minted warriors stepping out into Dun Morogh. Standing near the training grounds of Anvilmar, Thran Khorman is tasked with turning raw dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes into disciplined combatants. He maintains a gruff, uncompromising demeanor toward anyone who lacks the grit for front-line fighting. In his eyes, even though the Third War has concluded, peace is merely an illusion: troggs encroach upon Coldridge Pass, and the mountains remain fraught with peril. He demands relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield so that Ironforge's defenders never grow dull.

npc:thunderaan.text: Thunderaan. Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Adventurers who recover these relics can seek out Highlord Demitrian in Silithus to unleash him once more. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. The Prince was ambushed and betrayed by Ragnaros's powerful lieutenants, Baron Geddon and Garr, before being struck down by the Firelord's hammer, Sulfuras. Although defeated, Thunderaan's essence proved too mighty for Ragnaros to fully absorb. Unable to entirely devour the Prince of Air, Ragnaros sealed what little remained of Thunderaan's essence inside a talisman of elemental binding. To prevent the Prince from ever reforming, the Firelord shattered the talisman into two flawless halves. He entrusted one piece to Baron Geddon and the other to Garr, hiding both within the volcanic depths of the Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.

npc:tommy-joe-stonefield.text: Tommy Joe Stonefield. At the river west of Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield longs for Maybell Maclure. Their families have feuded for years, so he relies on secret notes and quiet banks to keep their love hidden. Tommy Joe Stonefield waits by the river west of Stonefield Farm, looking toward the Maclure homestead across the water. The Stonefields and Maclures have clashed for years over land, pride, and farmyard squabbles. Their elders keep the feud alive, but Tommy Joe has fallen in love with Maybell Maclure. The two cannot meet openly without angering both households. Gramma Stonefield, Tommy Joe’s sympathetic grandmother, helps them exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

npc:tormus-deepforge.text: Tormus Deepforge. Tormus Deepforge is a dwarven smith working at the center of the Great Forge in Ironforge. A dependable craftsman, he coordinates iron deliveries and supplies armaments for Alliance defense efforts across Khaz Modan and beyond. Positioned right beside the roaring fires of the Great Forge, Tormus Deepforge oversees substantial metalworking tasks on behalf of the Bronzebeard clan. Beyond hammering steel himself, Tormus mourns his mentor, Sturgy Ironband, whose smithing compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh was overrun by Dark Iron dwarves after a load of strange umbral ore arrived there.

npc:torwa-pathfinder.text: Torwa Pathfinder. Torwa Pathfinder is a lone tauren hunter and tracker camped at the entrance to Un'Goro Crater, just below the ramp descending from Tanaris. He observes the basin's primordial wildlife, studying the dangerous predators that rule the jungle floor. Adventurers seeking to test their mettle against the crater's legendary beasts often seek his guidance. Perched at the eastern base of the crater where the desert sands of Tanaris give way to humid jungle steam, Torwa Pathfinder serves as an informal warden for newcomers. He respects the wild forces of Un'Goro, understanding that careless wanderers quickly become fodder for the local fauna. His campsite provides a rare moment of respite before travelers dive into the sweltering depths. Much of Torwa's attention is consumed by Lar'korwi, a notoriously cunning and fierce raptor roaming the northern reaches of the crater. Torwa understands that brute strength alone cannot bring down such an apex predator. Instead, he instructs hunters to study its feeding habits, using fresh carcase meat and glands to craft a bait potent enough to lure the beast out into the open. Beyond hunting the crater's apex raptors, Torwa maintains a deep curiosity regarding the toxic flora and aggressive ape colonies that inhabit the basin. He directs travelers to harvest venom from volatile bloodpetals and observe the strength of dominant beasts like the mighty gorilla U'cha, constantly analyzing how nature's deadliest adaptations function in isolation.

npc:treshala-fallowbrook.text: Treshala Fallowbrook. Treshala Fallowbrook is a night elf residing quietly on the upper level of the Tradesmen's Terrace in Darnassus. She is the wife of Heralath Fallowbrook, whose work has taken him far from home into the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. Treshala Fallowbrook keeps a modest vigil on the second floor of a workshop in Darnassus's Tradesmen's Terrace. Her husband, Heralath, journeyed to the brambled depths of Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens, and she waits at home for word of him. The two are joined by a pendant of bonding, a keepsake of their marriage that Heralath carried with him into the quilboar's warrens.

npc:tsunaman.text: Tsunaman. Tsunaman is a sentient water elemental stationed at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Acting as an agent of the Tribunal of the Tides, he watches over the elemental currents of Kalimdor and rallies Horde adventurers to confront corrupting forces. Dwelling near the path leading from Sun Rock Retreat down into the Charred Vale, Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides, high-ranking servants aligned with the Tidehunter, Neptulon. Rather than showing mindless hostility to mortal travelers, he cooperates with the Horde to monitor elemental unrest throughout Kalimdor, particularly the disturbances rippling out of the submerged caverns of Blackfathom Deeps. True to his elemental nature, Tsunaman harbors an instinctive, visceral hatred for fire in all forms. He constantly fumes over the nearby burning landscapes of the Charred Vale and elemental fire incursions. In camp, his animosity is so petty and unyielding that he regularly marches over to nearby cooking fires and campfires just to smack them out with a heavy fist of water.

npc:tyrion.text: Tyrion. Inside Stormwind Keep, Tyrion watches the court and aids covert work. The gnome works with Elling Trias to gather intelligence and counter plots against the kingdom. Tyrion keeps to the halls of Stormwind Keep, watching the palace and staying in touch with contacts beyond official oversight. Elling Trias, a cheese merchant in the Trade District, trusts Tyrion with sensitive matters. Trias runs a discreet information network and sends reliable operatives to Tyrion when the House of Nobles' bureaucracy must be bypassed.

npc:ukor.text: Ukor. Near the eastern path outside the Valley of Trials, Ukor rests after carrying supplies from Razor Hill. The training grounds already had plenty, and he hopes the provisions can still help his people. Ukor rests by the eastern road outside the Valley of Trials, tired from carrying food south from Razor Hill. Orc peons often spend their days cutting lumber or hauling rocks under harsh taskmasters. Ukor chose to bring provisions to the recruits on his own initiative. He crossed Durotar's red plains, where scorpids and boars prowl, only to find the training grounds already well-stocked. His bundle was not needed. Now he asks passing young adventurers to carry the provisions back north to Innkeeper Grosk.

npc:ula-elek.text: Ula'elek. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek works armor for warriors across the Horde. The Darkspear smith joins forces with Thun'grim Firegaze, shaping specialized gear from traditional troll craft and trophies gathered across Kalimdor. Ula'elek is a skilled armorsmith serving the Darkspear in Sen'jin Village. Nearby quilboar and sea crawlers threaten the coastal settlement, so the tribe needs sturdy armor and working blades. Ula'elek's skill also draws seasoned warriors from across the Horde. Young warriors who visit Thun'grim Firegaze at his overlook in the Barrens are sent south to Sen'jin Village. The veteran trusts Ula'elek to forge Brutal Gauntlets for battle-hardened fighters. To make them, Ula'elek calls for rare materials, especially swollen, uncloven hooves from the satyrs draining the forest's magic in northeastern Ashenvale.

npc:umpi.text: Umpi. Umpi is a frog residing in Tarren Mill as the unwitting laboratory assistant of Apothecary Lydon. Kept inside the Royal Apothecary Society's workshop, she serves as a recurring test subject for experimental toxins and plague concoctions. Within the dark laboratories of Tarren Mill, the Forsaken work tirelessly to brew concoctions of death and torment. For Apothecary Lydon, scientific rigor requires living flesh to test his formulas, and Umpi bears the brunt of these trials. Lydon regularly tests lethal brews—such as the Elixir of Suffering and the Elixir of Agony—directly on her. Once the poisons take their inevitable toll and kill her, the apothecary re-animates the amphibian, ensuring she is ready to endure the next lethal dose for the glory of the Royal Apothecary Society.

npc:undertaker-mordo.text: Undertaker Mordo. Undertaker Mordo is the caretaker of the crypt of Deathknell, serving as the very first face newly awakened Forsaken see when they open their eyes. He tells those who wake that they are the Lich King's slaves no more and sends them on toward the Forsaken cause; the bodies that never stir go to the fire. Keeping the crypt of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades, Undertaker Mordo watches over the dead as corpses break free from the Scourge's shattered grip. For every newly liberated Forsaken who wakes in the cold of the crypt, Mordo provides their initial bearing in an unrecognizable second life. He assesses their sanity, introduces them to the reality of their condition, and immediately directs them toward duty under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. Not every body brought to the crypt wakes. Mordo does not wait long: the corpses that stay still are tossed into the fire, and those who do stir are greeted with dry impatience and little ceremony. Anyone who rises with their wits intact is sent up the steps and down the road to Shadow Priest Sarvis in the chapel, who explains their new existence. The mindless zombies that overrun the north of the village are Sarvis's concern, not Mordo's; the shadow priest sends the newly risen out to destroy them.

npc:ur-kyo.text: Ur'kyo. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo guides priests in the ways of shadow and light. The Darkspear regard him as their spiritual leader and greatest priest, and he teaches their traditions in the Horde capital. Ur'kyo guides Darkspear mystics and visiting practitioners from the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. After fleeing the Echo Isles, the Darkspear made a home in Durotar alongside Thrall's Horde. Their sacred traditions remain vital to the tribe, and Ur'kyo keeps those ancestral practices alive through his teaching. Priests who come to Ur'kyo find a patient instructor in faith and old rites. He teaches the Hex of Weakness and the defensive ward called Shadowguard. Horde priests also turn to him to learn about the coalition's varied spiritual ways, from troll voodoo and ancestral customs to foreign disciplines.

npc:uzzek.text: Uzzek. Uzzek watches the eastern Barrens from southwest of Far Watch Post. The battle-hardened orc survived many skirmishes across Kalimdor and now tests and trains promising Horde warriors crossing the plains. Uzzek trains young warriors southwest of Far Watch Post, near the eastern edge of the Barrens. He endured brutal combat in the recent wars and now tests those learning to defend themselves. To prove their skill, they face the savage wildlife and raiders that trouble the crossing.

npc:valstag-ironjaw.text: Valstag Ironjaw. Valstag Ironjaw is an Ironforge dwarven soldier stationed within Menethil Keep in the coastal marshlands of the Wetlands. Facing the pressing dangers that plague the trade passages connecting Loch Modan and the coast, he assists in securing regional routes and keeping the harbor's garrison informed of local threats. Found inside Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor, Valstag Ironjaw serves as part of the dwarven garrison keeping watch over the lowlands. The surrounding marsh is rife with danger, from hostile Dragonmaw orcs to ravenous wildlife, making communications and supply lines difficult to maintain. Valstag helps coordinate defense efforts along the primary thoroughfares, particularly the treacherous passage cutting through Dun Algaz toward Loch Modan. With the treacherous Algaz Gauntlet choked by hostile forces, travelers and supply convoys heading between Menethil Harbor and Loch Modan are under constant threat. Valstag directs capable adventurers to confront the brigands and orcs lurking in the passes, relaying crucial military intelligence back and forth between forward scouts and commanders like Captain Stoutfist.

npc:vanndar-stormpike.text: Vanndar Stormpike. Vanndar Stormpike is a fierce dwarf mountain king who commands the Stormpike Expedition from the northern fortress of Dun Baldar. Searching the frozen peaks of Alterac Valley for ancient relics and raw resources, he leads the Alliance's unyielding war against the Frostwolf orcs. A veteran mountain king of Ironforge, Vanndar Stormpike spearheads the dwarven excavation into Alterac Valley. Following the Third War, he marched the Stormpike Guard into the northern mountains seeking hidden mineral riches and long-lost titan artifacts. Settling into the fortified redoubt of Dun Baldar, Vanndar views the valley as an ancestral right and rightful Alliance territory. He directs military outposts, defensive bunkers, and frontline pushes with grim dwarven resolve, determined that no retreat will ever be sounded under his watch. Vanndar's relentless mining and prospecting encroached directly onto the home of the Frostwolf clan, sparking brutal mountain warfare. Despite orcish demands to withdraw, Vanndar refuses to yield an inch of ground, vowing that Alterac Valley will belong to the dwarves. From his throne room deep within Dun Baldar, flanked by his marshals and bodyguards, he personally oversees the defense against Frostwolf incursions while dispatching Alliance champions to break the enemy lines and claim the valley once and for all.

npc:varok-saurfang.text: Varok Saurfang. High Overlord Saurfang is a legendary orc warrior and a veteran of the Old Horde's wars. Serving as Warchief Thrall's trusted military commander in Orgrimmar, he represents the proud martial spine of the modern Horde. Few living warriors possess a martial pedigree to rival Saurfang. A veteran of the Old Horde's wars, he is considered an unstoppable force on the battlefield. Today he stands in Orgrimmar as High Overlord, a bulwark of Thrall's newborn Horde. Though he stands as an unmatched champion of the Horde, Saurfang is not driven by reckless battle-lust. While he will relentlessly defend the Horde and enforce Thrall's rule against any threat, Saurfang harbors a profound disdain for warmongering and fights strictly for honor and preservation.

npc:velarok.text: Velarok. Velarok Windblade is a lone human swordsman camped amid the ash and cinder of Searing Gorge, flanked by the mutilated corpses of Dark Iron dwarves. He seeks vengeance against the local Dark Irons for the brutal murder of his father, recruiting passing travelers to forge a weapon of retribution. His single-minded hunger for vengeance drives everything he asks of those who help him. Found southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade presents himself as a grieving human warrior stranded in the perilous wastes of the Searing Gorge. Surrounding his camp are the bloody, battered corpses of Dark Iron dwarves who crossed his blade. According to Velarok, these clan dwarves slaughtered his father in cold blood. Consumed by hatred, he enlists travelers to gather materials to assemble the Torch of Retribution, an enchanted weapon of vengeance against the Dark Irons and the minions of Ragnaros.

npc:velora-nitely.text: Velora Nitely. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Velora Nitely works the forge for the Forsaken and the Horde. Once among Lordaeron's finest armorsmiths, she now makes dry jokes that rarely land. Velora Nitely works near the anvils in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where she makes armor for the Horde. Before the Third War devastated the north, Lordaeron celebrated her as an exceptional armorsmith. Undeath took her life and warmth, but left her technical skill untouched. She works with Horde crafters across continents, including Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens. Her craft includes reinforcing heavy battle plate and forging the formidable Brutal Legguards from hardened materials such as Dragonmaw shinbones. Velora Nitely keeps trying to make jokes at the forge, though her humor rarely lands. Many of her somber Forsaken kin brood over their cursed fate, but she still makes room for levity. Death seems to have ruined her comedic timing: her quips sound flat, morbid, and thoroughly unfunny to the living and the dead alike. She keeps cracking them undeterred.

npc:ventaari-brightwish.text: Ventaari Brightwish. Ventaari Brightwish is a Skyborne resident of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. She greets travelers from across Azeroth and offers the quest The Gift of Skysight. Residing in Thendal Village upon the soaring cliffs of Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish is one of the local Skyborne. While she shares a surname with Belathaan Brightwish, her own duties center around aiding newcomers who find their way to the village, extending hospitality to both the Alliance and the Horde as she initiates visitors into the traditions of her people through tasks like The Gift of Skysight.

npc:verna-furlbrow.text: Verna Furlbrow. Verna Furlbrow waits beside her broken wagon near Westfall’s northern border. Bandits drove her from her family’s pumpkin patch, and the road to Elwynn Forest has left her stranded. Verna and her husband farmed pumpkins in northern Westfall until lawlessness drove them from their land. After outlaws took the farm, they loaded what they could onto their cart and set out for Elwynn Forest with their horse, Old Blanchy. Their wagon broke down just down the road from the abandoned Jansen Stead. Unable to repair the axle or continue, Verna now faces the elements, bandit raids, and scavengers. She depends on travelers to keep her household fed and guarded. Verna still welcomes those who have been driven to the roadside. Known for creating Westfall Stew, she shares meals and warm fires with wandering transients and refugees who have suffered similar fates. To fill her cooking pot, she needs ingredients gathered from the fields, including boar snouts, murloc eyes, okra, and stringy vulture meat. She makes hearty meals for the destitute from what the harsh frontier provides.

npc:veron-amberstill.text: Veron Amberstill. Veron Amberstill is a dwarven ram breeder residing at Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh. He tends to the rugged mountain rams that serve as the traditional mounts of Ironforge and offers them to skilled riders who have earned his trust. Tucked away in the snow-dusted hills of eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill oversees the celebrated stock of Amberstill Ranch. Mountain rams are perfectly suited for Khaz Modan's treacherous slopes, sure-footed and thick-coated against the bite of mountain blizzards. Veron breeds and trains these beasts to carry dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. While he gladly provides standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves, outsiders must prove their unwavering loyalty to the throne of Ironforge before he will part with any of his prized herd.

npc:veronica-nials.text: Veronica Nials. Captain Veronica Nials is an officer of the Stromgarde military stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Amid the kingdom's collapse, she coordinates defensive operations against the Syndicate and ogres that overrun the fallen capital. Following the Third War, the human kingdom of Stromgarde shattered, leaving its remnants struggling to survive against invading Boulderfist ogres and the treachery of the Syndicate. Captain Veronica Nials stands as one of the central commanders of the surviving Stromgarde defenders at Refuge Pointe. Tasked with holding the line, she directs Alliance champions against key Syndicate leadership, such as Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl, while striving to recover fallen soldiers' badges so their grieving families can find closure. Captain Nials's loyalties are strictly tied to her battered homeland. When Rhag Garmason and the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr begged for Stromgarde's assistance after Dark Iron saboteurs devastated the Thandol Span, Nials was forced to turn them away. Bound by honor and duty, her troops cannot spare a single blade beyond the Arathi Highlands while their own ancestral kingdom remains occupied.

npc:vesprystus.text: Vesprystus. At Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus sends travelers between Teldrassil and mainland Kalimdor. He tends the hippogryph roost at the great World Tree's base. At Teldrassil's southern base, Vesprystus tends the Rut'theran roost. Trained hippogryphs carry travelers from the isolated elven boughs toward Darkshore and the mainland. A magical portal also links Rut'theran to Darnassus in the canopy above. Across the strait, Vesprystus works with the flight master at Auberdine to carry sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers into Kalimdor.

npc:vidra-hearthstove.text: Vidra Hearthstove. Vidra Hearthstove is a dwarven cook residing in the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Known for preparing local specialties, she frequently relies on traveling adventurers to gather regional ingredients for her famous blood sausages. Within the bustling warmth of the Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove tends the kitchen and helps feed the locals and travelers passing through Loch Modan. Sharing a surname with the innkeeper, she keeps Thelsamar well-provisioned. Her signature dish, Thelsamar blood sausages, is a hearty dwarven staple that requires fresh game meats gathered from the surrounding wilderness, including boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

npc:volcor.text: Volcor. Volcor lies wounded in Blackwood Den, deep in southern Darkshore. The night elf scout depends on his bear Grimclaw and Auberdine's defenders to escape the hostile furbolgs. Volcor is a night elf scout wounded inside Blackwood Den. While tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe through its underground lair, he was ambushed and badly hurt. He could not fight past the hostile furbolgs alone, so he sent Grimclaw, his loyal bear companion, into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help in Auberdine.

npc:vorn-skyseer.text: Vorn Skyseer. Vorn Skyseer is a peaceful tauren resident of Camp Narache atop Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. Resting among the camp's tents, he greets young adventurers beginning their journeys and introduces them to local life. Situated in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Vorn Skyseer serves as an informal welcoming presence for young tauren. As they undertake their rites of passage before venturing into the wider valleys of Mulgore, Vorn offers kind words and hospitality, helping new arrivals settle into the camp. Vorn is no warrior. He leaves the camp's defense to its braves and keeps to a quiet, unhurried life, content to watch over the tranquil plains of his homeland.

npc:warcaller-gorlach.text: Warcaller Gorlach. Warcaller Gorlach patrols Orgrimmar, calling Horde champions to distant battlefronts. He rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands at outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Warcaller Gorlach walks Orgrimmar's thoroughfares, carrying the Horde's calls for expansion and defense. He gives orders among the city's people, seeking volunteers ready to test their mettle. Some he sends to the contested canopy of Ashenvale. Others he directs toward Camp Mojache in Feralas, where scouts face the wilderness. He also calls warriors to distant campaigns in the Plaguelands. As threats rise abroad, Gorlach calls on those in the capital to take up arms.

npc:warlord-goretooth.text: Warlord Goretooth. Warlord Goretooth is the commanding orc officer stationed at Kargath in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. From his watchtower, he coordinates the Horde's frontier campaigns against the neighboring Dark Iron dwarves and monitors the volcanic menace of Blackrock Mountain. Though strict in military matters, he can occasionally be found relaxing around the camp's bonfire. Perched atop the watchtower of Kargath, Warlord Lunk Goretooth directs Horde operations on the hostile eastern frontier. Kargath serves as Orgrimmar's primary staging ground against the threats lurking within Blackrock Mountain and the surrounding ravines. Goretooth oversees patrols, coordinates scout forces like the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and issues direct kill orders targeting the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leadership. When he descends from his lookout, the stern commander shows a lighter side, frequently warming himself by the camp bonfire and trading quips with the camp's Forsaken casters before returning to duty. Goretooth views the Dark Iron dwarves as a clear and present threat to Horde interests in the Eastern Kingdoms. Rather than engaging in defensive posturing, he pursues aggressive war plans against General Angerforge and Emperor Dagran Thaurissan's forces entrenched within Blackrock Depths. Recognizing the gravity of assaulting such an ancient subterranean stronghold, he frequently defers strategic matters to veteran orcs like Eitrigg in Orgrimmar, seeking seasoned wisdom before sanctioning further pushes into the mountain.

npc:warmaster-laggrond.text: Warmaster Laggrond. Warmaster Laggrond is a seasoned orc commander stationed outside the Horde entrance to Alterac Valley in the Alterac Mountains. He oversees recruitment and frontline recognition for warriors answering the call to aid the Frostwolf clan. Through his trials, fighters prove their mettle and earn the respect of the Horde vanguard. Standing watch in the bitter cold at the threshold of Alterac Valley, Warmaster Laggrond organizes the Horde's war effort against the Stormpike Expedition. He ensures that only capable fighters enter the valley to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde. Laggrond tests arriving combatants through the Proving Grounds before directing them into the thick of battle. As warriors spill blood across the frozen peaks, it is Laggrond who measures their standing, bestowing honors upon those who earn renown among the Frostwolves.

npc:warsong-outrider.text: Warsong Outrider. Stationed along the contested road leading east from Ashenvale into Azshara, the Warsong Outrider keeps watch over the Horde's frontier. She serves as an advanced scout for the Warsong clan, monitoring travelers and relaying crucial intelligence back to their forward encampments. Although armed and vigilant against night elf incursions, she maintains a passive watch unless directly provoked. The borderlands between Ashenvale and the shattered ruins of Azshara are fraught with danger. Operating far from the fortified safety of Splintertree Post or the lumber camps, the Warsong Outrider observes troop movements and patrols the transit corridor. Armed with a bow and toxic stingers, she stands ready to defend the Horde's claim over the region, though she conserves her strength by only firing upon Alliance trespassers who actively attack her.

npc:watch-captain-parker.text: Watch Captain Parker. Guard Parker is a vigilant town guardsman stationed at the Three Corners outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with patrolling the roads and monitoring aggressive gnoll packs, he serves as an early line of defense for travelers heading into Lakeshire. Positioned at the vital junction known as Three Corners, Parker keeps watch over the roads connecting Elwynn Forest, Duskwood, and Redridge. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and little official reinforcement reaching the region, solo watchmen like Parker carry the burden of keeping the crossroads clear of bandits, prowling predators, and raiding gnolls. Parker's immediate concern is the gnoll encampments gathering to the north and east of his post. As packs encroach closer toward the roadway, he sends able-bodied travelers to carry word of the gathering gnoll force to Deputy Feldon in Lakeshire. The Redridge pack's growing boldness poses an immediate danger to supply convoys and refugees seeking shelter in Lakeshire. Life on a lonely roadside post can be grim, but small kindnesses still find their way to Three Corners. Darcy, the server from the Lakeshire Inn, sends Parker a warm lunch while he is out on patrol. Touched by the gesture, Parker asks the adventurer who delivered it to fetch a bouquet from Lakeshire's herbalist and bring it back to her as a token of his appreciation, without telling the herbalist whom the flowers are from or for.

npc:watcher-backus.text: Watcher Backus. Along Duskwood's road, Watcher Backus keeps watch for danger and suspicious traffic tied to Stormwind's political intrigues. He patrols between Darkshire and Manor Mistmantle, watching for undead and strange travelers. Watcher Backus walks a solitary beat north of Darkshire, passing near Manor Mistmantle. Like the rest of the Night Watch, he struggles against Duskwood's curse. Stormwind's garrison gives the region little support, so local volunteers guard its misty paths on their own. Backus keeps beast and ghoul at bay along the road.

npc:watcher-dodds.text: Watcher Dodds. Watcher Dodds is a human scout of the Night Watch stationed at the central crossroads of Duskwood. Manning a lonely roadside outpost far from Darkshire's town walls, he monitors the encroaching horrors and tasks travelers with culling the local giant spider population. Watcher Dodds serves the Night Watch under Commander Althea Ebonlocke, holding down an exposed post at the intersection connecting Darkshire to Raven Hill and Deadwind Pass. While Darkshire huddles within its palisades, forward sentries like Dodds live on the knife's edge between wolf packs, ravenous ghouls, and oversized arachnids. From his roadside camp, he keeps an eye on approaching threats and enlists wandering mercenaries to thin out the spiders crawling out from the undergrowth before they completely overrun the overgrown thoroughfares.

npc:wilder-thistlenettle.text: Wilder Thistlenettle. Wilder Thistlenettle is a dwarven miner brooding in a tavern within Stormwind's Dwarven District. The sole survivor of a tragic cave-in deep within the Deadmines, he is haunted by the gruesome fate of his mining company and his brother. Wilder Thistlenettle can be found drowning his sorrows in an alehouse near the southeastern gates of the Dwarven District. Years ago, he joined an expedition into the deep lodes of Moonbrook's Deadmines alongside his brother and their companions. A catastrophic cave-in sealed the rest of the crew in the dark while Wilder barely made it to the surface alive.

npc:wiley-the-black.text: Wiley the Black. At the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black keeps out of sight. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle and shares what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood. Wiley the Black keeps to the Lakeshire Inn, away from Westfall's turmoil and Redridge's gnoll-infested borders. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia, who once saved him. Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let Wiley rot. When the militia needs insight into the Defias conspiracy, it turns to Wiley. He reluctantly shares covert intelligence to repay his debt.

npc:willem.text: Willem. Outside Northshire Abbey, Willem sends recruits to meet the valley's threats. He serves under Marshal McBride in the Stormwind Army, with the Defias Brotherhood pressing into Northshire. Deputy Willem watches the gates of Northshire Abbey, where the Stormwind Army keeps a foothold in the valley. The kingdom's soldiers are spread across many territories, leaving local defense to small groups like Marshal McBride's garrison. Willem meets incoming volunteers and sends them to aid residents and guard the valley's edges. The Defias Brotherhood is Willem's most pressing concern. Red-bandana bandits have entered Northshire, stolen supplies, threatened farmer Milly Osworth, and taken footholds among nearby vineyards and hills. Willem offers bounties on known cutthroats such as Garrick Padfoot, hoping to break their leadership before they can take the abbey grounds.

npc:williden-marshal.text: Williden Marshal. Williden Marshal is the ambitious human leader of Marshal's Expedition, based out of Marshal's Refuge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Driven by the lure of rare flora, mysterious crystals, and profitable scientific research, he brought his team into the crater only to watch their lower camps overrun by the basin's colossal beasts. Williden Marshal brought an entire scientific expedition deep into Un'Goro Crater seeking fortune and discovery. Intrigued by accounts of alien crystals, uncataloged plants, and untapped resources, he established multiple forward camps across the valley floor. However, the primeval wilderness quickly turned against them. The savage beasts of the crater dismantled their research posts, forcing Williden and his survivors to retreat up into the northern cliffs to establish Marshal's Refuge. Despite being driven to the crater's mountainous edge, Williden refuses to pack up and abandon his investment. From the relative safety of the refuge, he hires passing adventurers to delve back into the savage lowlands to recover lost food crates, expensive scientific instruments, and his personal expedition journal. Though often known simply as 'Wil' to close comrades like Spark Nilminer, he takes the venture seriously—insisting on recovering their work even as titanic predators stalk the valley beneath them. Williden is not the only Marshal in the crater: Hol'anyee Marshal shares his name and works alongside him at Marshal's Refuge. Together they chose the untamed primeval crater of southern Kalimdor, and Williden remains entirely convinced that Un'Goro's crystal deposits and ancient mysteries hold the true fortune.

npc:winna-hazzard.text: Winna Hazzard. Winna Hazzard is an eccentric Forsaken researcher stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. Accompanied by a feline companion and known for bouts of maniacal laughter, she studies the blighted ecosystem and conducts unsettling experiments with the zone's corrupted fauna. Winna Hazzard represents the Forsaken interest in Felwood's unnatural decay. Stationed in the Horde enclave of Bloodvenom Post, she spends her time observing the local wildlife and formulating experiments utilizing tainted waters and venomous samples. Her jovial, manic demeanor often masks callous motives, evident when she uses tainted liquids drawn from the land to corrupt the small kitten that stays by her side.

npc:winstone-wolfe.text: Winstone Wolfe. Winstone Wolfe is a human operative affiliated with the secretive Ravenholdt organization, stationed at their secluded estate nestled between Hillsbrad and the Alterac Mountains. He keeps watch over the estate's grounds and groundskeepers, serving as one of the trusted contacts within the hidden league of thieves and assassins. Tucked away in the hidden valley of Ravenholdt Manor, Winstone Wolfe operates among the ranks of Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's syndicate. Quiet, watchful, and practical, Wolfe is one of the capable hands who handles business around the manor, ensuring that only those with proper discretion and talent walk the grounds undisturbed.

npc:witch-doctor-jin-zil.text: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil is a Darkspear troll mystic dwelling in a cave at Malaka'jin in the southern Stonetalon Mountains. A longtime comrade of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan, he turns dark voodoo and ritual sorcery against the Horde's local enemies. Secluded inside an eastern cavern above the camp of Malaka'jin, Jin'Zil practices ancient jungle troll arts away from the coastal home of his tribe. Surrounded by bubbling cauldrons and captive prisoners, he gathers exotic reagents from the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains to weave potent blessings and curses in defense of the Horde's mountain encampment. Jin'Zil is no ordinary hedge wizard; he shares a storied history with senior Horde scouts, counting both Darsok Swiftdagger and the renowned shadow hunter Rokhan among his old friends. While Darsok coordinates frontline skirmishes against night elves and harpies, Jin'Zil fights the war spiritually and alchemically, using his forest magic and volatile voodoo to undermine threats before they ever reach the camp gates.

npc:witch-doctor-uzer-i.text: Witch Doctor Uzer'i. Witch Doctor Uzer'i is a jungle troll mystic residing at Camp Mojache in the primordial forests of Feralas. Dedicated to advancing the magical capabilities of the Horde, he researches techniques to trap and harness the muisek—the spiritual essence of powerful natural creatures. By capturing these ancient forest spirits, Uzer'i seeks to channel the raw primal energies traditionally favored by night elves directly into enchanted weapons. Rooted in traditional troll spiritualism, Witch Doctor Uzer'i has spent considerable effort studying the natural magic inherent to the untamed wilderness of Feralas. He argues that night elves have drawn upon the spirits of forest beasts for millennia, and believes the time has come for the Horde to seize those same primal forces. Central to his study is the concept of muisek: the vibrant spiritual essence that remains within a creature. To harness it, Uzer'i crafts specialized vessels capable of rapidly shrinking fallen beings before their escaping spirit disperses, allowing the essence to be stored and studied. Extracting muisek was merely the first phase of Uzer'i's broader ambition. Gathering resilient sinew, enchanted minerals, and petrified splintered logs from the very creatures whose spirits he trapped, the witch doctor fused physical materials with bound muisek. Through these rites, he learned to permanently bind ancient forest spirits into arms and armaments, providing the Horde with magically charged weapons. Beyond his ritual craftsmanship, Uzer'i maintains a deep curiosity regarding hidden places of power throughout Azeroth, actively tracking rumors of the ancient, submerged Sunken Temple.

npc:wizlo-bearingshiner.text: Wizlo Bearingshiner. Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin tinkerer stranded at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. The sole survivor of a centaur attack on his caravan, he recruits travelers to recover a valuable Hypercapacitor Gizmo from the wreckage. Staying alongside the tauren at Whitereach Post along the canyon road, Wizlo Bearingshiner faces an unwelcome delay. Centaur attacked his caravan, leaving him as its only survivor. His clients are waiting for their wares, and he worries that he will not deliver them in time. Wizlo's best gizmo hangs around the neck of a fierce panther caged beside his ruined caravan north of Whitereach Post. Even the centaur avoid the beast. Wizlo offers travelers the cage key and a reward for recovering the hypercapacitor, though he admits he has yet to work out what the device actually does.

npc:wizzle-brassbolts.text: Wizzle Brassbolts. Wizzle Brassbolts is a gnome engineer stationed alongside his fellow tinkerers out on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Working with the gnomish racing team at the Mirage Raceway, he seeks durable local materials to reinforce their experimental rocket cars. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnomish and goblin engineering takes the form of high-speed rocket car races. Wizzle Brassbolts works as part of the gnomish raceway crew, striving to keep their vehicles intact against blistering speeds and abrasive salt. To bolster their machines, he recruits adventurers to hunt the local wildlife—such as the sturdy turtles wandering the basin—harvesting their hard shells to build new fuel tanks strong enough to hold his brother's corrosive new rocket fuel. Wizzle maintains close ties with friends across the continents, including Pilot Longbeard, who sends couriers out with racing helmets for the brothers. With help like that, Wizzle keeps the gnomish team supplied despite their remote, inhospitable testing ground on the Shimmering Flats.

npc:wizzlecrank-s-shredder.text: Wizzlecrank's Shredder. In Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank's Shredder sits trapped among Venture Company operators. Pilot Wizzlecrank climbed inside the machine to steal it, but it will not move without a key. Its engine must be started before the goblin can try to escape. Deep in Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank waits inside a motionless shredder. The Venture Company machine is surrounded by hostile mercenaries in the polluted basin. Wizzlecrank climbed aboard to steal it, then learned he needed a key to unlock its movement column. When another shredder operator asked if all was well, he panicked and blamed a mechanical problem. Now he remains sealed inside, with guards and overseers nearby, hoping someone will fetch the key before the Venture Company grows suspicious.

npc:wrenix-the-wretched.text: Wrenix the Wretched. Beside his strange apparatus in Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched helps crack tough locks. The goblin tinker offers tools to open secure caches. Wrenix the Wretched works beside his machinery in Ratchet, the goblin port on the Barrens coast. As a tinker of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he knows mechanisms and contraptions, and how to bypass locks and salvage what lies beyond them. Rogues and scouts working the coast can turn to him for help. Wrenix keeps his gizmotronic apparatus close at hand. He uses it and his mechanical skill to supply thieves' tools and lock-picking instruments. Those seeking to recover stolen Southsea pirate contraband along the Merchant Coast can put them to use.

npc:wynne-larson.text: Wynne Larson. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson supplies mages across the kingdom with robes. Human clothier Wynne relies on local craftsmen since Dalaran and Quel'Thalas fell in the Third War, and points spellcasters toward rare materials for enchanted garments. Before the Third War, Dalaran and Quel'Thalas supplied the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments. Their destruction crippled the old trade routes and arcane textile production. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson now works with local tailors and enchanters such as Lucan Cordell. Together, they meet the city's growing demand for robes and spellwoven gear. Novice and journeyman mages seeking arcane garments come to Wynne's shop. She knows what materials are needed for vestments such as Manaweave Robes and Astral Knot Garments. To find those materials, she sends arcane practitioners into dangerous places to recover rare reagents like pristine spider silk. Her work helps keep Stormwind's mages outfitted despite shortages from the north.

npc:xavathras.text: Xavathras. Xavathras is a vicious satyr commander residing among the tents at the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood. Leading a band of Jadefire satyrs, he oversees the corruption of an ancient moonwell in service to his master, Xavaric. Within the tainted glades of Felwood, the Ruins of Constellas have fallen into the clutches of the Jadefire satyrs. Stationed in an encampment pitched amidst the elven stonework, Xavathras directs the defilement of a nearby moonwell on behalf of another cruel satyr, Xavaric. By poisoning the pure waters with demonic energy, Xavathras deepens the corruption that grips the forest. His presence poses a direct threat to any attempts to restore the woodland, earning the ire of night elves like Eridan Bluewind who mark him for death.

npc:yeh-kinya.text: Yeh'kinya. Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics. Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

npc:yvette-farthing.text: Yvette Farthing. Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken resident of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, dwelling in the Gallows' End Tavern alongside her father, Coleman. Though she appears as hardened and detached as any of Sylvanas's people, she carries the lingering ghost of a mortal romance cut short by the Scourge. Before the Third War swept Lordaeron into ruin, Yvette was in love with Thurman Agamand, one of the heirs of the prosperous Agamand Mills. When the Scourge plague approached, Yvette and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to abandon the estate and flee with them. Thurman refused out of devotion to his family's legacy. Both would eventually perish and rise into undeath, but while Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, Thurman's tragic final fate remained unknown to her.

npc:zaldimar-wefhellt.text: Zaldimar Wefhellt. On Goldshire's upper floor, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches young mages their first spells. When they outgrow his lessons, he sends them to Stormwind City for further training. Upstairs at the Lion's Pride Inn, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches novice mages the first arts of arcane, fire, and frost. When an apprentice outgrows those lessons, he sends them north to the Mage Quarter in Stormwind, where Jennea Cannon can teach them more.

npc:zamja.text: Zamja. In Orgrimmar’s Drag, Zamja teaches Horde travelers to cook. The Darkspear troll trains cooks to make meals from beasts of Kalimdor. Zamja works in the Drag, where she cuts meat and teaches Horde travelers to cook. Cooking helps travelers in the rugged lands of Durotar and the Barrens turn raw game into rations. Cooks who have mastered basic recipes can seek further training in Gadgetzan, to the south.

npc:zangen-stonehoof.text: Zangen Stonehoof. Zangen Stonehoof is a tauren keeper situated at the High Rise bonfire in the heart of Thunder Bluff. Dutiful and revered among his peers, he faithfully tends to the central flames each evening while coordinating efforts to aid his distant kin across Kalimdor. Perched on the High Rise of Thunder Bluff, Zangen Stonehoof maintains the central communal bonfire that overlooks the city's highest bluffs. As twilight falls over Mulgore, Zangen kindles the fire, providing warmth and an enduring beacon for the tribes assembled beneath High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Beyond keeping the flames alight, he maintains ties with allies beyond Mulgore's mesa, acting as a liaison for spiritual and ritual endeavors taking place across the continent. Zangen acts as an intermediary for Rau Cliffrunner, an associate stationed south in Thousand Needles. When Rau required the mystical waters of a night elf moonwell for sacred rituals, Zangen enlisted dependable Horde adventurers to brave the contested forests of Ashenvale. By securing the filled phial from the ancient groves and dispatching it south to Freewind Post, Zangen plays a quiet but pivotal part in preserving ancient rites and assisting scattered tauren posts.

npc:zankaja.text: Zankaja. In Orgrimmar, young orc woman Zankaja waits anxiously for word of her mate, Dogran. He was assigned to duty at the Crossroads, along the dangerous frontier of the Barrens. Zankaja waits for news of Dogran, her mate, in Orgrimmar. Dogran earned a promotion and went south to bolster the outpost at the Crossroads in the Barrens. The assignment honors a warrior, but the frontier is harsh, with quilboar, centaur, and aggressive beasts. When Dogran failed to send word or return as expected, Zankaja began asking travelers to seek news of him.

npc:zardeth-of-the-black-claw.text: Zardeth of the Black Claw. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Zardeth of the Black Claw protects a hidden warlock cabal from scrutiny. He dwells in the chambers beneath the Slaughtered Lamb and poses as an ordinary patron. When curious nobles look too closely, he makes sure their inquiries end for good. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, tunnels shelter those who practice darker arts while the Mage Quarter's spires study arcane discipline in the open. Zardeth of the Black Claw works from these crypts, guarding warlocks who hide right beneath the city guard's nose. The Alliance condemns fel magic, so the cabal survives by keeping its presence secret and removing threats before royal investigators arrive.

npc:zargh.text: Zargh. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Zargh sells meat and sends choice cuts to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sells cured meat, shank, and game from the surrounding plains. Travelers heading into the wilderness can find provisions at his shop. He also sends choice cuts across Durotar to Innkeeper Gryshka in the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar.

npc:zarlman-two-moons.text: Zarlman Two-Moons. Zarlman Two-Moons is a revered tauren mystic residing in Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. While Baine Bloodhoof oversees the village's daily earthly affairs, Zarlman guides its spiritual life and communions with the spirits. He plays a vital role in initiating young tauren into adulthood through the sacred Rite of Vision. Within Bloodhoof Village, leadership is divided between the physical and the mystical. Baine Bloodhoof commands the settlement's defense and temporal needs, but it is Zarlman Two-Moons who maintains the harmony of the spirit world. In a culture deeply rooted in reverence for the Earth Mother and ancestral wisdom, Zarlman serves as a conduit between the everyday struggles of the plains and the timeless voices of the past. Zarlman's most crucial duty to his people is administering the Rite of Vision, a traditional trial every maturing tauren must undertake. By guiding initiates to prepare sacred draughts and listen closely to ancestral portents, he helps young hunters, shamans, and warriors discover their destined path and spirit guides. Under his instruction, initiates learn that physical strength on the plains means little without spiritual clarity.

npc:zarrin.text: Zarrin. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin teaches the ways of Kaldorei cooking. He tends an open hearth on Teldrassil, where young night elves and visitors learn to prepare meals from the tree's native flora and fauna. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin tends an open cooking fire and teaches Kaldorei culinary arts. Teldrassil's native plants and animals provide food for those who live here. Zarrin shows visitors how to forage and prepare meals at home.

npc:zenn-foulhoof.text: Zenn Foulhoof. East of Dolanaar, Zenn Foulhoof asks travelers for forest reagents. The night elves watch him closely.

npc:zevrost.text: Zevrost. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Zevrost trains warlocks in fel magic. He guides Horde initiates through summoning rites and the handling of dark artifacts. In the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar, Zevrost is one of the chief mentors for Horde warlocks in Thrall’s capital. Orcs remain wary of fel magic after their past demonic corruption, so practitioners work under strict watch. Zevrost teaches the discipline needed to command demons without yielding to their corruption. He says fel ruins only those who lack inner strength. Zevrost guides warlocks beyond spells and curses, opening the way to greater dark undertakings. Initiates seeking advanced implements such as the Orb of Orahil, or the means to summon a fiery Felsteed, often come through his hands. He sends ambitious practitioners to other masters, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens, so they can push their command of shadow magic to its limits.

npc:zjolnir.text: Zjolnir. In Sen'jin Village, Zjolnir raises raptors for Darkspear riders and trusted Horde champions. His trained mounts carry deep cultural pride for troll riders. Near Sen'jin Village's pens, Zjolnir raises the fierce raptors the Darkspear favor as mounts. Predatory and temperamental, they need an expert hand before they can be raised and saddled for war. Zjolnir freely gives these prized mounts to fellow trolls who have learned the riding arts. Other Horde members must first earn the Darkspear tribe's exalted trust before he will entrust them with one of his raptors.

npc:zor-lonetree.text: Zor Lonetree. At Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree studies the Horde’s concerns beyond Durotar. His knowledge of Alliance politics helps the court judge foreign affairs across Kalimdor. Zor Lonetree watches beyond Durotar from Grommash Hold. A shrewd advisor to the Horde’s high leadership, he has an unusually keen understanding of human and Alliance politics. When foreign curiosities reach Orgrimmar, he studies them; when trouble stirs among the land’s spirits, he directs travelers toward it. He has examined noble jewelry recovered from human settlements and followed disturbances among the spirits of the Stonetalon Mountains, keeping the warchief’s court informed on both political and spiritual matters.

npc:zureetha-fargaze.text: Zureetha Fargaze. In the Valley of Trials, Zureetha Fargaze watches for threats to young Horde recruits. Alongside Foreman Thazz'ril in Durotar, she sends them to uncover and root out the Burning Blade cult hidden in the valley. Zureetha Fargaze watches for dangers beyond the work and discipline Foreman Thazz'ril oversees. The Burning Blade cult has secretly entered the Valley of Trials, corrupted lesser demons, and gathered strength in the nearby Burning Blade Coven. She sends untested adventurers to recover medallions from the cultists, confirm their presence, and disrupt their early efforts. Then she directs seasoned recruits farther into Durotar.

topic:agamaggan.text: Agamaggan. Agamaggan the Great Boar was one of the colossal Ancient Guardians who walked Azeroth in its earliest days. He fell ten thousand years ago fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients, and his sacrifice helped save Azeroth from ruin. Where his blood and body crashed into the earth, vast networks of thorny vines arose, creating the Razorfen and granting life and purpose to his descendants, the quilboar. Ten thousand years ago, during the War of the Ancients, the mighty demigod Agamaggan came forth to battle the Burning Legion. The colossal boar fought with terrifying ferocity, and though he ultimately fell in combat, his actions helped save Azeroth from ruin. Where Agamaggan collapsed in the southern Barrens, his colossal corpse reshaped the land. His spilled blood soaked into the soil, causing enormous, impenetrable brambles and thorny vines to burst upward from the dry earth. These tangled thickets became known as the Razorfen. The quilboar revere the site as their holiest ground, viewing the labyrinth of Razorfen Kraul as his resting body and Razorfen Downs as his gaping skull. Scattered throughout the Barrens are crystallized Blood Shards, believed to be the physical remnants of the demigod's spilled blood, pulsing with lingering primal energy that quilboar geomancers and shamans harness for power. Agamaggan is revered as the divine progenitor of all quilboar. They view the surrounding brambles not merely as homes, but as the living armor left behind by their creator to shelter them from hostile neighbors. Quilboar tribes believe their god's spirit watches over them, granting martial vigor to their warriors and earth magic to their geomancers. In turn, they aggressively defend the thorns against encroaching tauren, orcs, and centaur, convinced that their sacred duty is to guard the fallen body of the boar god who birthed them.

topic:alliance.text: Alliance. The Alliance is a grand coalition of mortal races bound by shared ideals of honor, duty, and the defense of order across Azeroth. Born out of the ashes of the northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its current heart beats in Stormwind City, united alongside the dwarves of Ironforge, the exiled gnomes, and the night elves of Kalimdor. The modern Alliance descends from the original Alliance of Lordaeron, founded when Sir Anduin Lothar led Stormwind refugees north during the Second War to unite the Seven Kingdoms, dwarves, and high elves against the Old Horde. While the Scourge and the Third War decimated the north—leaving Lordaeron in ruins and driving the survivors into scattered resistance—the restored Kingdom of Stormwind rose to fill the void. Today, Stormwind stands as the preeminent seat of human leadership, carrying the banners of honor and faith into a fractured world. The faction's backbone in the Eastern Kingdoms relies on the steadfast bond between humans and the dwarves of Ironforge under King Magni Bronzebeard. Alongside the dwarves reside the gnomes, driven from Gnomeregan by a devastating trogg uprising. Guided by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, the exiled gnomes lend their brilliant engineering to the Alliance war effort, believing the coalition's survival is paramount to ever reclaiming their irradiated home. Across the Great Sea, the reclusive night elves abandoned millennia of isolation after the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Reeling from the loss of their immortality and engaged in bitter territorial clashes against the Horde over logging in Ashenvale, the kaldorei allied with their newfound mortal companions. Though cultural friction remains—and some traditionalists decry the presence of humans and dwarves in ancient forests—the Alliance provides vital military and diplomatic cooperation to safeguard Kalimdor against demonic remnants and Horde expansion. Despite its outward strength, the Alliance is beset by internal strain. King Varian Wrynn vanished under mysterious circumstances en route to a diplomatic summit, leaving his young son Anduin on the throne under Highlord Bolvar Fordragon's regency. Relations with former human allies are fractured: the maritime kingdom of Kul Tiras keeps its distance, while Sylvanas Windrunner's undead Forsaken now hold the ruins of Lordaeron.

topic:brotherhood-of-northshire.text: Brotherhood of Northshire. The Brotherhood of Northshire is a holy human clerical order dedicated to the Church of the Holy Light, based out of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Originally known as the Clerics of Northshire, the order suffered catastrophic losses during the First War before being reformed under Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Today, the Brotherhood serves as both a spiritual sanctuary and the primary training ground for fledgling Alliance defenders. Centuries ago, pious missionaries traveled south from Lordaeron into the kingdom of Stormwind, establishing Northshire Abbey to minister to the people and soothe the realm through the Holy Light. Originally known as the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, their compassion was legendary—they even tended to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars. When the Orcish Horde crossed through the Dark Portal, the clerics marched bravely to the front lines without armor or weapons to heal fallen soldiers.
